insights.title: 18. Essential Global Attributes (id, class, lang, dir, hidden)
insights.content: Global attributes apply to any HTML element to control identity, styling, language, text direction, and visibility.

blocks.text: id must be unique across the page, whereas class can be shared by many elements. Use lang and dir="rtl" or dir="ltr" for multilingual content, title for advisory tooltips, and hidden to hide irrelevant elements.

insights.title: 19. Custom Data Attributes (data-*)
insights.content: Embed custom metadata directly on HTML elements using data-* attributes accessible via element.dataset in JS.

blocks.text: Any attribute starting with data- is valid HTML and lets you pass configuration or state cleanly without polluting classes or IDs. Hyphenated names like data-user-id convert to camelCase (dataset.userId) in JavaScript and work in CSS attr() or selectors.

blocks.code:
<button
  type="button"
  data-project-id="42"
  data-category="fullstack"
>
  Preview Project
</button>

insights.title: 20. Form Element Basics (action, method, autocomplete)
insights.content: The <form> element collects user input and submits it via GET or POST to an action endpoint.

blocks.text: Use method="get" for idempotent searches (data goes into the URL query string) and method="post" for mutations or sensitive payloads. Setting autocomplete="on" helps browsers and password managers autofill fields accurately.

blocks.code:
<form action="/api/contact" method="post" autocomplete="on">
  <label for="sender">Name</label>
  <input id="sender" name="sender" type="text" required />
  <button type="submit">Send</button>
</form>

insights.title: 21. Accessible Labels & Text Inputs
insights.content: Always pair every input with a <label> using matching for and id attributes, never relying on placeholder alone.

blocks.text: Clicking a properly linked <label> focuses its input, expanding the touch target and announcing the field name to screen readers. Each submitted field must also have a name attribute so the server receives its key-value pair.

insights.title: 22. Email, Password, URL & Search Inputs
insights.content: Specialized input types trigger optimized virtual keyboards and built-in format checks.

blocks.text: type="email" validates email syntax and shows the @ key on mobile, type="password" masks characters, type="url" expects a scheme like https://, and type="search" adds a quick clear button in many browsers.

blocks.code:
<input type="email" name="email" placeholder="you@domain.com" autocomplete="email" />
<input type="password" name="pass" minlength="8" autocomplete="current-password" />
<input type="url" name="website" placeholder="https://example.com" />
<input type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search articles..." />

insights.title: 23. Number, Range Slider & Tel Inputs
insights.content: Use type="number", type="range", and type="tel" with min, max, and step constraints.

blocks.text: type="number" provides numeric validation and spinner controls, whereas type="range" renders an interactive slider for approximate numeric selection. type="tel" opens the numeric dialpad on phones without enforcing strict country formatting.

blocks.code:
<label for="qty">Quantity</label>
<input id="qty" name="qty" type="number" min="1" max="20" step="1" value="1" />

<label for="vol">Volume</label>
<input id="vol" name="vol" type="range" min="0" max="100" step="5" value="60" />

<label for="phone">Phone</label>
<input id="phone" name="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel" />

insights.title: 24. Date & Time Picker Inputs
insights.content: Native date, time, datetime-local, month, and week inputs render built-in calendar and clock pickers.

blocks.text: Values always submit in standardized ISO formats (such as YYYY-MM-DD for date and HH:MM for time) regardless of the user's locale display format. You can restrict selectable ranges using min and max.

blocks.code:
<label for="start">Start Date</label>
<input id="start" name="start" type="date" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" />

<label for="meeting">Meeting Time</label>
<input id="meeting" name="meeting" type="time" value="09:30" />

<label for="launch">Launch Slot</label>
<input id="launch" name="launch" type="datetime-local" />

insights.title: 25. Checkboxes & Radio Buttons
insights.content: Use checkboxes for independent multi-select toggles and radio buttons with a shared name for mutually exclusive choices.

blocks.text: Radio buttons belong to a single group only when they share the exact same name attribute, allowing one selection at a time. Always assign distinct value attributes so form submissions identify which option was picked.

blocks.code:
<label><input type="checkbox" name="topics" value="html" checked /> HTML</label>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="topics" value="css" /> CSS</label>

<label><input type="radio" name="plan" value="free" checked /> Free</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="plan" value="pro" /> Pro</label>

insights.title: 26. Select Dropdowns & Option Groups
insights.content: Create dropdown menus with <select>, <option>, and <optgroup> to organize long option lists.

blocks.text: Add selected to pre-choose an option, disabled on a placeholder option, or multiple on <select> to allow multi-item selection. <optgroup label="..."> visually groups related options without making the group header selectable.

blocks.code:
<label for="stack">Primary Stack</label>
<select id="stack" name="stack">
  <option value="" disabled selected>Choose a framework...</option>
  <optgroup label="Frontend">
    <option value="nextjs">Next.js</option>
    <option value="react">React</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="Backend">
    <option value="bun">Bun</option>
    <option value="node">Node.js</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

insights.title: 27. Multi-line Input with <textarea>
insights.content: Use <textarea> instead of <input> when users need to enter multi-line prose, comments, or code.

blocks.text: Unlike <input>, <textarea> has an opening and closing tag and holds its default text between them. Control initial size with rows and cols, limit character count with maxlength, and control soft/hard line wrapping with wrap.

blocks.code:
<label for="bio">Short Bio</label>
<textarea
  id="bio"
  name="bio"
  rows="4"
  cols="40"
  maxlength="300"
  placeholder="Tell us about your engineering background..."
></textarea>

insights.title: 28. Button Element & Button Types
insights.content: Always specify type="submit", type="reset", or type="button" on <button> inside forms.

blocks.text: Inside a <form>, a <button> without a type defaults to type="submit", which can cause accidental form submissions on interactive UI controls. Unlike <input type="button">, <button> can contain rich HTML such as SVG icons alongside text.

blocks.code:
<form>
  <button type="submit">Save Changes</button>
  <button type="reset">Clear Form</button>
  <button type="button" onclick="alert('Preview')">Preview</button>
</form>

insights.title: 29. Grouping Controls with <fieldset> & <legend>
insights.content: Wrap related form controls such as radio groups or shipping addresses in <fieldset> with a <legend> title.

blocks.text: <legend> serves as the accessible group label announced by screen readers when entering the group. Adding disabled to a <fieldset> disables every descendant control inside it (except inputs inside its <legend>).

blocks.code:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Notification Preferences</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="freq" value="daily" /> Daily</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="freq" value="weekly" /> Weekly</label>
</fieldset>

insights.title: 30. Native Autocomplete Suggestions with <datalist>
insights.content: Link an <input> to a <datalist> via list="id" to offer searchable autocomplete suggestions without JavaScript.

blocks.text: Unlike <select>, <datalist> lets users pick a suggested value or type any custom text freely. It works seamlessly with text, search, url, color, and range inputs.

blocks.code:
<label for="browser">Preferred Browser</label>
<input id="browser" name="browser" list="browsers" />
<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Firefox"></option>
  <option value="Chrome"></option>
  <option value="Safari"></option>
  <option value="Edge"></option>
</datalist>

insights.title: 31. File Upload Inputs (type="file", accept, multiple)
insights.content: Allow file uploads using <input type="file"> with accept filters and optional multiple selection.

blocks.text: Always set enctype="multipart/form-data" and method="post" on the parent <form> when uploading files. The accept attribute guides the OS file picker using MIME types or extensions, though servers must still validate uploaded files.

blocks.code:
<form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <label for="photos">Upload Images</label>
  <input id="photos" name="photos" type="file" accept="image/png, image/webp" multiple />
  <button type="submit">Upload</button>
</form>

insights.title: 32. Color Picker & Hidden Inputs
insights.content: Use type="color" for native hex color pickers and type="hidden" to submit non-editable metadata.

blocks.text: type="color" expects and returns 7-character lowercase hex strings (#rrggbb). type="hidden" passes tokens or record IDs without rendering UI, though users can still inspect or alter them in DevTools.

blocks.code:
<label for="accent">Brand Accent</label>
<input id="accent" name="accent" type="color" value="#2563eb" />
<input type="hidden" name="form_version" value="v2" />

insights.title: 33. Progress Bars vs Gauges (<progress> vs <meter>)
insights.content: Use <progress> for ongoing task completion and <meter> for static scalar measurements within a known range.

blocks.text: Omitting value on <progress> renders an indeterminate loading state. <meter> supports low, high, and optimum thresholds so browsers automatically color-code healthy versus warning levels.

blocks.code:
<label for="upload-prog">Upload progress:</label>
<progress id="upload-prog" value="70" max="100">70%</progress>

<label for="disk">Disk usage:</label>
<meter id="disk" min="0" max="100" low="30" high="80" optimum="20" value="85">85%</meter>

insights.title: 34. Machine-Readable Dates & Contact Info (<time>, <address>)
insights.content: Annotate human-friendly dates with <time datetime="..."> and author contact blocks with <address>.

blocks.text: The datetime attribute gives search engines and scripts an exact ISO timestamp while keeping readable text inside the tag. <address> specifically represents contact details for the nearest <article> or <body> author, not arbitrary street addresses.

insights.title: 35. Native Disclosure Widget (<details> & <summary>)
insights.content: Create expandable/collapsible FAQ or accordion widgets natively without JavaScript using <details> and <summary>.

blocks.text: The <summary> element acts as the clickable toggle heading, while everything else inside <details> is revealed when expanded. Add the open boolean attribute to make it expanded on initial render.

insights.title: 36. Semantic Page Landmarks (header, nav, main, footer)
insights.content: Replace generic <div> wrappers with <header>, <nav>, <main>, and <footer> so assistive tools can jump between regions.

blocks.text: A document should have only one visible <main> landmark containing its primary unique content. <header> and <footer> represent introductory and closing content for the page or their nearest sectioning root.

insights.title: 37. Article vs Section vs Aside
insights.content: Use <article> for self-contained syndicatable items, <section> for thematic groupings, and <aside> for tangentially related content.

blocks.text: Think of an <article> as content that still makes sense in an RSS feed or standalone card (blog post, product card, comment). Each <section> should normally begin with a heading (<h2>–<h6>), while <aside> holds sidebars, callouts, or related links.

insights.title: 38. Native Audio Playback (<audio> & <source>)
insights.content: Embed sound with <audio controls> and provide multiple <source> formats for broad codec compatibility.

blocks.text: The browser picks the first <source> format it supports (such as Opus/WebM or MP3). Use preload="metadata" to fetch duration without downloading the entire audio file upfront.

blocks.code:
<audio controls preload="metadata">
  <source src="/audio/podcast-ep1.ogg" type="audio/ogg" />
  <source src="/audio/podcast-ep1.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" />
  Your browser does not support the audio element.
</audio>

insights.title: 39. Native Video Playback (<video>, poster, muted, playsinline)
insights.content: Configure <video> with poster thumbnails, explicit dimensions, and playsinline for reliable mobile playback.

blocks.text: Browsers block unmuted autoplay, so background or hero preview videos require muted alongside autoplay and loop. Include playsinline so iOS Safari plays video inline instead of forcing fullscreen.

blocks.code:
<video
  controls
  width="720"
  height="405"
  poster="/images/demo-poster.jpg"
  preload="metadata"
  playsinline
>
  <source src="/videos/demo.webm" type="video/webm" />
  <source src="/videos/demo.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
</video>

insights.title: 40. Video Subtitles & Captions (<track>)
insights.content: Add accessible WebVTT subtitles and closed captions to audio/video using the <track> element.

blocks.text: Use kind="captions" for deaf/hard-of-hearing audiences (including sound effects) and kind="subtitles" for translations. Specify srclang, label, and default on the primary track.

blocks.code:
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="/videos/talk.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  <track kind="captions" src="/captions/talk-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default />
  <track kind="subtitles" src="/captions/talk-ar.vtt" srclang="ar" label="العربية" />
</video>

insights.title: 41. Responsive Images with srcset & sizes
insights.content: Serve resolution-appropriate image files using srcset width descriptors (w) and sizes hints.

blocks.text: srcset lists available image widths (e.g., 400w, 800w, 1200w) while sizes tells the browser how wide the image will render at different viewport widths before CSS loads, saving mobile bandwidth.

insights.title: 42. Art Direction & Format Fallbacks with <picture>
insights.content: Use <picture> with <source> elements to swap image crops by viewport or serve next-gen AVIF/WebP formats.

blocks.text: The browser evaluates elements top-to-bottom based on media and type attributes, falling back to the required inner if none match. All styling, alt text, and dimensions still live on the inner .

insights.title: 43. Clickable Image Maps (<map> & <area>)
insights.content: Define clickable geometric regions inside an image using <map> and <area> linked via usemap.

blocks.text: Each <area> accepts shape="rect|circle|poly", pixel coords, an href, and an accessible alt attribute. For modern responsive graphics, inline SVG links often scale more reliably than fixed pixel coordinates.

insights.title: 44. Inline SVG Vector Graphics
insights.content: Embed crisp, scalable vector shapes and icons directly in HTML using <svg> and viewBox.

blocks.text: Inline <svg> elements live in the DOM, meaning you can style stroke and fill with CSS (like currentColor) and animate paths. Always set viewBox so the graphic scales cleanly, and add aria-hidden="true" for decorative icons.

blocks.code:
<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true">
  <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" />
  <path d="M9 12l2 2 4-4" />
</svg>

insights.title: 45. The <canvas> Drawing Surface
insights.content: Provide a bitmap drawing surface for 2D charts, games, or WebGL graphics with <canvas> and fallback content.

blocks.text: Set drawing resolution using the HTML width and height attributes (not just CSS) to prevent blurry scaling. Include descriptive fallback text or an accessible table inside <canvas> for assistive technologies.

blocks.code:
<canvas id="sparkline" width="320" height="120">
  Monthly visitors trend chart: steady 25% growth.
</canvas>
<script>
  const ctx = document.getElementById("sparkline").getContext("2d");
  ctx.fillStyle = "#3b82f6";
  ctx.fillRect(10, 40, 60, 70);
</script>

insights.title: 46. Embedding External Pages Safely with <iframe>
insights.content: Embed external media or sandboxes using <iframe> with a descriptive title, loading="lazy", and sandbox restrictions.

blocks.text: Screen readers require a title attribute on every <iframe>. The sandbox attribute locks down scripts, forms, and top-level navigation unless explicitly re-enabled (such as allow-scripts).

blocks.code:
<iframe
  src="https://example.com/embed/widget"
  title="Interactive code sandbox demo"
  width="600"
  height="360"
  loading="lazy"
  sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"
></iframe>

insights.title: 47. Essential SEO, Viewport & Charset Meta Tags
insights.content: Configure UTF-8 encoding, mobile viewport scaling, meta descriptions, and crawler directives inside <head>.

blocks.text: Place <meta charset="UTF-8"> within the first 1024 bytes of the document so parsers decode characters immediately. Avoid user-scalable=no in the viewport tag because disabling zoom hurts accessibility.

blocks.code:
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
  <meta name="description" content="Full-stack web developer portfolio and technical articles." />
  <meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />
</head>

insights.title: 48. Open Graph & Social Sharing Meta Tags
insights.content: Control how links preview on LinkedIn, X, WhatsApp, and Discord using Open Graph (og:*) and Twitter Card tags.

blocks.text: Platforms read og:title, og:description, og:image, and og:url when generating link cards. Always provide absolute HTTPS URLs for og:image so scrapers can fetch the preview thumbnail reliably.

blocks.code:
<meta property="og:type" content="website" />
<meta property="og:title" content="Ahmed Magdy — Software Engineer" />
<meta property="og:description" content="Explore production Next.js, TypeScript, and UI systems." />
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og-cover.png" />
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />

insights.title: 49. Canonical URLs & Modern Favicons
insights.content: Prevent duplicate-content SEO penalties with rel="canonical" and declare SVG/PNG favicons cleanly.

blocks.text: A canonical link tells search engines which URL is the authoritative version when query parameters or trailing slashes create duplicates. An SVG favicon scales crisply and can even adapt to dark mode internally.

blocks.code:
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/projects/portfolio" />
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml" />
<link rel="icon" href="/favicon-32.png" sizes="32x32" type="image/png" />
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/apple-touch-icon.png" />

insights.title: 50. Built-in Constraint Validation Attributes
insights.content: Validate required fields, text lengths, numeric ranges, and regex patterns natively in HTML before JavaScript runs.

blocks.text: Attributes like required, minlength, maxlength, min, max, and pattern integrate with the browser's Constraint Validation API and CSS pseudo-classes like :valid and :invalid. Add a descriptive title when using pattern to guide users.

blocks.code:
<form>
  <label for="slug">Project Slug</label>
  <input
    id="slug"
    name="slug"
    type="text"
    required
    minlength="3"
    maxlength="30"
    pattern="[a-z0-9-]+"
    title="Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only"
  />
  <button type="submit">Create</button>
</form>

insights.title: 51. Mobile Keyboards with inputmode & autocomplete Tokens
insights.content: Combine inputmode and semantic autocomplete tokens like one-time-code to optimize mobile input ergonomics.

blocks.text: Using type="text" with inputmode="numeric" avoids unwanted number spinners while displaying a numeric keypad on phones—ideal for OTP codes and postal codes. Specific autocomplete values like one-time-code enable automatic SMS code autofill.

<input
  id="otp"
  name="otp"
  type="text"
  inputmode="numeric"
  pattern="[0-9]{6}"
  autocomplete="one-time-code"
  required
/>

insights.title: 52. Button Form Overrides (formaction, formnovalidate)
insights.content: Override a form's action, method, or validation behavior per submit button using form* attributes.

blocks.text: A single form can have both a Publish button (full validation) and a Save Draft button using formnovalidate and a different formaction endpoint without needing separate <form> tags.

  <input type="text" name="title" required />
  <button type="submit">Publish</button>
  <button type="submit" formaction="/posts/draft" formnovalidate>
    Save Draft
  </button>
</form>

insights.title: 53. Linking External Controls with the form Attribute
insights.content: Associate an <input>, <select>, or <button> located outside a <form> using form="form-id".

blocks.text: HTML forbids nesting <form> inside another <form>, and complex table or modal layouts often place submit buttons elsewhere in the DOM. Pointing the form attribute to the <form>'s id connects them cleanly.

insights.content: Display calculated totals or interactive slider values semantically with <output> and its for attribute.

insights.title: 63. Non-Blocking Script Loading (defer, async, type="module")
insights.content: Avoid render-blocking JavaScript by using defer, async, or ES modules (type="module").

blocks.text: defer downloads scripts in parallel and executes them in document order right before DOMContentLoaded. async executes immediately upon download in unpredictable order (great for isolated analytics). ES modules defer automatically and run in strict mode.

blocks.code:
<script src="/js/analytics.js" async></script>
<script src="/js/app.js" defer></script>
<script type="module" src="/js/main.mjs"></script>

insights.title: 64. Resource Hints: preconnect, preload & prefetch
insights.content: Speed up critical rendering with <link rel="preconnect">, <link rel="preload">, and <link rel="prefetch">.

blocks.text: preconnect warms up DNS/TLS handshakes to third-party origins early. preload fetches critical current-page assets (like hero fonts or LCP images) at high priority, whereas prefetch opportunistically caches likely next-navigation assets at low priority.

blocks.code:

<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter-var.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin />
<link rel="prefetch" href="/projects/next-case-study.json" as="fetch" />

insights.title: 65. Image Priority & Decoding (fetchpriority, loading, decoding)
insights.content: Boost Core Web Vitals (LCP) by prioritizing above-the-fold hero images and lazy-loading offscreen media.

blocks.text: Set fetchpriority="high" on your Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) hero image—and never put loading="lazy" on it. Reserve loading="lazy" and decoding="async" for images below the fold.

insights.title: 66. Subresource Integrity (SRI) & crossorigin
insights.content: Verify third-party CDN scripts and stylesheets haven't been tampered with using integrity hashes.

blocks.text: The integrity attribute provides a cryptographic SHA-256/384/512 hash; if the fetched file differs by even one byte, the browser refuses to execute it. CDN assets also require crossorigin="anonymous" for SRI validation.

<script
  src="https://cdn.example.com/lib/v1.4.0/sdk.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC"
  crossorigin="anonymous"
></script>

insights.content: Set a single base URL (and optional default target) for all relative URLs on the page using <base>.

blocks.text: At most one <base> element may appear inside <head>, before any element that uses URLs (including <link> and <script>). Be aware it also affects anchor #fragment links relative to the base URL.

insights.title: 93. Preventing FOUC with blocking="render"
insights.content: Explicitly mark critical inline/external modules or view-transition stylesheets as render-blocking until ready.

blocks.text: Because <script type="module"> and async stylesheets are non-blocking by default, adding blocking="render" ensures critical theme scripts or cross-document View Transition state settle before first paint.

insights.content: Coordinate multi-page View Transitions using stable view-transition-name attributes or render-blocking <link rel="expect">.

blocks.text: When navigating between two MPA HTML pages, <link rel="expect" href="#target" blocking="render"> instructs the browser to wait for the key target element to parse before snapshotting the new page's transition frame.

insights.content: Mitigate XSS attacks by restricting allowed script/style origins via CSP and authorizing inline scripts with cryptographic nonces.

interviewQuestions.title: Why `<!DOCTYPE html>` Matters: Standards Mode vs Quirks Mode
interviewQuestions.content: `<!DOCTYPE html>` switches browsers into Standards Mode so CSS layout, box-sizing, and DOM APIs follow modern specifications instead of legacy Quirks Mode.

blocks.text:
• Standards vs Quirks Mode: Omitting `<!DOCTYPE html>` (or placing comments/whitespace before it in older parsers) triggers Quirks Mode, emulating 1990s IE5/Netscape box-model and table layout bugs.
• `<meta charset='utf-8'>`: Must appear within the first 1024 bytes of `<head>` so the parser knows character encoding before encountering non-ASCII text.
• `lang` Attribute: Helps screen readers pick the right pronunciation engine and search engines index language variants.

blocks.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Standards Mode</title>
  </head>
</html>

interviewQuestions.content: Semantic elements (`<main>`, `<nav>`, `<header>`, `<footer>`, `<aside>`, `<article>`, `<section>`) expose structural landmarks to assistive tech and search crawlers.

• Accessibility Landmarks: Screen reader users jump directly between `<main>`, `<nav>`, `<aside>` (complementary), and `<header>`/`<footer>` (banner/contentinfo when top-level).
• Single `<main>`: A document should have only one visible `<main>` containing the primary page content (excluding repeated nav/footer).
• SEO & Maintainability: Crawlers prioritize content inside `<main>`/`<article>`, and developers get cleaner, self-documenting markup.

interviewQuestions.title: `<dialog>` Element vs the Popover API (`popover` Attribute)
interviewQuestions.content: Both render in the browser's Top Layer without `z-index` hacks; `<dialog>.showModal()` creates blocking modals that trap focus, while `popover` handles non-blocking light-dismiss menus/tooltips.

blocks.text:
• `<dialog>` (`showModal()` vs `show()`): `showModal()` makes background content `inert`, traps focus, renders `::backdrop`, and closes on `Escape`. Submitting `<form method='dialog'>` closes it automatically.
• `popover` (`auto` vs `manual`): `popover='auto'` (default) supports light-dismiss (click outside / `Escape`) and auto-closes sibling popovers; `popover='manual'` stays open until explicitly dismissed. Works declaratively via `popovertarget`.

interviewQuestions.title: The `inert` Attribute & How It Simplifies Accessibility
interviewQuestions.content: Setting `inert` on an element excludes its entire subtree from tab focus, click/pointer events, text selection, find-in-page, and the accessibility tree.

blocks.text:
• What `inert` Disables Automatically: Keyboard focus (`Tab`), mouse/touch clicks, text selection, and screen reader discovery (acts like `aria-hidden='true'` + `disabled` + `pointer-events: none` combined).
• Why It's Better Than `aria-hidden`: `aria-hidden='true'` still leaves buttons focusable via Tab, breaking WCAG; `inert` blocks both screen readers and keyboard focus.
• Use Cases: Background page content behind custom drawers/modals, off-screen carousel slides, and collapsing sections.

blocks.code:
<main id="app-content" inert>
  <!-- Links, buttons, and text here cannot be clicked, tabbed to, or read by screen readers -->
  <button>Unreachable</button>
</main>
<aside role="dialog" aria-modal="true">Active Drawer</aside>

interviewQuestions.title: Invoker Commands API (`command` and `commandfor` Attributes)
interviewQuestions.content: The Invoker Commands API lets `<button>` elements declaratively trigger built-in (`show-modal`, `close`, `toggle-popover`) or custom (`--*`) actions on target elements without JS click handlers.

blocks.text:
• Declarative Replacement for JS Glue: Replaces `onclick='dialog.showModal()'` with `commandfor='id' command='show-modal'` on `<button>`.
• Built-in Commands: `show-modal`, `close`, `toggle-popover`, `show-popover`, `hide-popover`.
• Custom Commands: Prefix with `--` (e.g., `command='--next-slide'`) to dispatch a `CommandEvent` (`event.command`) directly on the target element for Web Components.

interviewQuestions.title: The Golden Rules of ARIA & Native HTML vs Custom ARIA Widgets
interviewQuestions.content: The First Rule of ARIA is to use native HTML elements whenever available—bad ARIA breaks keyboard and screen reader behavior worse than no ARIA.

blocks.text:
• Rule 1 (Native First): Never use `<div role='button'>` when `<button>` works; native elements include focusability, keyboard activation, and semantics automatically.
• Rule 2 (Don't Change Native Semantics): Avoid `<h2 role='button'>`; nest `<button>` inside `<h2>` instead.
• Rule 3 (Interactive Roles Require Keyboard Support): Any custom ARIA widget (`tablist`, `combobox`) must implement arrow/Escape/Enter key handlers.
• Rule 4 & 5: Never hide focusable elements with `aria-hidden='true'`, and ensure every interactive control has an accessible name.

blocks.code:
<!-- Good: Native button gets keyboard Enter/Space, focus, and role free -->
<button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="faq-1">Show Answer</button>

<!-- Bad: <div onclick="..."> lacks focus, role, and keyboard Enter/Space support -->

interviewQuestions.title: ARIA Live Regions (`aria-live`, `role='status'`, `role='alert'`)
interviewQuestions.content: ARIA live regions instruct screen readers to announce dynamic DOM updates (toasts, form errors, search counts) without moving user focus.

blocks.text:
• `aria-live='polite'` (or `role='status'`): Waits until the user/screen reader pauses before speaking—use for search result counts, saved notifications, and loading states.
• `aria-live='assertive'` (or `role='alert'`): Interrupts current speech immediately—reserve strictly for urgent errors or session timeouts.
• Key Pitfall: Mount the empty live-region container on initial page load and inject text into it later; dynamically inserting both the attribute and text at once is often ignored by screen readers.

interviewQuestions.title: `aria-label` vs `aria-labelledby` vs `aria-describedby`
interviewQuestions.content: `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` define an element's primary accessible name (priority goes to `labelledby`), while `aria-describedby` supplies supplementary hint/error text.

blocks.text:
• `aria-label`: Passes an invisible string directly (great for icon-only buttons like `<button aria-label='Close'>×</button>`).
• `aria-labelledby`: References IDs of visible text elements (even multiple space-separated IDs) and overrides `aria-label` and `<label>`.
• `aria-describedby`: Reads *after* the name and role with a slight pause—ideal for input format hints or inline validation error messages.

interviewQuestions.title: Focus Management, `tabindex` Values & Roving Tabindex
interviewQuestions.content: `tabindex='0'` adds an element to natural Tab order, `tabindex='-1'` allows JS `.focus()` only, and positive `tabindex` values are an anti-pattern.

blocks.text:
• `tabindex='0'`: Makes custom elements focusable in natural DOM order.
• `tabindex='-1'`: Excluded from Tab key, but focusable programmatically via `el.focus()` (used for skip-link targets, modal containers, and error summaries).
• Positive `tabindex='1+'`: Anti-pattern—scrambles natural reading order and breaks keyboard expectations.
• Roving Tabindex: For composite widgets (toolbars, tablists), keep `tabindex='0'` on the active item and `tabindex='-1'` on siblings, moving focus with Arrow keys.

interviewQuestions.title: Skip Links, Heading Hierarchy (`<h1>`–`<h6>`) & Landmark Structure
interviewQuestions.content: Skip links let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation menus, and a logical heading outline (`h1`–`h6` without skipped levels) is the #1 navigation method for screen reader users.

blocks.text:
• Skip Links: First focusable element on the page (visually hidden until `:focus`ed), jumping directly to `#main-content`.
• Heading Hierarchy: Use one descriptive `<h1>` per page/view and descend sequentially (`h1` → `h2` → `h3`) without choosing heading tags for font size.
• Landmark Labels: When multiple `<nav>` landmarks exist (primary vs footer), distinguish them with `aria-label`.

interviewQuestions.title: HTML5 Native Form Validation & the Constraint Validation API
interviewQuestions.content: HTML5 attributes (`required`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `type`) validate inputs natively, customizable via JS `ValidityState` and CSS `:user-invalid`.

blocks.text:
• Built-in Attributes: `required`, `minlength`/`maxlength`, `min`/`max`/`step`, `pattern`, and typed inputs (`email`, `url`).
• Constraint Validation API: `input.checkValidity()`, `input.reportValidity()`, `input.validity` (`valueMissing`, `patternMismatch`, `typeMismatch`), and `setCustomValidity(msg)` (pass `''` to clear error!).
• `novalidate` on `<form>`: Disables default browser popup bubbles when rendering custom accessible inline error UI while keeping `ValidityState` usable.

blocks.code:
<form novalidate>
  <input id="code" name="code" required minlength="4" pattern="[A-Z0-9]+" />
</form>
<script>
  const input = document.getElementById("code");
  input.addEventListener("input", () => {
    input.setCustomValidity(input.validity.patternMismatch ? "Use uppercase letters and digits only." : "");
  });
</script>

interviewQuestions.title: Accessible Form Labels, `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` & `autocomplete`
interviewQuestions.content: Every input needs a `<label>` (via `for`/`id` or wrapping), related radio/checkbox groups need `<fieldset>` + `<legend>`, and `autocomplete` tokens aid autofill and accessibility.

blocks.text:
• `<label>` Association: Increases clickable hit area (crucial for checkboxes/radios) and announces the field name on focus. Never use `placeholder` as a replacement for `<label>`.
• `<fieldset>` & `<legend>`: Provide group context for radio buttons, checkboxes, or address sections.
• `autocomplete` Tokens: Values like `given-name`, `email`, `new-password`, `one-time-code` enable password managers and satisfy WCAG 2.1 Identify Input Purpose.

blocks.code:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Shipping Method</legend>
  <label for="express">Express Delivery</label>
  <input id="express" type="radio" name="shipping" value="express" />
</fieldset>
<input type="email" name="email" autocomplete="email" />

interviewQuestions.title: `type` vs `inputmode` vs `enterkeyhint` for Mobile & UX
interviewQuestions.content: `type` controls validation and value semantics, `inputmode` selects the optimal virtual keyboard (e.g., numeric keypad for OTPs) without side effects, and `enterkeyhint` labels the mobile action key.

blocks.text:
• Why Not `type='number'` for OTP/ZIP/Card: `type='number'` strips leading zeros (`01234` → `1234`), allows `e`/`+`/`-`, and increments on mouse wheel scroll.
• `inputmode` Values: `numeric`, `decimal`, `tel`, `email`, `url`, `search`—gives mobile users the right keypad while keeping `type='text'`.
• `enterkeyhint`: Customizes the virtual keyboard's Enter key label (`search`, `send`, `next`, `done`, `go`).

blocks.code:
<!-- Numeric OTP input without unwanted browser spinner arrows -->
<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]*" autocomplete="one-time-code" enterkeyhint="done" />

interviewQuestions.title: `<datalist>`, `<optgroup>`, and Modern Customizable `<select>`
interviewQuestions.content: `<datalist>` attaches autocomplete suggestions to an `<input>` without restricting free text, while modern `appearance: base-select` enables full CSS styling of native `<select>` dropdowns.

blocks.text:
• `<datalist>` vs `<select>`: `<select>` enforces picking from fixed options; `<datalist>` provides native filterable autocomplete suggestions while still allowing custom typed values.
• Customizable `<select>` (`appearance: base-select`): Unlocks rich HTML inside `<option>` (avatars, badges), styling the popup via `::picker(select)`, and custom checkmark/arrow icons while keeping native keyboard & accessibility built in.

blocks.code:
<input list="browsers" name="browser" />
<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Chrome" /><option value="Firefox" />
</datalist>

<!-- Modern CSS customizable select opt-in -->
<style>
  select, ::picker(select) { appearance: base-select; }
</style>

interviewQuestions.title: Modern Semantic Tags: `<search>`, `<hgroup>`, `<time>`, `<figure>` & `<mark>`
interviewQuestions.content: `<search>` provides a native search landmark, `<hgroup>` pairs a heading with subtitle paragraphs, and `<time>`/`<figure>`/`<mark>` add machine-readable semantics.

    <input id="q" type="search" name="q" />
  </form>

interviewQuestions.title: Native `<details>`/`<summary>`, Exclusive Accordions (`name`) & `hidden='until-found'`
interviewQuestions.content: Sharing a `name` attribute across `<details>` elements creates an exclusive zero-JS accordion, while `hidden='until-found'` reveals collapsed content during Ctrl+F searches.

blocks.text:
• Native Disclosure: `<details>` + `<summary>` handles `open` state, `toggle` events, and keyboard Enter/Space out of the box.
• Exclusive Accordions (`name='group'`): Opening one `<details>` automatically closes siblings with the same `name`.
• `hidden='until-found'`: Keeps content collapsed until browser Find-in-Page (`Ctrl+F`) or fragment navigation targets it, firing a `beforematch` event.

interviewQuestions.title: Responsive Images: `srcset` + `sizes` vs `<picture>`
interviewQuestions.content: Use `` with `srcset` + `sizes` to let the browser pick optimal resolutions; use `` for art direction (different crops) or modern format fallbacks (AVIF/WebP).

blocks.text: • Resolution Switching (`srcset` + `sizes`): Gives the browser image widths (`400w`, `800w`) and rendered layout size (`sizes`), letting it factor in DPR and network conditions. • `` + ``: Strictly chooses the first matching `` for `media` breakpoints (art direction—portrait on mobile, landscape on desktop) or MIME `type` (`image/avif`, `image/webp`). • Always include a fallback `` inside `` (that's where `alt`, `width`, `height`, and `loading` live).

interviewQuestions.title: Preventing CLS with `width`/`height`, `decoding='async'` & Proper `alt` Text
interviewQuestions.content: Explicit `width` and `height` attributes let browsers reserve the image's aspect ratio before download (preventing CLS), while `alt=''` marks decorative images.

blocks.text:
• Preventing Layout Shift (CLS): Modern browsers compute `aspect-ratio` automatically from HTML `width`/`height` even when CSS sets `width: 100%; height: auto;`.
• `decoding='async'`: Allows off-thread image decoding so large images don't jank scroll/render frames (prefer `sync` or `auto` for above-the-fold LCP if needed).
• `alt` Rules: Describe content/function concisely; use empty `alt=''` for purely decorative images (omitting `alt` altogether makes screen readers read the raw filename!).

interviewQuestions.title: `loading='lazy'` vs `fetchpriority='high' | 'low'` & LCP Optimization
interviewQuestions.content: Use `loading='lazy'` for below-the-fold images and `fetchpriority='high'` on the above-the-fold LCP hero image—never combine both on the same element.

blocks.text: • `loading='lazy'`: Defers fetching off-screen `` and `

interviewQuestions.title: `<script>` vs `async` vs `defer` vs `type='module'`
interviewQuestions.content: Standard `<script>` blocks HTML parsing; `async` executes immediately on download in arbitrary order; `defer` and `type='module'` download in parallel and run in order after parsing.

blocks.text:
• Blocking `<script>`: Halts HTML parsing to fetch and execute immediately.
• `async`: Downloads in parallel, pauses HTML parsing to run as soon as ready—execution order is NOT guaranteed (best for independent analytics).
• `defer`: Downloads in parallel, preserves document order, and executes right before `DOMContentLoaded`.
• `type='module'`: Deferred by default, strict mode, scoped module environment, and supports `async` attribute if early execution is needed.

blocks.code:
<script defer src="/app.js"></script>
<script async src="/analytics.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="/main.mjs"></script>

interviewQuestions.title: Resource Hints: `preload`, `prefetch`, `preconnect`, `dns-prefetch` & `modulepreload`
interviewQuestions.content: `preconnect` warms early TLS/TCP connections, `preload` fetches critical current-page assets immediately, `modulepreload` also parses ES modules, and `prefetch` caches likely next-page assets.

blocks.text:
• `preconnect` (and fallback `dns-prefetch`): Opens DNS + TCP + TLS handshake early for third-party CDNs/APIs.
• `preload`: High-priority fetch for late-discovered resources needed on *this* page (custom fonts, CSS background hero images). Requires `as='...'` and `crossorigin` for fonts.
• `modulepreload`: Downloads AND parses/compiles an ES module tree early.
• `prefetch`: Low-priority fetch during idle time for *future* navigation.

blocks.code:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin />
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/app.mjs" />

interviewQuestions.title: Speculation Rules API for Predictive Prefetching & Prerendering
interviewQuestions.content: The Speculation Rules API uses declarative JSON rules (`<script type='speculationrules'>`) to prefetch or fully prerender likely next-page navigations for near-instant transitions.

blocks.text:
• Why It Replaces `<link rel='prefetch'>`: Supports document-level pattern rules (`href_matches`), CSS selector matching, and full background *prerendering* (not just downloading HTML).
• Eagerness Settings: `immediate`, `eager`, `moderate` (e.g., on hover/pointerdown ~200ms), and `conservative` (on pointerdown).
• Safety Considerations: Only prerender idempotent GET pages; avoid URLs that trigger side effects (logout, checkout) and respect `Sec-Purpose: prefetch;prerender` headers.

blocks.code:
<script type="speculationrules">
{
  "prerender": [
    {
      "where": { "href_matches": "/projects/*" },
      "eagerness": "moderate"
    }
  ]
}
</script>

interviewQuestions.title: Technical SEO in HTML: `canonical`, `robots`, `hreflang` & Metadata
interviewQuestions.content: Technical SEO relies on unique `<title>`/`meta description`, `rel='canonical'` to consolidate duplicate query-param URLs, `hreflang` for multilingual pages, and `robots` directives.

blocks.text:
• `rel='canonical'`: Prevents duplicate-content penalties when the same page is reachable via `?utm_source=...` or trailing slashes.
• `hreflang`: Maps localized variants (`en`, `ar`, `x-default`) so search engines serve the user's language.
• `robots` Meta: Controls indexing (`noindex`, `nofollow`) per page—avoid leaving `noindex` accidentally in production.
• `<title>` & `<meta name='description'>`: Keep titles ~50–60 chars and descriptions ~150–160 chars.

blocks.code:
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/projects/portfolio" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://example.com/en/projects" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="ar" href="https://example.com/ar/projects" />
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />

interviewQuestions.title: Open Graph Tags & JSON-LD Schema.org Structured Data
interviewQuestions.content: Open Graph/Twitter meta tags control rich social link previews, while JSON-LD (`application/ld+json`) embeds Schema.org entities for Google Rich Results.

blocks.text:
• Social Cards: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image` (absolute HTTPS URL, ~1200×630px), `og:url`, and `twitter:card='summary_large_image'`.
• JSON-LD Structured Data: Preferred over inline Microdata because it decouples Schema.org entities (`Person`, `Article`, `BreadcrumbList`, `FAQPage`) cleanly from visual HTML markup.

blocks.code:
<meta property="og:title" content="Ahmed Magdy — Portfolio" />
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/og.png" />
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Person",
  "name": "Ahmed Magdy"
}
</script>

interviewQuestions.title: Accessible HTML Data Tables: `<caption>`, `<thead>`, `scope` & `headers`
interviewQuestions.content: Accessible tables pair `<caption>` for title, `<thead>`/`<tbody>` for structure, and `<th scope='col|row'>` (or `headers` IDs for complex multi-level headers) so screen readers announce cell context.

blocks.text:
• `<caption>`: First child of `<table>`; acts as the table's accessible name.
• `<th scope='col' | 'row'>`: Links data `<td>` cells to their column/row headers when navigating cell-by-cell.
• Complex Tables: For merged cells (`colspan`/`rowspan`) with multi-tier headers, link `<td headers='col1 row2'>` to header IDs.
• Never use `<table>` for page layout (if ever legacy, add `role='presentation'`).

interviewQuestions.title: `<a>` vs `<button>`, `button type`, and `rel='noopener noreferrer'`
interviewQuestions.content: Use `<a href>` for navigation and `<button>` for actions; always specify `type='button'` on non-submit buttons inside forms and `rel='noopener'` on external `_blank` tabs.

blocks.text:
• Links vs Buttons: Links navigate (have a URL, support Middle-click/Open in New Tab, triggered by `Enter`); buttons trigger actions (triggered by both `Enter` and `Space`).
• `<button>` Default Trap: Inside a `<form>`, `<button>` defaults to `type='submit'`! Always write `type='button'` for non-submit buttons.
• `target='_blank'` Security: `rel='noopener'` prevents `window.opener` tabnabbing (modern browsers imply `noopener` automatically, though explicit `noopener` remains good practice).

interviewQuestions.title: Securing `<iframe>` Embeds: `sandbox`, `allow` & `title`
interviewQuestions.content: The `sandbox` attribute applies strict least-privilege restrictions to embedded iframes, `allow` grants Permissions Policy features, and `title` is required for screen readers.

blocks.text:
• `sandbox` Attribute: An empty `sandbox=''` blocks scripts, forms, popups, and gives the frame an opaque origin. Add back only minimal tokens (`allow-scripts`, `allow-forms`).
• Critical Security Trap: Never combine `allow-scripts` AND `allow-same-origin` on untrusted same-origin content—the iframe could remove its own `sandbox` attribute!
• `allow` (Permissions Policy): Controls camera, mic, geolocation, clipboard, and payment APIs.
• Accessibility: Always include a descriptive `title` on `<iframe>`.

blocks.code:
<iframe
  src="https://embed.example.com/widget"
  title="Interactive Widget"
  sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"
  allow="clipboard-write; fullscreen"
  loading="lazy"
  referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
></iframe>

interviewQuestions.title: Inline `` vs SVG `` Sprites
interviewQuestions.content: Inline `` enables HTTP caching/isolation; `` sprites balance caching and CSS styling.

blocks.text: • Inline ``: Browser-cached, sandboxed (scripts inside SVG won't run), but cannot style internal paths with external CSS. • ``: Caches the sprite file once while retaining `currentColor` styling. • A11y: Add `aria-hidden='true'` on decorative SVGs, or `role='img'` + `` if standalone informative.

blocks.code:
<!-- Decorative inline icon -->
<svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" width="20" height="20">
  <use href="/icons.svg#arrow-right" />
</svg>

interviewQuestions.title: `<svg>` vs `<canvas>`: Vector DOM vs Immediate-Mode Bitmap
interviewQuestions.content: `<svg>` is resolution-independent retained DOM (great for icons, interactive charts, and accessibility); `<canvas>` is a fast pixel buffer ideal for games, WebGL, and 10k+ particles.

blocks.text:
• `<svg>` (Retained Mode): Every shape is a DOM node supporting CSS styling, click listeners, crisp scaling at any zoom, and screen-reader accessibility—slows down with thousands of nodes.
• `<canvas>` (Immediate Mode): Renders pixels directly via 2D/WebGL/WebGPU APIs; handles tens of thousands of moving objects smoothly, but requires manual hit-testing, DPR (`devicePixelRatio`) scaling, and fallback content inside `<canvas>...</canvas>` for accessibility.

blocks.code:
<!-- SVG: DOM-based vector nodes -->
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Circle"><circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" /></svg>
<!-- Canvas: pixel buffer drawn via JS -->
<canvas id="chart" width="600" height="300">Fallback chart summary</canvas>

interviewQuestions.title: HTML5 `<video>` & `<audio>`: Formats, `preload`, `playsinline` & `<track>`
interviewQuestions.content: Optimize media with ordered `<source>` formats, `preload='metadata'`, `poster` thumbnails, mobile `playsinline`, and `<track>` WebVTT captions for accessibility.

blocks.text:
• `preload` Attribute: Use `metadata` (fetches duration/dimensions without downloading full video) or `none` to save bandwidth; `auto` wastes data.
• Autoplay Rules: Browsers block unmuted autoplay—background loops require `autoplay muted loop playsinline`.
• Accessibility (`<track>`): Provide `.vtt` caption/subtitle tracks (`kind='captions'` includes sound effects for deaf/HoH users; `subtitles` translates dialogue).

blocks.code:
<video controls preload="metadata" poster="/thumb.jpg" playsinline width="1280" height="720">
  <source src="/clip.webm" type="video/webm" />
  <source src="/clip.mp4" type="video/mp4" />
  <track kind="captions" src="/captions-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default />
</video>

interviewQuestions.title: Web Components: `<template>`, `<slot>`, Shadow DOM & Declarative Shadow DOM
interviewQuestions.content: Web Components encapsulate markup and CSS via Shadow DOM (`attachShadow` or declarative `<template shadowrootmode='open'>`) and compose light DOM children via `<slot>`.

blocks.text:
• Core Pillars: Custom Elements (`customElements.define`), Shadow DOM (scoped CSS/DOM tree), and `<template>` + `<slot>` (inert reusable HTML fragments + content projection).
• `open` vs `closed`: `open` exposes `el.shadowRoot` to external JS; `closed` hides it (rarely needed and breaks testing/tooling).
• Declarative Shadow DOM (`shadowrootmode='open'`): Lets SSR render Shadow DOM directly in HTML without waiting for JS hydration.

interviewQuestions.title: `data-*` Custom Attributes, `element.dataset` & Pitfalls
interviewQuestions.content: `data-*` attributes store custom string metadata directly on HTML elements, accessed in JS via `element.dataset` (converting kebab-case to camelCase).

blocks.text:
• Mapping Rule: `data-user-id` becomes `el.dataset.userId` (all values are strings).
• Good Uses: Event delegation hooks (`data-action='delete'`), analytics tags, and CSS attribute selectors (`[data-state='open']`).
• Pitfalls: Never store secrets or large JSON payloads in `data-*` (visible in DOM, bloats HTML, and mutating `dataset` triggers DOM attribute updates).

<button data-user-id="42" data-action="archive">Archive</button>
<script>
  const btn = document.querySelector("button");
  console.log(btn.dataset.userId); // "42" (kebab-case -> camelCase)
</script>

interviewQuestions.title: `role='presentation'` / `role='none'` vs `aria-hidden='true'` & Safari `role='list'`
interviewQuestions.content: `role='none'` (`presentation`) strips an element's own semantic role while keeping its children visible, whereas `aria-hidden='true'` hides the element and its entire subtree.

blocks.text:
• `role='none'` / `role='presentation'`: Removes implicit role (e.g., stripping layout `<table>` semantics) while preserving child text content; ignored if the element is focusable.
• `aria-hidden='true'`: Removes the element *and all descendants* from the accessibility tree.
• Safari Gotcha: VoiceOver + Safari drops list semantics when CSS sets `list-style: none`; adding `role='list'` restores list item counts.

interviewQuestions.title: Internationalization & Bidirectional Text (RTL/LTR): `dir`, `lang`, `<bdi>` & `<bdo>`
interviewQuestions.content: Use `lang` and `dir='rtl'|'ltr'|'auto'` for document/input directionality, and wrap dynamic user strings in `<bdi>` to prevent bidirectional text scrambling.

blocks.text:
• `dir='rtl' | 'ltr' | 'auto'`: Sets base text direction, scroll direction, and mirrors CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`). `dir='auto'` inspects the first strong directional character (ideal for mixed user comments).
• `<bdi>` (Bidirectional Isolation): Isolates unknown usernames/numbers inside RTL sentences so punctuation doesn't jump to the wrong side.
• `<bdo>` (Bidirectional Override): Forces explicit character ordering when needed.

interviewQuestions.title: `contenteditable` (`plaintext-only`), `spellcheck`, `autocapitalize` & `translate='no'`
interviewQuestions.content: HTML attributes provide fine-grained editing and browser-translation controls, including `contenteditable='plaintext-only'` and `translate='no'` for brand/code blocks.

blocks.text:
• `contenteditable='true' | 'plaintext-only'`: Standard `true` allows arbitrary pasted HTML formatting; `plaintext-only` permits inline editing without pasting messy `<span>`/`<font>` tags.
• `translate='no'`: Prevents Chrome/Google Translate from mangling brand names, variable identifiers, or `<code>` blocks.

interviewQuestions.title: Critical Rendering Path: HTML Parsing, Render-Blocking CSS & `DOMContentLoaded` vs `load`
interviewQuestions.content: HTML parses incrementally into the DOM while CSS builds the CSSOM (blocking rendering and synchronous scripts); `DOMContentLoaded` fires before images finish, unlike `load`.

blocks.text:
• Critical Rendering Path: HTML → DOM + CSS → CSSOM → Render Tree → Layout → Paint → Composite.
• Why CSS Blocks JS: Synchronous `<script>` tags pause until pending CSSOM finishes downloading/parsing, because JS might read computed styles (`getComputedStyle`).
• `DOMContentLoaded` vs `load`: `DOMContentLoaded` fires once DOM is parsed and `defer`/module scripts finish; `load` waits for all images, fonts, and subframes.

blocks.code:
<!-- DOMContentLoaded fires after HTML parse + deferred scripts (before images finish) -->
<!-- window 'load' fires only after ALL subresources (images, stylesheets, iframes) finish -->

interviewQuestions.title: Progressive Enhancement vs Graceful Degradation in Modern Web Apps
interviewQuestions.content: Progressive enhancement builds core navigation and form functionality on resilient semantic HTML first, then layers JavaScript interactivity on top.

blocks.text:
• Progressive Enhancement: Start with working HTML (`<a href>`, `<form action method>`, server-rendered content) so pages remain usable before/without JS hydration, then enhance with `fetch`, optimistic UI, and animations.
• Graceful Degradation: Build for modern full-JS environments and add fallbacks if features fail.
• Modern Relevance: Frameworks like Next.js Server Actions, Remix, and Astro embrace progressive enhancement for faster TTI and reliability on flaky networks.

blocks.code:
<form action="/subscribe" method="POST">
  <input type="email" name="email" required />
  <button type="submit">Subscribe</button>
</form>

interviewQuestions.title: Subresource Integrity (SRI) & CSP `nonce` Attributes in HTML
interviewQuestions.content: SRI (`integrity` + `crossorigin`) verifies third-party CDN scripts/styles against cryptographic hashes, while CSP `nonce` authorizes specific inline scripts.

blocks.text:
• Subresource Integrity (SRI): If a third-party CDN is compromised and serves tampered JS/CSS, the browser checks the SHA-256/384/512 hash in `integrity` and refuses execution if mismatched.
• Requires `crossorigin='anonymous'` for cross-origin resources so CORS allows reading the response.
• CSP `nonce`: Server generates a fresh per-request cryptographic random token on `<script nonce='...'>` matching the `Content-Security-Policy` header.

blocks.code:
<script
  src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js"
  integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC"
  crossorigin="anonymous"
></script>

interviewQuestions.title: HTML Form `method`, `enctype` (`urlencoded` vs `multipart/form-data`) & `accept`
interviewQuestions.content: Default forms encode fields as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, whereas file uploads require `method='POST'` and `enctype='multipart/form-data'`.

blocks.text:
• `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (default): Encodes key/value pairs in query string (`GET`) or body (`POST`); cannot transmit binary files.
• `multipart/form-data`: Splits each field and binary file into boundary-delimited parts—mandatory for `<input type='file'>`.
• `accept` Attribute: Hints OS file pickers (`image/*`, `.pdf`), though server-side MIME/magic-byte validation is still mandatory for security.

blocks.code:
<form action="/upload" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <input type="file" name="avatar" accept="image/png,image/jpeg" />
  <button type="submit">Upload</button>
</form>

interviewQuestions.title: `<progress>` vs `<meter>` vs `<output>`
interviewQuestions.content: `<progress>` tracks task completion over time, `<meter>` represents a static scalar measurement within known bounds (disk usage, password strength), and `<output>` holds calculated results.

blocks.text:
• `<progress>`: Task completion (`value` + `max`, or omit `value` for an indeterminate spinner/bar).
• `<meter>`: Static gauge within `min`/`max` with optional `low`/`high`/`optimum` thresholds (automatically colors green/amber/red in browsers).
• `<output for='a b'>`: Live calculation result tied to form inputs (often announced as `role='status'` by screen readers).

blocks.code:
<label for="quota">Storage used:</label>
<meter id="quota" min="0" max="100" low="30" high="80" optimum="20" value="85">85%</meter>

<label for="upload">Uploading:</label>
<progress id="upload" max="100" value="65">65%</progress>

interviewQuestions.title: Viewport Meta Tag, `viewport-fit=cover`, `theme-color` & Zoom Accessibility
interviewQuestions.content: `width=device-width, initial-scale=1` aligns CSS pixels to device width; never disable pinch-to-zoom (`user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1`) as it violates WCAG.

blocks.text:
• `user-scalable=no` Anti-Pattern: Blocks low-vision users from zooming on mobile and fails accessibility audits.
• `viewport-fit=cover`: Extends full-bleed layouts into notch/safe areas (pair with CSS `env(safe-area-inset-*)`).
• `theme-color`: Colors browser chrome/status bars and supports `media='(prefers-color-scheme: dark)'`.

blocks.code:
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover" />
<meta name="theme-color" content="#0f172a" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" />
<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest" />

interviewQuestions.title: Building Fully Accessible Modals & Drawers (Native `<dialog>` vs Custom)
interviewQuestions.content: An accessible modal requires focus movement on open, background containment (`inert`), `Escape` dismissal, proper `aria-labelledby`, and restoring focus to the trigger element on close.

blocks.text:
• Why Native `<dialog>.showModal()` Wins: Automatically handles Top Layer stacking, `inert` background, `Escape` closing, and focus restoration.
• Custom Modal Checklist:
  1. `role='dialog'`, `aria-modal='true'`, and `aria-labelledby` pointing to the modal heading.
  2. Apply `inert` to main app content outside the modal.
  3. Save `document.activeElement` before opening and `.focus()` it back when closing.

interviewQuestions.title: WAI-ARIA Authoring Pattern for Accessible Tabs & Comboboxes
interviewQuestions.content: ARIA Tabs pair `role='tablist'`, `role='tab'` (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`), and `role='tabpanel'` (`aria-labelledby`) with Left/Right arrow keyboard navigation.

blocks.text:
• Tabs Pattern: `Tab` moves focus into the active tab and then directly into the `tabpanel` (not through every inactive tab!); Arrow keys switch between tabs using roving `tabindex`.
• Combobox Pattern (`role='combobox'`): Input carries `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` pointing to `role='listbox'`, and `aria-activedescendant` to track the highlighted `role='option'` without stealing input focus.

interviewQuestions.title: Void Elements & Boolean Attributes in HTML5
interviewQuestions.content:
Void elements (``, ``, `
`, ``, ``) cannot have children or closing tags, and boolean attributes (`disabled`, `checked`, `required`) are truthy whenever present regardless of value.

blocks.text:
• Boolean Attribute Trap: Writing `<button disabled='false'>` in raw HTML still disables the button! You must omit the attribute (or use `el.disabled = false` / React's boolean prop handling).
• Void Elements: `area`, `base`, `br`, `col`, `embed`, `hr`, `img`, `input`, `link`, `meta`, `source`, `track`, `wbr`. Note `<div />` does NOT self-close in HTML—it opens a `<div>`!

blocks.code:
<!-- Void elements have no closing tag -->
<input type="checkbox" checked disabled />
<!-- Presence alone means true; disabled="false" is STILL disabled! -->

interviewQuestions.title: HTML5 Native Drag-and-Drop API & Its Accessibility Limitations
interviewQuestions.content: Native HTML5 Drag-and-Drop uses `draggable='true'`, `ondragover` (`preventDefault()` required to allow drop), and `DataTransfer`, but lacks built-in keyboard/touch accessibility.

blocks.text:
• Required `dragover` Prevention: Calling `event.preventDefault()` inside `dragover` is mandatory—otherwise `drop` never fires.
• `DataTransfer`: Carries dragged payloads (`setData`/`getData`) and dropped OS files (`e.dataTransfer.files`).
• Limitations: Poor mobile touch support and inaccessible to keyboard/screen-reader users unless paired with button/arrow-key reorder controls and `aria-live` announcements.

interviewQuestions.title: `beforeinput` Events, `inputType` & `EditContext` for Rich Text Editors
interviewQuestions.content: `beforeinput` lets editors intercept user intent (`formatBold`, `insertParagraph`, `deleteWordBackward`) before DOM mutation, while `EditContext` decouples IME/text input from the DOM.

blocks.text:
• `beforeinput` vs `keydown`: `keydown` breaks on mobile virtual keyboards, voice dictation, and CJK/Arabic IME composition; `beforeinput` exposes semantic `e.inputType` and `e.getTargetRanges()` and is cancelable.
• `EditContext` API: Allows canvas-based or virtualized code editors (like VS Code/Monaco or Google Docs) to receive native OS spellcheck and IME composition without relying on `contenteditable` DOM hacks.

interviewQuestions.title: Native `<script type='importmap'>` in HTML
interviewQuestions.content: Import Maps let browsers resolve bare ES module specifiers (like `'react'` or `'@app/utils'`) directly to URLs without requiring a JavaScript bundler.

blocks.text:
• How It Works: Placed before module scripts in HTML, the JSON `imports` map (and optional `scopes` for version conflicts) translates bare names into fetchable paths/CDNs.
• Cache Busting Advantage: Maps logical module names to content-hashed URLs so changing one dependency doesn't invalidate importer hashes.
• Baseline Support: Supported across all major evergreen browsers.

blocks.code:
<script type="importmap">
{
  "imports": {
    "lodash-es": "/vendor/lodash-es/lodash.js",
    "@app/": "/src/"
  }
}
</script>
<script type="module">
  import { debounce } from "lodash-es";
</script>

interviewQuestions.title: The `<base>` Tag: Relative URL Resolution, Anchor Pitfalls & CSP `base-uri`
interviewQuestions.content: `<base href>` sets the root for all relative URLs on a page, but unexpectedly redirects same-page `#section` anchor links unless handled carefully and introduces a CSP injection risk.

blocks.text:
• Same-Page `#hash` Trap: With `<base href='/docs/'>` while on `/docs/intro`, `<a href='#top'>` resolves to `/docs/#top` instead of `/docs/intro#top`, triggering unintended navigation!
• Security Risk: If an HTML injection bug lets an attacker inject `<base href='https://evil.com/'>`, all relative `<script src='app.js'>` tags load from the attacker's server—always set `base-uri 'self'` (or `'none'`) in CSP.

interviewQuestions.title: Optimizing Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) Through HTML Architecture
interviewQuestions.content: HTML structure directly drives Core Web Vitals: server-rendered markup + `fetchpriority='high'` speeds up LCP, explicit dimensions prevent CLS, and `defer`/streaming minimizes INP blocking.

blocks.text:
• LCP (<= 2.5s): Server-render the hero HTML (don't hide it behind client JS bundles), avoid `loading='lazy'` on the LCP image, and use `fetchpriority='high'` or `<link rel='preload'>`.
• CLS (<= 0.1): Always specify `width`/`height` on images/iframes/ads and reserve space for dynamic banners.
• INP (<= 200ms): Keep initial DOM size lean (< ~1,500 nodes where practical) and avoid blocking `<script>` tags in `<head>`.
