languages.title: CSS
languages.description: Style sheet language used for describing the presentation of a document written in markup language.

insights.title: 01. CSS Syntax & Rule Structure
insights.content: A CSS rule pairs a selector with a declaration block of property-value pairs inside curly braces.

blocks.text: Each declaration ends with a semicolon (;) and sets a property name followed by a colon and value. External stylesheets linked via <link rel="stylesheet"> are preferred over inline styles for caching and maintainability.

insights.title: 02. Basic Selectors: Universal, Type, Class & ID
insights.content: Target elements broadly with * or tag names, reuse styles across components with .class, and avoid overusing #id.

blocks.text: Class selectors (.card) are the workhorse of scalable CSS because they are reusable and keep specificity low. Reserve #id selectors for unique page anchors or JavaScript hooks rather than general styling.

insights.title: 03. Grouping & Combinator Selectors
insights.content: Combine selectors using comma grouping (,), descendant ( ), child (>), next-sibling (+), and subsequent-sibling (~).

blocks.text: A > B matches only direct children, whereas A B matches any nested descendant. The next-sibling combinator (h2 + p) styles an element immediately following another—great for spacing consecutive paragraphs.

insights.title: 04. Attribute Selectors ([attr], ^=, $=, *=)
insights.content: Style elements based on attribute presence or substring patterns without adding extra utility classes.

blocks.text: Match exact values ([type="email"]), prefixes ([href^="https"]), suffixes ([href$=".pdf"]), or substrings ([class*="btn-"]). Adding an i flag before ] makes the match case-insensitive.

insights.title: 05. The CSS Cascade & Inheritance
insights.content: CSS resolves competing rules by origin, cascade layer, specificity, and source order, while typography properties inherit downward.

blocks.text: Properties like color, font-family, and line-height inherit automatically from parent to child, whereas layout properties like border, padding, and margin do not unless explicitly set to inherit.

insights.title: 06. Specificity Calculation & Avoiding !important
insights.content: Specificity is scored as (IDs, Classes/Attributes/Pseudo-classes, Elements/Pseudo-elements), where inline styles override stylesheet rules.

blocks.text: A selector with 1 ID (1,0,0) beats even ten stacked classes (0,10,0). Keep specificity flat with single classes and avoid !important except for rare utility overrides or accessibility preferences.

insights.title: 07. CSS Color Formats (Hex, RGB, HSL, currentColor)
insights.content: Express colors with hex (#rrggbb), modern space-separated rgb()/hsl() with alpha, and currentColor.

blocks.text: HSL (hue, saturation, lightness) makes creating consistent hover and tint variations intuitive. The currentColor keyword reuses an element's computed text color for borders, shadows, or SVG strokes.

insights.title: 08. Typography Essentials (font-family, size, weight, line-height)
insights.content: Create readable text with system or web font stacks, unitless line-height, and balanced letter-spacing.

blocks.text: Always specify fallback fonts ending in a generic family (sans-serif, serif, monospace). Use unitless line-height (e.g., 1.6) so nested elements calculate line spacing proportionally to their own font size.

insights.title: 09. Text Alignment, Decoration & Overflow Ellipsis
insights.content: Control text casing, underline offsets, and single-line truncation with text-decoration and text-overflow.

blocks.text: Modern CSS lets you customize underline color, thickness, and text-underline-offset for clean link styling. For single-line truncation, combine white-space: nowrap, overflow: hidden, and text-overflow: ellipsis.

insights.title: 10. The CSS Box Model
insights.content: Every rendered element is a rectangular box composed of content, padding, border, and margin.

blocks.text: Padding adds inner breathing room inside the border and shows the element's background; margin creates transparent outer spacing separating neighboring boxes.

insights.title: 11. box-sizing: border-box vs content-box
insights.content: Use box-sizing: border-box globally so width and height include padding and borders predictably.

blocks.text: By default (content-box), adding padding or a border increases an element's total rendered width beyond width. Applying border-box universally prevents unexpected grid or column overflows.

insights.title: 12. Understanding Vertical Margin Collapse
insights.content: Adjacent vertical margins in normal block flow collapse into the larger single margin rather than adding together.

blocks.text:
If an

has margin-bottom: 24px and the following

has margin-top: 16px, the gap between them is 24px—not 40px. Margins never collapse inside Flex or Grid containers.

blocks.code:
h2 { margin-bottom: 24px; }
p { margin-top: 16px; } /* Effective gap = max(24px, 16px) = 24px */

insights.title: 13. Borders, Outlines & border-radius
insights.content: Borders take up layout space, whereas outline draws outside the border without shifting layout—ideal for focus rings.

blocks.text: Use outline with outline-offset for crisp keyboard focus indicators that never cause layout jitter. Combine border-radius: 50% on a square element for circles, or 9999px for pill badges.

insights.title: 14. Background Images, Sizing & Positioning
insights.content: Control background images cleanly using background-size: cover/contain, background-position, and background-repeat.

blocks.text: cover scales the image to fill the container while cropping excess edges; contain fits the entire image inside without cropping. You can also layer multiple comma-separated backgrounds (such as a dark overlay gradient over a photo).

insights.title: 15. CSS Units: px, em, rem & Percentages
insights.content: Use rem for consistent typography and spacing scaled to root font size, em for component-local proportions, and px for crisp 1px borders.

blocks.text: 1rem always equals the root <html> font-size (typically 16px), respecting user browser zoom/font preferences. 1em equals the current element's font-size, making it ideal for padding on buttons that scales with text.

insights.title: 16. Dynamic Viewport Units (vh, dvh, svh, lvh)
insights.content: Prefer min-height: 100dvh over 100vh on mobile so dynamic browser toolbars don't clip hero sections.

blocks.text: Classic 100vh assumes the largest possible viewport, often overflowing beneath mobile address bars. svh represents the smallest viewport, lvh the largest, and dvh dynamically adapts as toolbars expand or retract.

insights.title: 17. Display Modes: block, inline, inline-block & none
insights.content: Control how elements flow and accept dimensions using display: block, inline, inline-block, or none.

blocks.text: block elements stack vertically and fill available width; inline elements flow horizontally and ignore width/height/top-bottom margin; inline-block flows inline while respecting width, height, and vertical padding.

insights.title: 18. Hiding Elements: display: none vs visibility vs opacity
insights.content: Choose between removing from layout (display: none), preserving space (visibility: hidden), or keeping interactivity (opacity: 0).

blocks.text: display: none removes the box from layout and accessibility trees. visibility: hidden preserves empty layout space and blocks clicks. opacity: 0 keeps both layout space and click/focus interactivity while remaining animatable.

insights.title: 19. Positioning: static, relative & absolute
insights.content: Create a positioning anchor with position: relative so child elements with position: absolute align precisely to it.

blocks.text: An absolute element is removed from normal flow and positioned relative to its nearest positioned ancestor (anything other than static). Using inset: 0 stretches an overlay across all four edges.

insights.title: 20. Fixed vs Sticky Positioning
insights.content: Use position: fixed to pin UI to the viewport, and position: sticky to stick an element inside its scrolling container.

blocks.text: A sticky header behaves normally until reaching its threshold (like top: 0), then sticks while its parent remains in view. Note that overflow: hidden on an ancestor disables position: sticky—use overflow: clip instead.

insights.title: 21. Stacking Order & z-index
insights.content: Control which overlapping positioned element paints on top using integer z-index layers.

blocks.text: z-index only affects positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) or flex/grid children. Keep a clean layer scale (e.g., 10, 20, 30, 40) rather than arbitrary values like 99999.

blocks.code:
.dropdown-menu { position: absolute; z-index: 30; }
.modal-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 40; }

insights.title: 22. Overflow Handling (hidden, auto, scroll, clip)
insights.content: Manage overflowing content cleanly with overflow: auto for scrollbars or overflow: clip for zero-scroll clipping.

blocks.text: overflow: auto shows scrollbars only when content exceeds bounds, whereas scroll always reserves them. Unlike hidden, overflow: clip prevents programmatic scrolling and preserves position: sticky inside ancestors.

insights.title: 23. Responsive Sizing with max-width & aspect-ratio
insights.content: Prevent horizontal overflow with max-width: 100% and enforce media proportions with aspect-ratio.

blocks.text: Setting width: min(100%, 72ch) or max-width: 100% keeps containers fluid on narrow screens. aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 automatically computes height from width for videos, cards, and skeleton loaders.

insights.title: 24. Elevation & Depth with box-shadow and text-shadow
insights.content: Add subtle layered shadows using box-shadow (x, y, blur, spread, color) and inset highlights.

blocks.text: Combine two soft shadows—one tight ambient shadow and one larger diffused shadow—for realistic elevation instead of one harsh dark blur.

insights.title: 25. Interactive Pseudo-classes (:hover, :active, :focus)
insights.content: Style pointer hover, press, and keyboard focus states cleanly in LVHA order (Link, Visited, Hover, Active).

blocks.text: Order matters when styling links: :hover should follow :link/:visited, and :active should follow :hover so press feedback isn't overridden. Wrap hover effects in @media (hover: hover) if targeting touch devices.

insights.title: 26. Smart Focus Styles with :focus-visible & :focus-within
insights.content: Show focus outlines only for keyboard navigation via :focus-visible and highlight parent wrappers with :focus-within.

blocks.text: :focus-visible spares mouse clicks from ugly focus rings while keeping keyboard Tab navigation unmistakably clear. :focus-within activates on a container whenever any descendant input receives focus.

insights.title: 27. Structural Pseudo-classes (:first-child, :nth-child)
insights.content: Target elements by sibling position using :first-child, :last-child, :nth-child(odd|even|An+B), and :nth-of-type.

blocks.text: nth-child(3n) selects every third item (useful for grid rows), while :first-child and :last-child remove edge borders or margins in lists cleanly.

insights.title: 28. Negation & Empty State (:not() and :empty)
insights.content: Exclude specific elements with :not() and hide or style containers that have zero children using :empty.

blocks.text: Modern :not() accepts a comma-separated selector list like :not(.active, :disabled). Beware that whitespace or newlines inside an element prevent :empty from matching.

insights.title: 29. Generated Content with ::before and ::after
insights.content: Insert decorative badges, dividers, or overlays via CSS ::before and ::after without extra HTML elements.

blocks.text: Pseudo-elements do not render unless the content property is set (even content: ""). Keep critical text in real HTML rather than content strings because generated text is inconsistent in screen readers and cannot be selected.

insights.title: 30. Customizing List Markers with ::marker
insights.content: Style bullet points, numbers, and <summary> arrows directly using the ::marker pseudo-element.

blocks.text: Instead of hiding list-style and faking bullets with ::before, ::marker lets you change marker color, font-size, or even replace the bullet symbol with a custom character or emoji cleanly.

insights.title: 31. Styling Form Controls (accent-color, :checked, :disabled)
insights.content: Theme native checkboxes, radios, and progress bars in one line using accent-color alongside state pseudo-classes.

blocks.text: accent-color preserves native accessibility and contrast calculations while matching your brand color. Combine :checked, :disabled, and :placeholder-shown for responsive form states.

insights.title: 32. Interaction Hints: cursor, pointer-events & user-select
insights.content: Control pointer appearance, click pass-through (pointer-events: none), and text selection behavior.

blocks.text: Use pointer-events: none on decorative overlays or disabled visual layers so clicks pass straight through to elements underneath. Reserve user-select: none for interactive UI controls, never body copy.

insights.title: 33. Media Cropping with object-fit & object-position
insights.content: Fit and

blocks.text: object-fit works on replaced elements just like background-size works on backgrounds. Pair object-fit: cover with object-position: top (or 50% 20%) on portraits so faces aren't cropped off.

insights.title: 34. Linear, Radial & Conic Gradients
insights.content: Create smooth color transitions, spotlights, and pie-chart rings natively with CSS gradient functions.

blocks.text: linear-gradient() transitions along an angle or direction, radial-gradient() radiates from a center point, and conic-gradient() sweeps around a center circle—perfect for progress rings and color wheels.

insights.title: 35. Smooth Anchor Scrolling & scroll-margin-top
insights.content: Enable smooth in-page navigation and offset anchor targets below sticky headers using scroll-margin-top.

blocks.text: Wrap scroll-behavior: smooth inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference to respect motion sensitivity. Setting scroll-margin-top on section headings ensures sticky navbars never cover jumped-to headings.

insights.title: 36. Flexbox Fundamentals (direction & wrap)
insights.content: Use display: flex for one-dimensional row or column layouts with automatic item wrapping.

blocks.text: flex-direction sets the main axis (row by default, or column). Adding flex-wrap: wrap allows items to flow onto new lines cleanly instead of overflowing narrow screens.

insights.title: 37. Flexbox Alignment & Gap Spacing
insights.content: Align along the main axis with justify-content, the cross axis with align-items, and space items cleanly with gap.

blocks.text: Always prefer gap over child margins inside Flex containers so outer edges stay flush. Combine justify-content: space-between with align-items: center for classic responsive navigation bars.

insights.title: 38. Flex Item Sizing (grow, shrink, basis, min-width: 0)
insights.content: Control how flex children expand and contract with flex: grow shrink basis, and prevent text overflow with min-width: 0.

blocks.text: flex: 1 expands to fill remaining space (shorthand for 1 1 0%). Flex items default to min-width: auto, which can prevent long code or text from shrinking unless you explicitly set min-width: 0.

insights.title: 39. CSS Grid Fundamentals & the fr Unit
insights.content: Build true two-dimensional layouts with display: grid, grid-template-columns, and fractional (fr) tracks.

blocks.text: Unlike percentages, fr units distribute only the remaining free space after gaps and fixed tracks are allocated. Use minmax(0, 1fr) if you want columns to stay strictly equal regardless of wide child content.

insights.title: 40. Grid Item Placement & Spanning
insights.content: Span cards across multiple columns or rows using grid-column and grid-row line numbers.

blocks.text: grid-column: 1 / -1 spans from the very first grid line to the very last line, making full-width banners inside any multi-column grid effortless.

insights.title: 41. Semantic Visual Layouts with grid-template-areas
insights.content: Sketch ASCII-art page templates using grid-template-areas and assign regions with grid-area.

blocks.text: Named grid areas make responsive layout reorganization crystal clear—you simply redefine the string map inside a media query without touching HTML source order.

insights.title: 42. Intrinsic Responsive Grid (auto-fit + minmax)
insights.content: Create fluid card grids that automatically add or wrap columns without writing a single media query.

blocks.text: Using repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(280px, 100%), 1fr)) wraps cards cleanly to the screen width while guaranteeing cards never overflow screens narrower than 280px.

insights.title: 43. Grid Alignment Shorthands (place-items & place-content)
insights.content: Center elements both horizontally and vertically in two lines using display: grid and place-items: center.

blocks.text: place-items combines align-items and justify-items for items inside their grid cells, while place-content aligns the entire grid tracks inside a larger container.

insights.title: 44. Responsive Media Queries & Range Syntax
insights.content: Write mobile-first breakpoints using min-width or modern CSS Media Queries Level 4 range operators.

blocks.text: Mobile-first styling keeps base CSS simple and layers multi-column enhancements as screens widen. Modern browsers also support intuitive range comparisons like (width >= 768px) or (600px <= width <= 1024px).

insights.title: 45. User Preference Media Queries (Dark Mode & Reduced Motion)
insights.content: Respect OS-level accessibility and theme preferences using prefers-color-scheme and prefers-reduced-motion.

blocks.text: Never force intense parallax or looping motion on users who set Reduce Motion at the OS level. Pair prefers-reduced-motion: reduce with subtle opacity fades instead of large spatial translations.

insights.title: 46. CSS Custom Properties (Variables) & Fallbacks
insights.content: Define reusable design tokens with --custom-name and read them via var(--custom-name, fallback).

blocks.text: Unlike Sass variables compiled away at build time, CSS custom properties are live in the DOM: they cascade, inherit, respond to media queries, and can be updated dynamically via JavaScript.

insights.title: 47. Scoped Tokens & Multi-Theme Switching
insights.content: Override CSS variables on a class or [data-theme="dark"] attribute to re-theme whole sections effortlessly.

blocks.text: Component-scoped variables let a single .btn class support primary, danger, or ghost variants just by swapping two local tokens without duplicating padding or hover rules.

insights.title: 48. CSS Math Functions: calc(), min(), max(), clamp()
insights.content: Compute mixed-unit expressions dynamically in CSS using calc(), min(), max(), and clamp(min, preferred, max).

blocks.text: calc() can combine rem, %, and px (e.g., calc(100% - 2rem)). Remember to always put spaces around + and - operators inside calc(). min() and max() pick the smaller or larger value dynamically.

insights.title: 49. Fluid Typography & Spacing with clamp()
insights.content: Scale headings smoothly between mobile and desktop sizes without breakpoints using clamp(min, preferred, max).

blocks.text: Include a rem component in the middle preferred expression (like 1.25rem + 2vw) so user browser zoom still scales the heading proportionally for accessibility.

insights.title: 50. Smooth State Changes with CSS Transitions
insights.content: Animate property changes smoothly using transition: property duration timing-function delay.

blocks.text: Explicitly list the properties you want to animate (such as transform and opacity) rather than transition: all, which can trigger unexpected layout thrashing and slow frames.

insights.title: 51. 2D Transforms & transform-origin
insights.content: Move, scale, rotate, and skew elements on the GPU without shifting surrounding layout using transform.

blocks.text: Because transforms don't alter document flow, neighboring elements never jump when an element scales or translates on hover. Change the pivot point with transform-origin (e.g., left center for underline bars).

insights.title: 52. Individual Transform Properties (translate, rotate, scale)
insights.content: Animate translate, rotate, and scale independently without overwriting each other in a single transform string.

blocks.text: Previously, changing scale on :hover while also running a @keyframes rotate animation required wrapper divs. Standalone translate, rotate, and scale properties compose cleanly in fixed order.

insights.title: 53. 3D Transforms, Perspective & Card Flips
insights.content: Create realistic 3D depth and flipping cards using perspective, transform-style: preserve-3d, and backface-visibility.

blocks.text: Apply perspective on the parent scene (or perspective() first inside transform) to establish foreshortening. Hiding the reverse side via backface-visibility: hidden completes clean front/back card flips.

insights.title: 54. Keyframe Animations (@keyframes & animation)
insights.content: Define multi-step animations with @keyframes and control looping, direction, and fill modes via animation.

blocks.text: Use animation-fill-mode: both (or forwards) when an entrance animation should stay at its final 100% state instead of snapping back.

insights.title: 55. 60/120fps Compositor-Friendly Animations
insights.content: Animate transform, opacity, filter, and clip-path rather than width, top, or left to avoid layout recalculations.

blocks.text: Animating geometric properties like top, height, or margin forces the browser to recalculate layout and repaint every frame. Stick to GPU-composited properties, and use will-change sparingly only right before heavy animations.

insights.title: 56. Visual Filters & Glassmorphism (filter & backdrop-filter)
insights.content: Apply blur, brightness, or drop-shadow to elements with filter, and blur content behind translucent panels with backdrop-filter.

blocks.text: Unlike box-shadow, filter: drop-shadow() follows the alpha contour of transparent PNGs and SVGs. Pair backdrop-filter: blur(12px) with a semi-transparent background for frosted-glass navbars.

insights.title: 57. Blend Modes & isolation: isolate
insights.content: Blend overlapping layers with mix-blend-mode and confine blending boundaries cleanly with isolation: isolate.

blocks.text: Without isolation: isolate on a parent card, mix-blend-mode inside it can accidentally blend all the way down into the page background. Setting isolation: isolate creates a clean local compositing group.

insights.title: 58. Geometric Clipping & Alpha Masking (clip-path & mask-image)
insights.content: Cut custom polygons or circles with clip-path, and fade image edges smoothly using gradient mask-image.

blocks.text: clip-path crops to crisp vector geometry (like diagonal hero dividers or hexagon avatars), while mask-image uses alpha transparency—ideal for fading out scrolling marquee edges.

insights.title: 59. Automatic Numbering with CSS Counters
insights.content: Number steps, sections, or nested headings automatically in CSS using counter-reset, counter-increment, and counter().

blocks.text: CSS counters eliminate hardcoding step numbers in HTML when items can be reordered or filtered dynamically.

insights.title: 60. Typographic Pseudo-elements (::selection, ::placeholder, ::first-line)
insights.content: Customize text highlight colors with ::selection, input hints with ::placeholder, and opening lines with ::first-line.

blocks.text: Keep high color contrast inside ::selection so highlighted text stays legible, and remember ::placeholder uses reduced opacity by default in Firefox unless opacity: 1 is set.

insights.title: 61. Stacking Contexts: Why z-index Sometimes Fails
insights.content: Properties like opacity < 1, transform, filter, and isolation create a new stacking context that traps child z-index values.

blocks.text: If a dropdown inside a card with transform: translateY(0) appears behind the next card even with z-index: 9999, that parent created a local stacking context. Moving modals to the Top Layer (<dialog>/popover) or lifting the parent context solves it.

insights.title: 62. Native Carousels with CSS Scroll Snap
insights.content: Build buttery-smooth horizontal carousels or vertical full-page slides with scroll-snap-type and scroll-snap-align.

blocks.text: Set scroll-snap-type: x mandatory on the scrollable track and scroll-snap-align: start (or center) on child slides—giving touch momentum and keyboard scrolling without heavy JS carousel libraries.

insights.title: 63. Preventing Scroll Chaining & Layout Shift (overscroll-behavior & scrollbar-gutter)
insights.content: Stop inner modals from scrolling the outer page with overscroll-behavior: contain, and reserve scrollbar space via scrollbar-gutter.

blocks.text: scrollbar-gutter: stable prevents the annoying horizontal jump when navigating between short and tall pages or opening a modal that hides the body scrollbar.

insights.title: 64. Newspaper-Style Multi-Column Layout
insights.content: Flow long prose or tag directories automatically across balanced columns using columns and break-inside: avoid.

blocks.text: Unlike Grid, CSS Multi-Column flows text continuously from the bottom of one column to the top of the next. Use break-inside: avoid on cards or figures inside columns so they never split mid-box.

insights.title: 65. Clean Data Table Styling & Sticky Headers
insights.content: Build crisp data tables using border-collapse: collapse, tabular-nums for aligned digits, and sticky <thead> headers.

blocks.text: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums makes numbers in columns align vertically by giving every digit the exact same width. Wrap wide tables in an overflow-x: auto container for mobile safety.

insights.title: 66. @font-face, font-display: swap & Variable Fonts
insights.content: Load self-hosted WOFF2 fonts efficiently with @font-face, prevent invisible text via font-display: swap, and span weights with variable fonts.

blocks.text: One variable WOFF2 font file replaces multiple static weights (100–900), cutting HTTP requests while letting you animate or fine-tune font-weight continuously.

insights.title: 67. Progressive Enhancement with @supports
insights.content: Test browser support for modern CSS properties or selectors before applying enhanced styles using @supports.

blocks.text: Write a clean baseline layout first, then wrap bleeding-edge enhancements—like @supports (grid-template-columns: subgrid) or @supports selector(:has(*))—to progressively upgrade capable browsers.

insights.title: 68. Native CSS Nesting (&)
insights.content: Nest child selectors, pseudo-classes, and media queries natively inside parent rules without Sass or PostCSS.

blocks.text: Use & to reference the parent selector explicitly (especially for &:hover, &.is-open, or modifier classes). Nested @media rules keep responsive overrides right next to the component they affect.

insights.title: 69. Specificity Control with :is() and :where()
insights.content: Simplify repetitive selector lists with :is() and :where(), where :where() always contributes zero specificity.

blocks.text: :is() takes the highest specificity among its arguments, whereas :where() has (0,0,0) specificity—making :where() perfect for base resets and theme defaults that any single utility class can effortlessly override.

insights.title: 70. Print-Friendly Stylesheets (@media print)
insights.content: Hide navigation chrome, preserve readable contrast, and avoid awkward page splits when users print or export to PDF.

blocks.text: Use @media print to hide navbars/buttons, expand link URLs via attr(href) if helpful, and apply break-inside: avoid on cards and tables.

insights.title: 71. Aligning Nested Cards with CSS Subgrid
insights.content: Share parent grid track sizing across nested child elements using grid-template-rows: subgrid or subgrid columns.

blocks.text: Without subgrid, card titles, descriptions, and footers inside a multi-column card grid misalign when titles wrap to two lines. Making each card span 3 parent rows and setting grid-template-rows: subgrid aligns every card section horizontally across the row.

insights.title: 72. Component-Driven Responsive UI with @container
insights.content: Adapt components to their parent container's width—not the whole browser viewport—using container-type: inline-size and @container.

blocks.text: A reusable project card can render vertically in a narrow sidebar and horizontally in a wide main feed automatically when queried against its named container.

insights.title: 73. Container Query Units (cqi, cqw, cqh)
insights.content: Scale card headings and padding proportionally to their enclosing container using cqi (container query inline) units.

blocks.text: 1cqi equals 1% of the query container's inline width (respecting horizontal and vertical writing modes). Combine clamp() with cqi for self-scaling modular components.

insights.title: 74. Container Style Queries (@container style(...))
insights.content: Apply batch styles to descendants based on a parent's CSS custom property value using style() queries.

blocks.text: Instead of writing long descendant class selectors for every variant, set --surface: dark on a section and style all child cards automatically via @container style(--surface: dark).

insights.title: 75. Cascade Layers (@layer) for Conflict-Free CSS
insights.content: Establish explicit priority tiers (reset, base, components, utilities) using @layer regardless of selector specificity.

blocks.text: Rules in a later layer always beat earlier layers even if the earlier rule has higher selector specificity—and unlayered styles override all layers. Declare layer order upfront at the top of your main stylesheet.

insights.title: 76. Donut Scoping with @scope
insights.content: Scope styles strictly to a component root and stop before nested child slots using @scope (.root) to (.slot).

blocks.text: @scope solves two classic CSS pain points: limiting selector reach to a subtree and keeping specificity predictable without BEM naming boilerplate.

insights.title: 77. The :has() Relational Selector (Parent Selection)
insights.content: Style a parent or preceding sibling based on its children or state using :has().

blocks.text: Often called CSS's long-awaited parent selector, :has() lets you style a .card differently when it contains an , adjust grid columns by child count, or react to hovered siblings.

insights.title: 78. Pure-CSS Interactive Patterns with :has()
insights.content: Highlight whole form rows on invalid input, lock body scroll when a modal opens, or dim sibling cards with :has().

blocks.text: Combining :has() with :checked, :invalid, or dialog[open] eliminates dozens of state-syncing JavaScript event handlers.

insights.title: 79. Typed Animatable Variables with @property
insights.content: Register custom properties with strict syntax types (<color>, <angle>, <percentage>) via @property so CSS can interpolate them.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, CSS cannot transition gradients because custom properties are treated as untyped strings. Registering --grad-angle as <angle> lets you smoothly animate conic or linear gradients on hover.

insights.title: 80. Entry Transitions from display: none with @starting-style
insights.content: Define initial pre-mount styles inside @starting-style so newly shown elements (like dialogs or popovers) transition in smoothly.

blocks.text: Elements transitioning from display: none have no prior computed style to animate from. Placing initial opacity: 0 and transform inside @starting-style gives the browser an explicit starting frame.

insights.title: 81. Animating Exit Transitions with allow-discrete & overlay
insights.content: Keep elements visible during exit animations before display: none takes effect using transition-behavior: allow-discrete.

blocks.text: Pairing @starting-style for entry with transition-behavior: allow-discrete on display and overlay lets native <dialog> and [popover] elements fade out smoothly instead of vanishing abruptly on close.

insights.title: 82. Styling the Top Layer & ::backdrop
insights.content: Dim or blur content behind modal <dialog> and [popover] elements using the ::backdrop pseudo-element.

blocks.text: ::backdrop sits directly behind the Top Layer element and does not inherit from :root custom properties in older browsers unless declared on ::backdrop or *.

insights.title: 83. Scroll-Driven Progress Bars with scroll()
insights.content: Bind CSS animations directly to scroll position using animation-timeline: scroll() on the compositor thread—zero JS scroll listeners.

blocks.text: Because scroll-driven animations run off the main thread, reading progress bars and parallax effects stay silky smooth even while JavaScript is busy.

insights.title: 84. Viewport Reveal Animations with view() Timeline
insights.content: Animate elements as they enter and cross the viewport using animation-timeline: view() and animation-range.

blocks.text: Setting animation-range: entry 0% cover 35% reveals cards smoothly as they scroll into view without needing IntersectionObserver.

insights.title: 85. Named Scroll & View Timelines
insights.content: Drive an animation on a separate sibling or parent element from a container's scroll using scroll-timeline-name and timeline-scope.

blocks.text: Declare scroll-timeline-name on the scrolling container and timeline-scope on a shared ancestor so a header or sidebar indicator can react to an inner container's scroll.

insights.title: 86. Perceptually Uniform & Wide-Gamut Colors with oklch()
insights.content: Define vibrant P3 colors with predictable perceived lightness across hues using oklch(lightness chroma hue).

blocks.text: Unlike HSL—where yellow at 50% lightness looks far brighter than blue at 50%—OKLCH ensures equal L values look equally bright to the human eye, simplifying accessible palette generation.

insights.title: 87. Dynamic Shades with color-mix() & Relative Color Syntax
insights.content: Generate hover states, subtle borders, and translucent tints directly from one base CSS variable using color-mix() or oklch(from ...).

blocks.text: color-mix(in oklch, var(--brand) 85%, black) darkens any token dynamically without maintaining separate shade variables. Relative color syntax oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l - 0.1) c h) gives surgical channel control.

insights.title: 88. Automatic Dual-Theme Tokens with light-dark()
insights.content: Declare both light and dark values in a single token using color-scheme: light dark and the light-dark() function.

blocks.text: light-dark(lightVal, darkVal) automatically resolves based on the element's computed color-scheme, drastically reducing duplicated :root and .dark theme blocks.

insights.title: 89. Logical Properties for Seamless RTL & LTR Support
insights.content: Replace physical left/right/top/bottom properties with margin-inline, padding-block, and inset-inline-start for automatic Arabic/English mirroring.

blocks.text: In an English/Arabic bilingual app, margin-inline-start automatically maps to left in LTR and right in dir="rtl"—eliminating [dir="rtl"] override hacks.

insights.title: 90. Logical Sizing, Borders & Corner Radii
insights.content: Use inline-size, block-size, border-start-start-radius, and text-align: start for full writing-mode independence.

blocks.text: Physical border-top-left-radius stays pinned on the left when switching to Arabic; border-start-start-radius and border-end-start-radius flip cleanly with text direction.

insights.title: 91. View Transitions API & ::view-transition-* Pseudos
insights.content: Morph elements smoothly between DOM states using view-transition-name and ::view-transition-group().

blocks.text: Assigning a unique view-transition-name to a card thumbnail and its detail hero image lets the browser cross-fade and interpolate position/size smoothly during document.startViewTransition().

insights.title: 92. Zero-JS Cross-Document View Transitions
insights.content: Enable native page-to-page morph animations across standard multi-page links with @view-transition { navigation: auto; }.

blocks.text: Place @view-transition { navigation: auto; } in both the source and destination same-origin pages so clicking standard <a> links triggers smooth GPU view transitions automatically.

insights.title: 93. CSS Anchor Positioning for Tooltips & Popovers
insights.content: Tether floating tooltips and menus to any trigger element—even in the Top Layer—using anchor-name, position-anchor, and position-area.

blocks.text: Anchor Positioning eliminates manual getBoundingClientRect() math and ResizeObserver listeners, plus supports position-try-fallbacks: flip-block to auto-flip when hitting viewport edges.

insights.title: 94. Animating to height: auto with interpolate-size
insights.content: Transition smoothly between height: 0 and intrinsic height: auto using interpolate-size: allow-keywords or calc-size().

blocks.text: For years, CSS couldn't animate height: 0 to height: auto without JS measurements or max-height hacks. Setting interpolate-size: allow-keywords unlocks native intrinsic-size transitions on accordions and <details>.

insights.title: 95. Rendering Performance with content-visibility: auto
insights.content: Skip layout and paint work for offscreen sections until scrolled near using content-visibility: auto.

blocks.text: Always pair content-visibility: auto with contain-intrinsic-size (e.g., auto 500px) so the browser estimates scrollbar height accurately without jumping as sections enter view.

insights.title: 96. CSS Containment (contain: layout paint style)
insights.content: Isolate heavy widgets so internal DOM updates don't force the browser to re-layout the entire document.

blocks.text: contain: content (shorthand for layout, paint, style) tells the browser that changes inside a widget won't affect outside layout, dramatically speeding up dynamic dashboards. Note: container-type: inline-size also implies inline-size containment.

insights.title: 97. Trigonometric & Stepped Math in CSS (sin, cos, round)
insights.content: Arrange items along circles or compute stepped pixel-snapped values purely in CSS using sin(), cos(), and round().

blocks.text: Radial menus, clock faces, and orbital badges can compute exact X/Y offsets from a single --index variable using cos(angle) and sin(angle) without hardcoded coordinates.

insights.title: 98. Polished Line Wrapping with text-wrap: balance & pretty
insights.content: Prevent awkward single-word orphans in headings with text-wrap: balance and refine body paragraphs with text-wrap: pretty.

blocks.text: text-wrap: balance distributes words evenly across lines for short headings (typically capped at 6 lines for speed), while text-wrap: pretty avoids lonely last-line words in multi-paragraph prose.

insights.title: 99. Filtered Sibling Counting with :nth-child(An+B of S)
insights.content: Stripe or style every nth matching element even when hidden or filtered siblings sit in between using :nth-child(... of S).

blocks.text: Classic :nth-child(even) counts hidden items too, breaking zebra striping when rows are filtered out. :nth-child(even of :not([hidden])) counts only visible items dynamically.

insights.title: 100. Modern Zero-Conflict CSS Architecture
insights.content: Unify @layer ordering, OKLCH + light-dark() tokens, logical RTL properties, @container queries, and @starting-style into one cohesive system.

blocks.text: Modern native CSS provides the complete toolkit for scalable design systems: predictable cascade layers, perceptually uniform dual-theme tokens, automatic Arabic/English mirroring, and zero-JS interactive transitions.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Box Model & `box-sizing: content-box` vs `border-box`
interviewQuestions.content: `content-box` (default) adds padding and border on top of declared width/height, whereas `border-box` includes padding and border inside the declared dimensions.

blocks.text:
• Layers (Inner to Outer): Content → Padding → Border → Margin (note: margin is outside the element's border box and never included in `border-box`).
• `content-box`: `width: 100%` + `padding: 16px` overflows its parent by 32px.
• `border-box`: Keeps `width` and `height` predictable, which is why modern resets apply `box-sizing: border-box` globally.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Cascade Order, Specificity Weight & Property Inheritance
interviewQuestions.content: The CSS cascade resolves conflicts by Origin & `!important` → Cascade Layers (`@layer`) → Specificity `(ID, Class, Element)` → Source Order.

blocks.text:
• Cascade Precedence: Inline styles (`style=''`) > IDs (`#id`) > Classes / Attributes / Pseudo-classes (`.cls`, `[type]`, `:hover`) > Type selectors / Pseudo-elements (`div`, `::before`). Universal `*`, combinators (`>`, `+`), and `:where()` add `(0, 0, 0)`.
• `!important` Inversion: Author `!important` beats normal author rules, while User-Agent `!important` beats Author `!important`.
• Inheritance: Typography (`color`, `font-family`, `line-height`) inherits automatically; box properties (`margin`, `padding`, `border`) do not unless set to `inherit`.

interviewQuestions.title: Cascade Layers (`@layer`): Solving Specificity Wars
interviewQuestions.content: `@layer` lets authors define explicit precedence tiers evaluated *before* selector specificity—a low-specificity utility in a later layer overrides a high-specificity rule in an earlier layer.

blocks.text:
• Ordering Rule: Layers declared earlier have *lower* priority than layers declared later (`@layer reset, base, utilities;`).
• Unlayered Styles Trap: Any CSS outside an `@layer` has *higher* priority than all normal `@layer` rules (the opposite holds for `!important`, which reverses layer order!).
• Practical Architecture: Tailwind CSS v4 and design systems use `@layer` so component overrides never need `!important` or `#id` hacks.

interviewQuestions.title: Flexbox Deep Dive: `flex: 1` vs `flex: auto` & `flex-grow`/`shrink`/`basis`
interviewQuestions.content: `flex-basis` sets initial size before free space distribution; `flex: 1` sets `flex-basis: 0%` for equal columns, while `flex: auto` sets `flex-basis: auto` proportional to content.

blocks.text:
• Three `flex` Shorthand Values:
  - `flex: 1` → `1 1 0%`: Ignores intrinsic content size so columns share space equally.
  - `flex: auto` → `1 1 auto`: Starts from content width then grows/shrinks proportionally.
  - `flex: none` → `0 0 auto`: Rigid fixed size.
• Common Gotcha: Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, preventing long text/code from shrinking/ellipsizing unless you set `min-width: 0`!

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Grid vs Flexbox & `auto-fit` vs `auto-fill`
interviewQuestions.content: Flexbox excels at 1D content-driven rows/columns, while CSS Grid excels at 2D layout-driven tracks; `auto-fit` collapses empty tracks whereas `auto-fill` preserves them.

blocks.text:
• 1D vs 2D: Use Flexbox for navbars, button groups, and wrapping tags; use Grid for page shells, card matrices, and overlapping areas.
• `auto-fit` vs `auto-fill`: When fewer items exist than fit in a row, `auto-fit` collapses empty tracks to `0px` so existing items stretch to `1fr`, while `auto-fill` keeps empty column slots reserved.
• Overflow Guard: Wrap minimum track in `minmax(min(260px, 100%), 1fr)` so narrow mobile screens never overflow horizontally.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Grid Subgrid (`grid-template-rows: subgrid`)
interviewQuestions.content: `subgrid` lets a nested grid item inherit its parent grid's row or column track sizes, aligning internal headings, bodies, and buttons evenly across sibling cards.

blocks.text:
• Problem Solved: Traditional nested `display: grid` creates independent inner tracks, so a 3-line title in Card 1 pushes its footer lower than Card 2's 1-line title.
• How Subgrid Works: Make the card span `N` parent tracks (`grid-row: span 3`) and set `grid-template-rows: subgrid` so all sibling cards share identical row tracks.
• Gap Control: Subgrid inherits parent `gap` by default, which can be overridden locally.

interviewQuestions.title: Container Queries (`@container`) vs Media Queries (`@media`)
interviewQuestions.content: Media queries react to the browser viewport, whereas container queries let modular components adapt to the width of their nearest ancestor containment wrapper.

blocks.text:
• Component-Driven Responsiveness: The same `<ProductCard>` adapts automatically whether placed in a narrow 280px sidebar or a wide 900px main grid.
• Setup: Define `container-type: inline-size` (prefer `inline-size` over `size` so height still wraps naturally!) on a parent wrapper.
• Infinite Loop Trap: You cannot style the container element itself with `@container`—the query must style descendants inside the container.

interviewQuestions.title: Container Query Units (`cqi`, `cqw`) & Container Style Queries (`style()`)
interviewQuestions.content: Container query length units (`cqi`, `cqw`, `cqh`) scale typography and spacing relative to a container's dimensions, while `style()` queries react to custom property values.

blocks.text:
• Container Units: `1cqi` equals 1% of the query container's inline size (`cqw` width, `cqh` height, `cqmin`/`cqmax`), enabling fluid component typography with `clamp()`.
• Style Queries (`@container style(--theme: compact)`): Apply bulk CSS rules to descendants based on an ancestor's custom property value—no size containment required!

interviewQuestions.title: The `:has()` Relational Pseudo-Class ('Parent Selector')
interviewQuestions.content: `:has()` styles a parent or previous sibling based on matching descendants or subsequent siblings, eliminating JS state-class toggles.

blocks.text:
• Beyond Parent Selection: `.card:has(img)` checks descendants; `h2:has(+ p)` checks next siblings; `body:has(dialog[open])` locks page scroll cleanly.
• Specificity Rule: `:has()` takes the specificity of its *most specific* argument inside the parentheses (like `:is()`).
• Forgiving List & Limitation: Unrecognized arguments inside `:has()` are ignored safely, though `:has()` cannot be nested inside another `:has()`.

interviewQuestions.title: `:is()` vs `:where()` vs `:not()` — Specificity & Forgiving Lists
interviewQuestions.content: `:is()` takes the highest specificity of its arguments, whereas `:where()` always has zero specificity `(0,0,0)`, making `:where()` ideal for CSS resets and library defaults.

blocks.text:
• Specificity Contrast:
  - `:where(a, #id)` → `(0, 0, 0)` (zero specificity!).
  - `:is(a, #id)` and `:not(a, #id)` → `(1, 0, 0)` (takes the highest-weight selector in the list even for elements matching `a`!).
• Forgiving Selector Lists: `:is()` and `:where()` ignore invalid/unsupported selectors inside the list instead of discarding the entire rule.

interviewQuestions.title: Native CSS Nesting (`&`) vs Sass Nesting
interviewQuestions.content: Native CSS nesting runs directly in browsers without a preprocessor, using `&` to reference the parent selector and wrapping parent lists in `:is()` semantics.

blocks.text:
• `&` Nesting Selector: Explicitly represents the parent selector—required for compound states (`&:hover`, `&.active`) and placing parent after an ancestor (`.dark &`).
• Key Difference From Sass: Sass performs text concatenation (`&__item` → `.card__item`), which native CSS does NOT support! Also native CSS desugars nested selectors like `:is(parent) child`, adopting `:is()`'s highest-specificity rule.

interviewQuestions.title: `position: sticky` Pitfalls & Stacking Contexts (`z-index`)
interviewQuestions.content: `position: sticky` requires a threshold (`top`/`inset`) and fails if any ancestor has `overflow: hidden`; `z-index` only orders siblings inside the same Stacking Context.

blocks.text:
• Why `position: sticky` Breaks:
  1. Missing `top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right` offset.
  2. An ancestor has `overflow: hidden | auto | scroll` (use `overflow: clip` instead!).
  3. Parent height equals the sticky element's height (no room to stick).
• What Creates a Stacking Context: `z-index` on positioned/flex/grid items, `opacity < 1`, `transform`, `filter`, `isolation: isolate`, and `will-change`. Use `isolation: isolate` to scope `z-index` cleanly.

interviewQuestions.title: Margin Collapsing & Block Formatting Context (`display: flow-root`)
interviewQuestions.content: Adjacent vertical margins collapse into the larger margin in normal block flow; establishing a new Block Formatting Context (BFC) via `display: flow-root` stops collapse cleanly.

blocks.text:
• When Margins Collapse: Adjacent block siblings, parent/first-or-last-child with no border/padding separating them, and empty blocks. Never occurs in Flex/Grid containers or horizontal margins.
• Creating a BFC: `display: flow-root` is the modern, side-effect-free way to create a BFC (unlike `overflow: hidden`, which clips shadows/sticky!).

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Custom Properties (`--var`) vs Sass Variables (`$var`)
interviewQuestions.content: CSS custom properties are live DOM-inherited runtime values mutable via JS and media queries, whereas Sass variables are statically compiled away at build time.

blocks.text:
• Runtime Power: CSS variables cascade, inherit down the DOM, react to `@media`/`@container`/`.dark` class switches dynamically, and can be read/set via `el.style.setProperty('--x', val)`.
• Fallback Syntax: `var(--gap, 16px)` uses the fallback if `--gap` is unset.
• Important Gotcha (IACVT): If a variable resolves to an invalid value for a property, CSS resets that property to `initial`/inherited (does NOT fall back to previous declaration).

interviewQuestions.title: `@property` (CSS Houdini): Typed Custom Properties & Gradient Animations
interviewQuestions.content: `@property` registers custom properties with an explicit type (`syntax`), `inherits` flag, and `initial-value`, enabling smooth transitions on gradients and typed validation.

blocks.text:
• Why Standard `--vars` Couldn't Animate: Browsers treat unregistered custom properties as opaque token strings and snap rather than interpolate.
• `@property` Superpowers:
  1. Smoothly animate gradient angles, colors, or numeric stops.
  2. Prevent unintended inheritance with `inherits: false`.
  3. Provide safe type-checked fallbacks via `initial-value` if an invalid value is assigned.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Logical Properties for Effortless RTL/LTR Internationalization
interviewQuestions.content: Logical properties replace physical directions (`left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom`) with flow-relative axes (`inline-start`/`inline-end`/`block-start`/`block-end`), automatically mirroring in RTL layouts.

blocks.text:
• Axis Mapping (Horizontal Writing Mode): `inline` = horizontal (`left`/`right`), `block` = vertical (`top`/`bottom`).
• Key Properties: `margin-inline`, `padding-block`, `inset-inline-start`, `inline-size` (width), `block-size` (height), `border-inline-end`, `text-align: start`.
• Why Interviews Love This: Eliminates duplicate `[dir='rtl']` override stylesheets in bilingual English/Arabic apps.

interviewQuestions.title: Modern CSS Units: `rem` vs `em`, `dvh`/`svh`/`lvh`, `ch` & `clamp()`
interviewQuestions.content: `rem` scales from root font-size (respecting user browser zoom), `em` scales from parent/self font-size, and `dvh`/`svh`/`lvh` fix mobile `100vh` address-bar overflow.

blocks.text:
• `rem` vs `em`: Use `rem` for global font sizes and spacing (avoids compounding); use `em` for component-proportional padding/icons, and `ch` (~width of `'0'`) for readable line lengths (`max-width: 65ch`).
• Viewport Units Fix: Classic `100vh` overflows mobile screens behind browser toolbars. Use `svh` (smallest viewport), `lvh` (largest), or `dvh` (dynamic as URL bar hides).

blocks.code:
.hero { min-height: 100dvh; }
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 3vw + 1rem, 3.25rem); }

interviewQuestions.title: Modern Media Queries: Range Syntax & User Preference Queries
interviewQuestions.content: Modern CSS supports clean range comparisons (`width >= 768px`) alongside accessibility preference queries like `prefers-reduced-motion`, `prefers-color-scheme`, and `pointer: coarse`.

blocks.text:
• Media Query Range Syntax: Write `@media (400px <= width <= 900px)` instead of awkward `min-width`/`max-width` overlaps.
• Essential Preference Queries:
  - `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: Disables vestibular-triggering parallax/zoom animations.
  - `prefers-contrast: more` & `forced-colors: active`: High-contrast accessibility.
  - `hover: hover` & `pointer: fine`: Distinguishes mouse precision from touchscreens.

interviewQuestions.title: `color-scheme` & the `light-dark()` Function for Native Theming
interviewQuestions.content: `color-scheme: light dark` enables dark native browser UI (scrollbars, form inputs), and `light-dark(lightVal, darkVal)` switches colors automatically without duplicate `@media` blocks.

blocks.text:
• `color-scheme` Property: Tells the browser to style scrollbars, checkboxes, date pickers, and default canvas backgrounds appropriately.
• `light-dark()` Function: Resolves to the first color when active `color-scheme` is `light` and the second when `dark`.
• Manual Toggle Support: Setting `color-scheme: dark` on `.dark` or `[data-theme='dark']` automatically switches all `light-dark()` tokens inside that subtree!

interviewQuestions.title: Modern CSS Colors: `oklch()`, `color-mix()` & Relative Color Syntax
interviewQuestions.content: `oklch()` provides perceptually uniform lightness/chroma/hue across wide-gamut displays, while `color-mix()` and relative color syntax generate design-system shades natively.

blocks.text:
• Why `oklch()` Beats `hsl()`: In `hsl()`, yellow and blue at `50%` lightness have dramatically different perceived brightness; `oklch(L C H)` keeps perceived contrast consistent across hues.
• `color-mix(in oklch, color1 p1, color2)`: Mixes colors or creates translucent tints (`15%` + `transparent`) from a single CSS variable.
• Relative Color Syntax (`oklch(from var(--c) ...)`): Derives hover/border shades dynamically without Sass `darken()`/`lighten()`.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Anchor Positioning (`anchor-name`, `anchor()`, `position-try-fallbacks`)
interviewQuestions.content: CSS Anchor Positioning tethers tooltips, popovers, and menus directly to trigger elements with automatic viewport edge-flipping—replacing JS positioning libraries like Popper/Floating UI.

blocks.text:
• Core Properties: Declare `anchor-name: --id` on the trigger, bind `position-anchor: --id` on the floating element, and place edges with `anchor(top | bottom | left | center)` or `position-area`.
• Automatic Collision Handling: `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline` flips a menu upward or inward if it would clip off-screen.
• Works seamlessly alongside `[popover]`, which runs in the Top Layer.

interviewQuestions.title: `@starting-style` & `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` for Entry/Exit Animations
interviewQuestions.content: `@starting-style` defines the initial pre-render styles for newly inserted or `display: none` → `block` elements, while `allow-discrete` enables smooth exit transitions before `display: none` applies.

blocks.text:
• The Old Limitation: Transitions couldn't run when an element changed from `display: none` to `block` (like `<dialog>` or `[popover]`) because there was no computed initial style.
• `@starting-style`: Provides the initial frame (`opacity: 0`) so CSS transitions animate smoothly on entry.
• `allow-discrete`: Delays flipping `display: none` and Top Layer `overlay` removal until the exit transition finishes.

interviewQuestions.title: View Transitions API (`view-transition-name` & Pseudo-Elements)
interviewQuestions.content: The View Transitions API captures before/after snapshots of DOM updates (or cross-document MPA navigations) and smoothly morphs matching `view-transition-name` elements.

blocks.text:
• How It Works: `document.startViewTransition(updateDOM)` snapshots the old state, executes the update, snapshots the new state, and animates `::view-transition-old(name)` → `::view-transition-new(name)` pseudo-elements.
• Shared Element Morphs: Assigning a unique `view-transition-name` to a thumbnail and its detail hero image automatically interpolates size and position.
• MPA Support: `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` enables smooth transitions across standard multi-page links on the same origin.

interviewQuestions.title: Scroll-Driven Animations (`scroll()` & `view()` Timelines)
interviewQuestions.content: CSS Scroll-Driven Animations bind `@keyframes` progress directly to scroll offset (`scroll()`) or viewport entry (`view()`) on the compositor thread with zero JS scroll listeners.

blocks.text:
• `scroll()` Timeline: Tracks container/root scroll progress from 0% to 100% (ideal for reading progress bars and parallax).
• `view()` Timeline: Tracks an element's visibility journey through its scrollport (`entry`, `exit`, `contain`, `cover` via `animation-range`).
• Performance Win: Runs off the main thread on the GPU compositor when animating `transform` and `opacity`.

interviewQuestions.title: Compositor-Only Animations (`transform`/`opacity`) & `will-change` Caveats
interviewQuestions.content: Animating `transform`, `opacity`, and `filter` runs on the GPU compositor skipping Layout and Paint; overusing `will-change` wastes GPU VRAM.

blocks.text:
• Rendering Pipeline Cost:
  - Layout + Paint + Composite: `width`, `height`, `top`, `left`, `margin` (janky on low-end devices).
  - Paint + Composite: `background-color`, `color`, `box-shadow`.
  - Composite Only (Fastest): `transform`, `opacity`, `clip-path`, `filter`.
• `will-change` Trap: Promotes elements to separate GPU textures—apply sparingly right before animation, never on `* { will-change: transform; }` (exhausts memory).

interviewQuestions.title: Animating to `height: auto` with `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` & `calc-size()`
interviewQuestions.content: Opting into `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` (or using `calc-size(auto, size)`) lets CSS smoothly transition intrinsic keyword sizes like `height: 0` → `height: auto`.

blocks.text:
• Classic Pain Point: For 20 years CSS couldn't transition to `height: auto`, forcing `max-height: 999px` timing hacks or JS `scrollHeight` measurement.
• `interpolate-size: allow-keywords`: Inherited property allowing transitions between `0` and `auto`/`min-content`/`max-content`.
• `calc-size(auto, size * 1.1)`: Also enables math expressions directly on intrinsic sizes.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS `@scope`: Donut Scoping & Proximity-Based Cascade
interviewQuestions.content: `@scope` limits selector reach between a root (`@scope (.card)`) and optional lower boundary (`to (.nested)`), and introduces scoping proximity into the cascade.

blocks.text:
• Donut Scoping (`@scope (.root) to (.slot)`): Styles `.card` internals without leaking into nested sub-components placed inside `.slot`.
• Proximity Tie-Breaker: If two rules have equal specificity, the rule whose `@scope` root is closer in the DOM tree wins regardless of stylesheet order.
• Inline `<style>` Scoping: Placing `<style>@scope { ... }</style>` inside an HTML element scopes styles automatically to its parent.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Containment (`contain`) & `content-visibility: auto`
interviewQuestions.content: `content-visibility: auto` skips layout and painting for off-screen sections until scrolled near, dramatically accelerating initial page rendering on long documents.

blocks.text:
• `content-visibility: auto`: Applies `layout`, `style`, and `paint` containment, skipping rendering work for off-screen subtrees while still keeping them searchable (`Ctrl+F`) and accessible.
• `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 320px`: Supplies a placeholder height so scrollbars don't jump wildly; `auto` remembers the real measured size after first render.
• `contain`: Isolate subtrees (`contain: layout paint`) so internal updates don't trigger whole-page layout recalculation.

interviewQuestions.title: Pseudo-Classes (`:`) vs Pseudo-Elements (`::`) & `:nth-child(n of S)`
interviewQuestions.content: Pseudo-classes select existing elements in a particular state (`:hover`, `:focus-visible`, `:nth-child`), while pseudo-elements create/style virtual sub-parts (`::before`, `::backdrop`, `::marker`).

blocks.text:
• Syntax Rule: Single colon `:` for state/structural pseudo-classes; double colon `::` for pseudo-elements (an element can only have one pseudo-element at the end of a selector, though `:hover::before` works).
• Modern `:nth-child(2n of .active)`: Filters down to `.active` siblings first before applying zebra striping (solves filtered-list styling!).
• Useful Modern Pseudo-Elements: `::backdrop`, `::marker`, `::placeholder`, `::selection`, `::part()`.

interviewQuestions.title: `:focus` vs `:focus-visible` vs `:focus-within` for Accessible Focus Rings
interviewQuestions.content: `:focus-visible` displays focus outlines primarily for keyboard navigation while hiding distracting rings on mouse clicks, preserving WCAG keyboard accessibility.

blocks.text:
• Never Do `*:focus { outline: none; }` Alone: Destroys keyboard navigation visibility.
• `:focus-visible`: Browsers apply heuristics so mouse clicks on `<button>` skip the ring, while `Tab` navigation (and `<input>` clicks) always show a clear focus indicator.
• `:focus-within`: Matches a parent wrapper when any descendant inside it has focus (great for highlighting active search bars or form rows).

interviewQuestions.title: Modern Form Styling: `:user-invalid`, `accent-color` & `field-sizing: content`
interviewQuestions.content: `:user-invalid` waits until user interaction before showing red error styles, `accent-color` themes native checkboxes/radios, and `field-sizing: content` auto-grows inputs/textareas.

blocks.text:
• `:user-invalid` vs `:invalid`: `:invalid` flashes red immediately on page load for empty `required` inputs; `:user-invalid` only matches *after* the user edits/submits the field.
• `accent-color`: One-line theming for `<input type='checkbox'>`, `radio`, `range`, and `<progress>`.
• `field-sizing: content`: Auto-resizes `<textarea>` and `<input>` to fit typed text without JS height hacks.

interviewQuestions.title: Modern Typography: `text-wrap: balance | pretty`, `font-display` & Unitless `line-height`
interviewQuestions.content: `text-wrap: balance` evens line widths in headings, `text-wrap: pretty` avoids orphan words in paragraphs, and unitless `line-height` scales proportionally on child elements.

blocks.text:
• `text-wrap: balance` vs `pretty`: `balance` optimizes equal line lengths (capped ~6 lines by browsers for performance—ideal for headings/cards); `pretty` prevents single-word orphans on the last line of body paragraphs.
• Why Unitless `line-height: 1.5`: `line-height: 1.5em` computes to a fixed px value on the parent and inherits that *fixed px* into larger/smaller headings! Unitless `1.5` inherits the multiplier.
• `font-display: swap`: Shows fallback font immediately during webfont download (prevents FOIT).

blocks.code:
h1, h2, h3 { text-wrap: balance; }
p { text-wrap: pretty; line-height: 1.6; } /* Unitless line-height! */

interviewQuestions.title: `overflow: clip`, `overscroll-behavior`, `scrollbar-gutter` & Scroll Snap
interviewQuestions.content: `overflow: clip` clips overflow without creating a scroll container (keeping `sticky` working), `overscroll-behavior` stops scroll chaining, and Scroll Snap creates zero-JS carousels.

blocks.text:
• `overflow: clip` vs `hidden`: `hidden` creates a programmatic scroll container (breaking `position: sticky`); `clip` strictly clips paint and allows `overflow-clip-margin`.
• `overscroll-behavior: contain`: Prevents scrolling inside a modal/drawer from scrolling the background page or triggering pull-to-refresh.
• `scrollbar-gutter: stable`: Reserves scrollbar space so pages don't shift horizontally when modals toggle overflow.

interviewQuestions.title: `aspect-ratio`, `object-fit` & `object-position` for Media Containers
interviewQuestions.content: `aspect-ratio` reserves responsive proportional boxes without the legacy padding-top hack, while `object-fit: cover` fills frames without distorting image proportions.

blocks.text:
• `aspect-ratio: 16 / 9`: Replaces old `padding-bottom: 56.25%` wrappers; note it only enforces ratio when at most one dimension (`width` or `height`) is fixed.
• `object-fit` Values: `cover` (crops edges to fill box), `contain` (letterboxes full image inside box), `fill` (stretches/distorts).
• `object-position: center top`: Keeps faces/subjects centered when `cover` crops portraits.

interviewQuestions.title: `filter` vs `backdrop-filter`, `clip-path`, `mask-image` & `mix-blend-mode`
interviewQuestions.content: `filter` affects the element itself, whereas `backdrop-filter` blurs/tints pixels *behind* a translucent element; `clip-path` cuts hard vector shapes while `mask-image` supports soft alpha gradients.

blocks.text:
• `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)`: Powers glassmorphism (requires semi-transparent `background`).
• `clip-path` vs `mask-image`: `clip-path` (`polygon()`, `circle()`) creates sharp vector boundaries without altering layout box; `mask-image` uses alpha/luminance gradients for soft fade-outs.
• `mix-blend-mode` & `isolation: isolate`: Controls pixel blending with layers below; `isolation: isolate` caps blending inside a component.

interviewQuestions.title: Modern Centering Techniques in CSS (Grid, Flexbox, `margin: auto`)
interviewQuestions.content: CSS Grid (`place-items: center`) and Flexbox (`justify-content` + `align-items`) are the standard centering patterns, while `inset: 0; margin: auto` works for positioned overlays.

blocks.text:
• Grid `place-items: center`: Shortest 2-line centering for single or stacked children.
• Flex `margin: auto`: Inside a flex container, `margin: auto` centers the item along *both* axes (and prevents clipping overflow when centered content exceeds container height, unlike `justify-content: center`!).
• `place-content: center`: Centers multi-line wrapped items/tracks as a whole block.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Reset vs Normalize vs Preflight & `all: unset | revert | revert-layer`
interviewQuestions.content: Resets strip browser defaults, Normalize harmonizes cross-browser differences, and `revert` / `revert-layer` roll properties back to browser UA or previous cascade-layer defaults.

blocks.text:
• Reset vs Normalize: Modern resets (Josh Comeau / Tailwind Preflight) combine `box-sizing: border-box`, zero margins, and `img { display: block; max-width: 100%; }`.
• `unset` vs `initial` vs `revert` vs `revert-layer`:
  - `initial`: Resets to CSS spec default (e.g., `display: inline` even on a `<div>`!).
  - `unset`: Inherits if inheritable, else `initial`.
  - `revert`: Restores browser User-Agent styles (e.g., `display: block` on `<div>`).
  - `revert-layer`: Rolls back to the previous `@layer` value.

interviewQuestions.title: How Browsers Match CSS Selectors (Right-to-Left) & Style Recalculation Cost
interviewQuestions.content: CSS engines match selectors right-to-left starting from the rightmost 'key selector', so overly broad key selectors (`*`, `div`, `a`) with deep descendant chains increase style-recalc work.

blocks.text:
• Right-to-Left Matching: For `.card ul li a`, the browser first collects *every* `<a>` in the DOM and walks upward checking `li`, `ul`, `.card`.
• Real Bottleneck in Modern Apps: Single-selector speed matters less than **DOM size** and **invalidation scope**—toggling a class on `<body>` with deep descendant selectors forces massive style recalculation.
• Best Practice: Keep selectors flat (single class / BEM / utility) and limit `:has()` on huge root containers like `html:has(...)` when simpler scoped containers work.

interviewQuestions.title: Render-Blocking CSS, Critical CSS Inlining & `media` Attribute Optimization
interviewQuestions.content: External stylesheets block first paint until downloaded and parsed into the CSSOM; inlining above-the-fold Critical CSS and adding `media` hints prevents blocking non-matching sheets.

blocks.text:
• Why CSS Blocks Rendering: Prevents Flash of Unstyled Content (FOUC) and ensures layout accuracy.
• `media` Optimization: `<link rel='stylesheet' href='print.css' media='print'>` still downloads at low priority, but does NOT block initial screen rendering!
• Critical CSS Trade-off: Inline only tiny above-the-fold CSS (< ~14KB gzipped) in `<head>` for fast FCP/LCP while keeping the full stylesheet cacheable; avoid duplicating massive inline styles on every HTML response.

blocks.code:
<!-- Non-blocking print stylesheet -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/print.css" media="print" />

interviewQuestions.title: `grid-template-areas`, `grid-auto-flow: dense` & Overlapping Grid Cells
interviewQuestions.content: `grid-template-areas` creates readable ASCII-art layouts easily rearranged in breakpoints, while placing items in shared grid cells overlaps layers without `position: absolute`.

blocks.text:
• `grid-template-areas`: Visualizes layout regions cleanly and lets media queries reorganize regions without touching HTML order (watch WCAG reading-order vs visual-order alignment!).
• Overlapping Without `position: absolute`: Assigning two children to `grid-area: 1 / 1` stacks them while preserving intrinsic flow height.
• `grid-auto-flow: dense`: Backfills earlier grid gaps with smaller items—avoid on interactive lists because visual order diverges from DOM Tab order.

interviewQuestions.title: Sticky Footer & Holy Grail Layout in Modern CSS
interviewQuestions.content: A 3-line Grid (`min-height: 100dvh; display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;`) anchors the footer to the bottom on short pages and pushes it down naturally on long pages.

blocks.text:
• Sticky Footer: Header (`auto`), Main (`1fr` absorbs extra viewport space), Footer (`auto`)—works cleanly with `100dvh` on mobile.
• Holy Grail Layout: Combine header/footer full-span `grid-column: 1 / -1` with a `minmax(0, 1fr)` center column (`minmax(0, 1fr)` prevents wide code blocks or tables from blowing out the grid track!).

interviewQuestions.title: Styling the Browser Top Layer (`dialog`, `[popover]`, `::backdrop`)
interviewQuestions.content: Elements opened via `dialog.showModal()` or `[popover]` are promoted to the browser's Top Layer above all `z-index` contexts and styled with the `::backdrop` pseudo-element.

blocks.text:
• Top Layer Advantages: Immune to parent `overflow: hidden`, `transform`, or `z-index: 99999` traps.
• `::backdrop`: Full-viewport pseudo-element behind modal dialogs and popovers (inherits only from its originating element, NOT `:root`, unless custom properties inherit or you target `::backdrop`!).
• `:popover-open` & `dialog[open]`: Pseudo-classes/attributes for active open states.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Counters, `content: attr(...)` & Accessibility of Generated Content
interviewQuestions.content: CSS counters auto-number headings or steps purely in CSS, while `content` strings with `/ ''` alt text prevent screen readers from announcing decorative icons.

blocks.text:
• CSS Counters: `counter-reset`, `counter-increment`, `counter(name)`, and `counters(name, '.')` for nested `1.1`, `1.2` numbering.
• `content: attr(data-badge)`: Reads HTML attribute strings into `::before`/`::after` (modern CSS `attr()` is expanding to typed numbers/colors too).
• A11y Warning: Screen readers DO read `content` text! Add alternative text (`content: '★' / ''`) to mute decorative symbols.

interviewQuestions.title: `pointer-events`, `user-select` & `touch-action` for Interaction Control
interviewQuestions.content: `pointer-events: none` passes clicks through overlays, `user-select` controls text highlighting, and `touch-action` tells the browser which touch gestures stay native without JS lag.

blocks.text:
• `pointer-events: none`: Note it disables mouse/touch clicks—NOT keyboard `Tab` focus (use `disabled` or `inert` for true disabling!). Children can re-enable with `pointer-events: auto`.
• `touch-action: pan-y` / `manipulation`: Removes 300ms double-tap delay (`manipulation`) and lets vertical page scrolling stay smooth while handling horizontal swipes in JS.
• `user-select: none`: Prevent accidental label selection on rapid double-clicked buttons.

interviewQuestions.title: `@media print` Styling & `@media (forced-colors: active)` (High Contrast Mode)
interviewQuestions.content: Print stylesheets hide nav chrome and prevent split cards via `break-inside: avoid`, while `forced-colors` adapts UI for Windows High Contrast Mode using system colors and borders.

blocks.text:
• Print CSS: Use `break-inside: avoid` on cards/tables, `@page { margin: 1.5cm; }`, and `print-color-adjust: exact` when brand backgrounds must print.
• `forced-colors: active`: Strips custom `background-color` and `box-shadow` in Windows High Contrast Mode! Never rely solely on background color or shadow to outline cards/focus—add a transparent `1px solid transparent` border that becomes visible in Forced Colors Mode.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Math Functions: `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()` & Unit Rules
interviewQuestions.content: `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, and `clamp(min, preferred, max)` compute mixed-unit dimensions natively in CSS, replacing fixed media-query breakpoint steps.

blocks.text:
• `min(1200px, 100% - 2rem)`: Clean one-line responsive container with automatic horizontal padding.
• `clamp(min, val, max)`: Equivalent to `max(min, min(val, max))`—remember to include a relative unit like `rem` in the middle fluid term (`1rem + 2vw`) so browser text-zoom still works!
• `calc()` Syntax Rules: Always put whitespace around `+` and `-` (`100% - 2rem`), and multiply/divide at least one unitless operand (modern CSS also supports unit-divided ratios like `calc(100vw / 1px)` in typed contexts).

interviewQuestions.title: Styling & Animating SVGs with CSS: `currentColor`, `fill`, `stroke-dasharray`
interviewQuestions.content: `currentColor` binds SVG `fill`/`stroke` directly to text `color` inheritance, while `stroke-dasharray` and `stroke-dashoffset` power pure-CSS SVG line-drawing animations.

blocks.text:
• `currentColor`: Inherited color keyword lets button icons automatically match text color across `:hover` and dark mode.
• Presentation Attributes vs CSS: CSS rules override SVG `fill='...'` HTML attributes.
• Line Draw Effect: Set `stroke-dasharray` equal to `path.getTotalLength()` (or `pathLength='100'` in SVG) and animate `stroke-dashoffset` from `100` to `0`.

interviewQuestions.title: CSS Architecture Trade-offs: BEM vs CSS Modules vs Utility-First (Tailwind v4)
interviewQuestions.content: BEM enforces flat naming discipline, CSS Modules automate local scoping at build time, and Tailwind v4 uses CSS-first `@theme` + `@layer` for minimal, zero-runtime utility styling.

blocks.text:
• BEM (`block__element--modifier`): Predictable flat specificity without tooling, verbose class names.
• CSS Modules: Locally scopes class hashes (`Card_title__x9a`) automatically; composes nicely with component files.
• Utility-First / Tailwind v4: Near-zero CSS growth as apps scale, built-in `@layer` cascade control, CSS-native `@theme` tokens instead of JS config, and zero runtime JS overhead (unlike runtime CSS-in-JS).

interviewQuestions.title: Feature Queries (`@supports` & `@supports selector(...)`) for Safe Fallbacks
interviewQuestions.content: `@supports` tests property/value or selector support natively in CSS so you can pair baseline fallbacks with progressive modern enhancements.

blocks.text:
• Property Checks: `@supports (container-type: inline-size)` or `@supports (color: oklch(50% 0.2 240))`.
• Selector Checks: `@supports selector(:has(*))` safely wraps `:has()` rules without failing in legacy browsers.
• Combinators: Supports `and`, `or`, and `not` (`@supports not (display: grid)`). Remember browsers already ignore unknown standalone declarations automatically—use `@supports` when a *group* of interdependent rules must toggle together.

interviewQuestions.title: Debugging Real-World CSS Bugs: `transform` Breaking `fixed`, `min-width: 0` & `z-index`
interviewQuestions.content: An ancestor with `transform`, `filter`, or `perspective` hijacks `position: fixed` containing blocks; Flex/Grid items default to `min-width: auto` causing overflow until `min-width: 0` is set.

blocks.text:
• Bug 1 (`position: fixed` Not Fixed to Viewport): Any ancestor with `transform`, `filter`, `backdrop-filter`, or `contain: paint` becomes the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants!
• Bug 2 (Flex/Grid Horizontal Blowout): Children default to `min-width: auto`—set `min-width: 0` on the flex/grid child so truncation/scrolling works.
• Bug 3 (`z-index` Ignored): Check if the element is static (`position: static` ignores `z-index` unless a flex/grid child) or trapped inside a lower-level Stacking Context (`opacity < 1`, `transform`).

languages.aboutDescription: Designing beautiful and responsive user interfaces.

roadmap.title: Cascade, Specificity, Box Model & Logical Properties
roadmap.description: Master the cascade, @layer ordering, box-sizing, margin collapsing, stacking contexts, and RTL-friendly logical properties (inline/block).

roadmap.title: Flexbox & CSS Grid Layout Systems
roadmap.description: Build fluid 1D and 2D layouts using Flexbox, Grid repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), named grid areas, and Subgrid track alignment.

roadmap.title: Responsive Design, Fluid Typography & Container Queries
roadmap.description: Combine clamp(), min()/max(), media queries, and @container size queries to create resilient component-level responsiveness.

roadmap.title: Design Tokens, Custom Properties & Color Systems
roadmap.description: Architect dark/light themes using CSS variables, @property, light-dark(), oklch() perceptual colors, and color-mix().

roadmap.title: Modern Selectors, Nesting & Scoping
roadmap.description: Write concise stylesheets with native nesting, :is()/:where() specificity control, :has() parent selection, and @scope boundaries.

roadmap.title: Motion, Transitions & View Transitions
roadmap.description: Animate compositor-friendly transform/opacity properties, @starting-style entry animations, View Transitions API, and prefers-reduced-motion.

roadmap.title: CSS Architecture, Performance & Anchor Positioning
roadmap.description: Optimize rendering containment (contain/content-visibility), eliminate CLS, and adopt emerging Anchor Positioning and Scroll-Driven Animations.

Same-document View Transitions API interoperability across core browser engines

frameworks.title: React
frameworks.description: A JavaScript library for building component-based user interfaces with a focus on efficiency and scalability.

insights.title: 01. JSX Syntax and JavaScript Expressions
insights.content: JSX lets you write HTML-like markup inside JavaScript and embed dynamic expressions using curly braces.

blocks.text: JSX compiles to React.createElement calls under the hood, requiring a single root element, camelCase attributes like className, and closed tags. Any valid JavaScript expression—variables, function calls, or arithmetic—can be evaluated inside {} braces.

insights.title: 02. Functional Components and Exports
insights.content: React components are JavaScript functions whose names start with a capital letter and return JSX.
