interviewQuestions.content: Use semantic HTML first, manage focus explicitly with refs when opening/closing overlays, trap or restore focus, and announce dynamic async updates via `aria-live` regions.

blocks.text:
• Focus Restoration: Save `document.activeElement` before opening a modal/drawer and restore focus to the trigger button on close.
• Keyboard Support: Support `Escape` to close, arrow keys (roving `tabIndex`) in menus/tabs, and avoid clickable `<div>` elements when `<button>` belongs there.
• Live Regions: Use `role="status"` (`aria-live="polite"`) for toast/save confirmations and `role="alert"` (`aria-live="assertive"`) for critical validation errors.

interviewQuestions.title: Why does React Testing Library focus on user behavior over component internals, and how do you test async UI reliably?
interviewQuestions.content: Testing Library queries by accessible roles and text rather than state or class names so tests survive refactors; async UI is tested with `userEvent` and `findBy*` / `waitFor`.

blocks.text:
• Behavior Over Implementation: Query via `getByRole`, `getByLabelText`, and `getByText` rather than internal state or CSS selectors—this doubles as an accessibility check.
• Async Best Practices: Prefer `await userEvent.click(...)` over `fireEvent`, and `await screen.findByText(...)` (which polls cleanly) instead of arbitrary `setTimeout` waits.
• Network Mocking: Use MSW (Mock Service Worker) at the network boundary rather than mocking `fetch` or internal hooks inconsistently.

interviewQuestions.title: Why does calling `setCount(count + 1)` multiple times in one event lose updates, and how do functional updaters fix it?
interviewQuestions.content: `count` is a constant snapshot for the current render, so calling `setCount(count + 1)` three times schedules `0 + 1` three times; passing `c => c + 1` queues sequential updates on the latest pending state.

blocks.text:
• State as a Snapshot: Within a single render execution, `count` never mutates when `setCount` is called; React batches updates and reads the snapshot value each time.
• Functional Updater Queue: Passing `prev => prev + 1` puts updater functions in React's update queue, where each receives the return value of the previous updater before committing.

frameworks.title: Next.js
frameworks.description: The React Framework for Production, offering SSR, SSG, and optimized developer experience.

insights.title: 01. App Router Directory Structure and page.tsx
insights.content: In the Next.js App Router, folders define URL segments and a page.tsx file makes that route publicly accessible.

blocks.text: Every folder inside app/ corresponds to a route path, while non-page files colocated in the same folder are not exposed as URLs. Only directories containing page.tsx (or route.ts) become reachable endpoints.

insights.title: 02. Root Layout (app/layout.tsx) and HTML Shell
insights.content: The root layout is required in app/layout.tsx and defines the shared <html> and <body> tags for your entire app.

blocks.text: Unlike nested layouts, only the root layout contains <html> and <body>. It runs as a Server Component by default and wraps every page, making it ideal for global fonts, providers, and metadata.

insights.title: 03. Nested Layouts and Shared UI Persistence
insights.content: Nested layout.tsx files wrap child routes and preserve component state across sibling navigations.

blocks.text: When navigating between /dashboard and /dashboard/settings, app/dashboard/layout.tsx does not re-mount—its sidebar scroll position and local state remain intact while only the active page swaps.

insights.title: 04. Route Groups (folder) Without Affecting URLs
insights.content: Wrapping a folder name in parentheses like (marketing) organizes routes or applies distinct layouts without adding a URL segment.

blocks.text: Route groups let /pricing and /login live under different layouts—(marketing)/layout.tsx vs (auth)/layout.tsx—while keeping their clean top-level URLs.

insights.title: 05. Private Folders (_folder) for Colocated Helpers
insights.content: Prefixing a folder with an underscore (_components) excludes it and all its files from Next.js routing.

blocks.text: Even if a private folder contains a page.tsx file, Next.js will never turn it into a route, making _lib or _components safe for colocating internal route helpers.

insights.title: 06. Templates (template.tsx) vs Layouts on Navigation
insights.content: Unlike layouts that persist across routes, template.tsx creates a fresh component instance on every navigation.

blocks.text: Use template.tsx when you intentionally want page-entry animations, per-page useEffect analytics tracking, or reset form/DOM state each time the user moves between child routes.

insights.title: 07. Client-Side Navigation with next/link
insights.content: The <Link> component enables fast client-side route transitions and automatic background prefetching.

blocks.text: When a <Link> enters the viewport in production, Next.js prefetches the target route payload automatically so clicking feels instantaneous without full-page reloads.

insights.title: 08. Active Link Styling with usePathname
insights.content: Read the current URL path in a Client Component using usePathname() to highlight active navigation items.

blocks.text: Because hooks require browser/navigation context, wrap only the small nav link item with 'use client' and compare pathname against href.

insights.title: 09. Image Optimization with next/image
insights.content: next/image automatically optimizes, resizes, lazy-loads, and serves modern WebP/AVIF formats while preventing layout shift.

blocks.text: Provide explicit width and height (or fill inside a sized relative container with sizes) and mark above-the-fold hero images with preload or loading='eager' / priority as needed.

insights.title: 10. Google and Local Fonts with next/font
insights.content: next/font self-hosts fonts at build time with zero external network roundtrips and zero layout shift.

blocks.text: Import fonts from next/font/google or next/font/local, attach their CSS variable or className to <html> or <body>, and reference the variable in Tailwind CSS.

insights.title: 11. Instant Loading UI with loading.tsx
insights.content: Adding a loading.tsx file automatically wraps the sibling page.tsx in a React Suspense boundary.

blocks.text: Users immediately see the loading skeleton on navigation while the Server Component fetches data on the server and streams the completed HTML in.

insights.title: 12. Segment Error Handling with error.tsx
insights.content: An error.tsx file defines a React Error Boundary for its route segment without crashing parent layouts.

blocks.text: error.tsx must be a Client Component ('use client'). It receives the error object (plus digest on production server errors) and a reset() function to re-attempt rendering the segment.

insights.title: 13. Root Layout Errors with global-error.tsx
insights.content: app/global-error.tsx catches errors thrown inside the root app/layout.tsx where segment error.tsx cannot reach.

blocks.text: Because global-error.tsx replaces the root layout when active, it must be a Client Component and render its own <html> and <body> tags.

insights.title: 14. Handling 404s with not-found.tsx and notFound()
insights.content: Call notFound() from next/navigation to abort rendering and show the nearest not-found.tsx UI with a 404 status.

blocks.text: Place app/not-found.tsx for global unmatched URLs and segment-specific not-found.tsx files for missing database items like /projects/[slug].

insights.title: 15. Dynamic Route Segments ([slug]) and Async params
insights.content: Folder names in brackets like [slug] capture dynamic URL segments, and in Next.js 16 params is a Promise you await.

blocks.text: Always type params as Promise<{ slug: string }> and await it inside async Server Components, or unwrap it with React.use(params) in Client Components.

insights.title: 16. Catch-All ([...slug]) and Optional Catch-All ([[...slug]]) Routes
insights.content: Spread syntax inside brackets captures multi-segment paths like /docs/a/b/c as a string array.

blocks.text: [...slug] requires at least one segment (/docs/intro), whereas [[...slug]] also matches the base path (/docs) with slug being undefined.

insights.title: 17. Reading Query Strings with Async searchParams
insights.content: Page components receive searchParams as a Promise containing URL query parameters like ?page=2&sort=asc.

blocks.text: Reading await searchParams makes the page dynamically rendered at request time because query parameters vary per request. Wrap dynamic reads in Suspense when using Cache Components.

insights.title: 18. Programmatic Navigation with useRouter
insights.content: Use useRouter from next/navigation inside Client Components to push, replace, go back, or refresh routes.

blocks.text: Prefer <Link> for normal links so browsers get accessibility and prefetching. Reserve router.push() for post-submit redirects or imperative navigation.

insights.title: 19. Reading and Updating Query Params with useSearchParams
insights.content: Read live query parameters on the client with useSearchParams() and wrap the component in <Suspense>.

blocks.text: Clone existing parameters via new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString()) before calling router.replace() so existing filters aren't wiped out.

insights.title: 20. Server Redirects with redirect() and permanentRedirect()
insights.content: Call redirect() in Server Components, Server Actions, or Route Handlers to send a 307/303 redirect.

blocks.text: redirect() throws an internal Next.js control-flow error to stop execution immediately, so never wrap it inside a generic try/catch block unless you rethrow it. Use permanentRedirect() for 308 SEO redirects.

insights.title: 21. 401 Unauthorized and 403 Forbidden Helpers
insights.content: Next.js provides unauthorized() and forbidden() with matching unauthorized.tsx and forbidden.tsx UI files.

blocks.text: Enable experimental: { authInterrupts: true } in next.config.ts to throw semantic 401/403 interrupts directly from Server Components and Server Actions.

insights.title: 22. Static Assets in public/ vs Imported Assets
insights.content: Files placed inside public/ are served from the root URL (/), whereas imported assets get content hashes and automatic dimensions.

blocks.text: Put favicon, robots fallback, or downloadable PDFs in public/docs/resume.pdf, and import local UI images directly in TSX so next/image knows width and height automatically.

insights.title: 23. Styling with CSS Modules and Tailwind CSS v4
insights.content: Next.js supports zero-config Tailwind CSS v4 alongside locally scoped *.module.css files.

blocks.text: CSS Modules generate unique class hashes automatically so styles never collide across components, while Tailwind CSS v4 compiles utility classes via @import 'tailwindcss'.

insights.title: 24. Static Metadata Export in layout.tsx and page.tsx
insights.content: Export a typed Metadata object from any Server Component layout or page to configure title, description, and Open Graph tags.

blocks.text: Next.js merges metadata shallowly from the root layout down to the leaf page and supports title.template for consistent brand suffixes.

insights.title: 25. Favicon, Apple Icon, and Web Manifest Conventions
insights.content: Drop icon.png, apple-icon.png, or manifest.ts into app/ and Next.js automatically wires the <head> links.

blocks.text: File-based metadata avoids manual <link rel='icon'> tags and supports dynamic TypeScript generation via app/manifest.ts.

insights.title: 26. robots.ts and sitemap.ts File Conventions
insights.content: Generate /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml dynamically using app/robots.ts and app/sitemap.ts.

blocks.text: Exporting typed MetadataRoute.Robots and MetadataRoute.Sitemap functions ensures search engines always crawl up-to-date URLs and disallow private routes like /admin.

insights.title: 27. Environment Variables (Server-Only vs NEXT_PUBLIC_)
insights.content: Environment variables without the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix are accessible exclusively on the server and never exposed to the browser.

blocks.text: Prefix only non-sensitive browser config (like analytics IDs) with NEXT_PUBLIC_, because Next.js inlines those into client JavaScript bundles at build time.

insights.title: 28. Next.js Configuration (next.config.ts)
insights.content: next.config.ts configures build output, image rules, redirects, experimental flags, and Next.js 16 caching.

blocks.text: Using TypeScript for next.config.ts with the NextConfig type provides instant autocomplete and validation for all framework options.

insights.title: 29. Configuring Remote Images with remotePatterns
insights.content: Whitelist external image hosts explicitly in next.config.ts using images.remotePatterns to prevent abuse of the image optimizer.

blocks.text: Restrict protocol, hostname, and pathname as tightly as possible so attackers cannot proxy arbitrary third-party images through your Next.js server.

insights.title: 30. Route Segment Config Options (maxDuration, runtime)
insights.content: Export special constants like maxDuration or runtime from a page or route handler to tune execution behavior.

blocks.text: Note that when Cache Components (cacheComponents: true) is enabled in Next.js 16, legacy dynamic/revalidate segment exports are replaced by 'use cache' and cacheLife.

insights.title: 31. Path Aliases (@/* or ~/*) in tsconfig.json
insights.content: Configure clean module aliases in tsconfig.json so imports stay readable regardless of folder nesting depth.

blocks.text: Next.js resolves paths defined under compilerOptions.paths automatically in both Turbopack and TypeScript without extra bundler plugins.

insights.title: 32. Strict TypeScript Typed Routes (typedRoutes)
insights.content: Enable typedRoutes: true in next.config.ts to catch broken <Link href> paths at compile time.

blocks.text: Next.js generates route types inside .next/types so TypeScript flags typos in static or dynamic Link href strings immediately during typecheck.

insights.title: 33. Turbopack as the Default Bundler in Next.js 16
insights.content: Next.js 16 uses Turbopack by default for both next dev and next build, delivering drastically faster HMR and builds.

blocks.text: Turbopack compiles only the routes and modules requested in development and supports persistent filesystem caching and standard CSS/TypeScript features out of the box.

insights.title: 34. Server Components by Default and Zero Client Bundle
insights.content: Every component in app/ is a React Server Component (RSC) by default, shipping zero component JS to the browser.

blocks.text: Server Components can directly query databases, read files, and use heavy server libraries like Markdown parsers without inflating the user's JavaScript download.

insights.title: 35. Client Components with the 'use client' Directive
insights.content: Add 'use client' at the very top of a file to opt into React hooks, event listeners, and browser APIs.

blocks.text: Client Components are still pre-rendered to HTML on the server for fast first paint, then hydrated on the client for interactivity.

insights.title: 36. Composition: Passing Server Components as children to Client Components
insights.content: You cannot import a Server Component inside a 'use client' file, but you can pass it as children from a Server parent.

blocks.text: This lets interactive wrappers like modals, drawers, or theme providers surround heavy server-rendered content without turning that content into Client JS.

insights.title: 37. Keeping Client Boundaries Small (Leaf Components)
insights.content: Push 'use client' down to the smallest interactive leaf component instead of marking an entire page or layout.

blocks.text: Putting 'use client' on a top-level page forces every imported child into the client bundle. Isolating just the interactive SearchBar or VoteButton keeps 90% of the page server-only.

insights.title: 38. Preventing Server Code Leaks with 'server-only'
insights.content: Import 'server-only' in modules that touch secrets or databases so importing them in a Client Component fails the build.

blocks.text: This acts as a compile-time safety net, guaranteeing private API keys or admin queries can never accidentally be bundled into client JavaScript.

insights.title: 39. Preventing Server Imports with 'client-only'
insights.content: Import 'client-only' in modules relying on browser globals like window, localStorage, or WebGL.

blocks.text: If a Server Component accidentally imports a browser-only helper, the build fails with a clear error message instead of throwing ReferenceError: window is not defined at runtime.

insights.title: 40. Fetching Data Directly in Async Server Components
insights.content: Server Components can be async functions that await fetch(), ORMs, or database clients directly during render.

blocks.text: You don't need an internal API route or useEffect just to load initial page data—fetch right inside the Server Component where data lives next to the UI.

insights.title: 41. Parallel Data Fetching with Promise.all
insights.content: Start independent async requests together with Promise.all() in Server Components to cut total latency.

blocks.text: Awaiting one fetch after another creates a server-side waterfall. Triggering independent promises concurrently waits only for the slowest single request.

insights.title: 42. Sequential Data Fetching When Queries Depend on Each Other
insights.content: Use sequential awaits only when the second request strictly depends on a field returned by the first.

blocks.text: Wrap dependent child components in <Suspense> when possible so the parent's initial data renders immediately while the dependent follow-up streams in.

insights.title: 43. Per-Request Deduplication with React cache()
insights.content: Wrap database or ORM queries in React's cache() so calling the same function across layout, metadata, and page runs once per request.

blocks.text: Next.js automatically deduplicates identical GET fetch() calls, while React cache() brings the same per-request memoization to Prisma, Drizzle, or file reads.

insights.title: 44. Route Handlers (route.ts) for GET and POST APIs
insights.content: Create Web-standard Request/Response API endpoints by exporting GET, POST, PUT, or DELETE functions from route.ts.

blocks.text: Never place route.ts in the same folder as page.tsx. Use NextRequest and NextResponse (or standard Response.json) to build REST endpoints, webhooks, or OAuth callbacks.

insights.title: 45. Dynamic Route Handlers with Async params
insights.content: Route Handlers inside dynamic segments like app/api/items/[id]/route.ts receive params as a Promise in Next.js 16.

blocks.text: Await context.params before querying your database, and return 404 JSON responses cleanly when the record does not exist.

insights.title: 46. Parsing Query Strings, JSON, and FormData in Route Handlers
insights.content: Use NextRequest.nextUrl.searchParams for query params and request.json() or request.formData() for request bodies.

blocks.text: Always validate incoming payloads with a schema validator like Zod and handle malformed JSON gracefully with a 400 status.

insights.title: 47. Reading and Setting Cookies with await cookies()
insights.content: In Next.js 16, cookies() from next/headers is async and lets Server Components, Actions, and Route Handlers inspect cookies.

blocks.text: Server Components can only read cookies, whereas Server Actions and Route Handlers can also call cookieStore.set() and cookieStore.delete() with HttpOnly flags.

insights.title: 48. Inspecting Request Headers with await headers()
insights.content: Call await headers() from next/headers inside Server Components or Route Handlers to read incoming HTTP headers.

blocks.text: Common uses include reading accept-language, user-agent, or proxy-injected custom headers like x-request-id. Calling headers() opts the route into dynamic request-time rendering.

insights.title: 49. Dynamic Metadata with generateMetadata
insights.content: Export an async generateMetadata function to compute per-route SEO titles, descriptions, and OG images from params.

blocks.text: Next.js waits for generateMetadata before streaming the <head> and deduplicates shared fetch() or React cache() calls with the page component.

insights.title: 50. Pre-rendering Dynamic Routes with generateStaticParams
insights.content: Export generateStaticParams() from a dynamic route to statically pre-build known slugs at build time.

blocks.text: Returning [{ slug: 'one' }, { slug: 'two' }] lets Next.js build those HTML pages ahead of time so visitors receive instant cached responses.

insights.title: 51. Controlling Unmatched Dynamic Params with dynamicParams
insights.content: Set export const dynamicParams = false to return 404 immediately for any slug not returned by generateStaticParams.

blocks.text: By default dynamicParams is true, meaning unknown slugs render on demand. Setting it to false locks the dynamic segment strictly to pre-built paths.

insights.title: 52. Redirects and Rewrites in next.config.ts
insights.content: Configure static URL redirects (changing the browser URL) and transparent rewrites (proxying internally) in next.config.ts.

blocks.text: Redirects preserve SEO when moving old URLs; rewrites let /docs/* proxy silently to an external service or internal path without changing the address bar.

insights.title: 53. Proxy (proxy.ts) in Next.js 16 (Replacing middleware.ts)
insights.content: In Next.js 16, proxy.ts replaces middleware.ts to run lightweight request interception before routes render.

blocks.text: Place proxy.ts at the project root (or src/proxy.ts) and export a function named proxy(request: NextRequest) to redirect, rewrite, or adjust headers before rendering.

insights.title: 54. Authentication Checks and Header Injection in proxy.ts
insights.content: Use proxy.ts for fast optimistic session-cookie redirects and forwarding custom request headers downstream.

blocks.text: Check for an auth cookie to bounce unauthenticated users to /login immediately, while always re-verifying session signatures inside Server Components and Server Actions.

insights.title: 55. Matcher Configuration in proxy.ts
insights.content: Export a config.matcher array from proxy.ts so proxy logic skips static files, images, and _next assets.

blocks.text: Filtering out _next/static, _next/image, and favicon.ico avoids unnecessary proxy invocations on every asset request.

insights.title: 56. Internationalization (i18n) Routing Pattern with proxy.ts
insights.content: Detect missing locale prefixes in proxy.ts and redirect or rewrite users to /en/... or /ar/....

blocks.text: Combine a [lang] dynamic segment in app/[lang]/page.tsx with proxy.ts cookie/Accept-Language detection for clean bilingual URLs.

insights.title: 57. Draft Mode (draftMode()) for Headless CMS Previews
insights.content: Use draftMode() from next/headers to bypass cached content and preview unpublished CMS drafts securely.

blocks.text: Enable draft mode inside a secret-protected Route Handler by calling (await draftMode()).enable(), then check isEnabled in your Server Components.

insights.title: 58. Static Rendering vs Dynamic Rendering Explained
insights.content: Routes without request-time APIs render statically at build time, while reading cookies(), headers(), or searchParams switches to dynamic rendering.

blocks.text: Static pages are served instantly from CDN/cache; dynamic pages render fresh per request for personalized or real-time data.

insights.title: 59. Opting Into Request-Time Rendering with connection()
insights.content: Call await connection() from next/server when a Server Component needs to render at request time (e.g., Math.random or new Date()) without reading cookies.

blocks.text: In Next.js 16, connection() cleanly signals that the following code depends on an incoming request rather than prerender build time.

insights.title: 60. Handling CORS in Next.js Route Handlers
insights.content: Add Access-Control-Allow-* headers and an OPTIONS preflight handler in route.ts when external origins call your API.

blocks.text: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to trusted domains in production instead of using '*' whenever credentials or private endpoints are involved.

insights.title: 61. Streaming Responses and Server-Sent Events in Route Handlers
insights.content: Return a Web ReadableStream from a Route Handler to stream AI tokens, logs, or Server-Sent Events (SSE) incrementally.

blocks.text: Because Next.js Route Handlers build on standard Web Streams, clients receive chunks immediately without buffering the full payload in server memory.

insights.title: 62. Sharing Types Between Server and Client Components
insights.content: Keep shared TypeScript interfaces in pure type files or use import type so zero runtime code crosses boundaries unintentionally.

blocks.text: Type-only imports are erased completely during compilation, letting Client Components reference database DTO types safely without pulling server modules into the browser.

insights.title: 63. Serialization Rules Across the Server-Client Boundary
insights.content: Props passed from Server Components to Client Components must be serializable (JSON-compatible primitives, plain objects, arrays, Dates, or Promises).

blocks.text: You cannot pass functions, class instances, or database connection objects from Server to Client—pass plain DTO objects or Server Actions ('use server') instead.

insights.title: 64. Integrating Third-Party Scripts with next/script
insights.content: Load external analytics or widget scripts using next/script with strategy='afterInteractive' or 'lazyOnload'.

blocks.text: Unlike raw <script> tags, next/script prevents render-blocking JavaScript from hurting Core Web Vitals and deduplicates scripts across route transitions.

insights.title: 65. Route Handlers vs Server Functions for Mutations
insights.content: Use Server Functions ('use server') for app UI forms and mutations, and Route Handlers (route.ts) for external webhooks or public REST APIs.

blocks.text: Server Functions integrate directly with React 19 useActionState and Next.js cache invalidation (updateTag/revalidatePath), while Route Handlers provide explicit HTTP verb control for third-party callers.

insights.title: 66. Protecting Environment Secrets and Data Access Layers
insights.content: Centralize database and secret access inside a server-only Data Access Layer (DAL) that enforces authorization checks.

blocks.text: Never pass raw database records with sensitive columns (like passwordHash or internal flags) to Client Components; return strictly mapped DTO fields.

insights.title: 67. Debugging Server Logs vs Client Logs and Hydration Diffs
insights.content: Server Component console.log appears in your terminal, while Client Component logs appear in the browser DevTools.

blocks.text:
In Next.js 16, the error overlay displays exact component diff trees when server HTML and client hydration diverge—commonly caused by invalid HTML nesting (like

inside

) or browser-only dates.

insights.title: 68. Streaming SSR with React Suspense Boundaries
insights.content: Wrap slow async Server Components in <Suspense> so Next.js streams the fast page shell immediately and fills slow sections when ready.

blocks.text: Streaming prevents one slow database query or third-party API call from blocking TTFB for the entire page.

insights.title: 69. Granular Loading States with Multiple Suspense Shells
insights.content: Split independent slow sections into separate Suspense boundaries so each card streams in as soon as its own query finishes.

blocks.text: Users can interact with fast widgets and navigation immediately rather than staring at a single full-page spinner.

insights.title: 70. Server Actions ('use server') in Forms
insights.content: Mark an async function with 'use server' to execute secure mutations directly on the server when a form submits.

blocks.text: Next.js creates a secure POST endpoint automatically and supports progressive enhancement so forms work smoothly with React 19 transitions.

insights.title: 71. Server Action Validation with Zod and Return States
insights.content: Validate every Server Action FormData input with Zod and return structured field errors to useActionState.

blocks.text: Client-side HTML validation can always be bypassed. Always validate types, lengths, and formats on the server and return serializable error messages.

insights.title: 72. Calling Server Actions from Event Handlers with useTransition
insights.content: Invoke Server Actions from onClick or onChange handlers inside startTransition to track pending UI state.

blocks.text: Wrapping the async call in startTransition prevents UI freezes and automatically exposes isPending while the server mutation completes.

insights.title: 73. Optimistic Mutations with Server Actions and useOptimistic
insights.content: Combine React 19's useOptimistic with Server Actions to show instant updates before the database confirms.

blocks.text: When the Server Action finishes and calls updateTag/revalidatePath, React seamlessly swaps the optimistic state with the authoritative server snapshot.

insights.title: 74. Securing Server Actions (Auth & Ownership Checks)
insights.content: Treat every Server Action like a public HTTP POST endpoint—always authenticate and authorize inside the action.

blocks.text: Never trust hidden form inputs like userId or role sent from the client; derive the acting user from the server session cookie before mutating records.

insights.title: 75. Cache Components in Next.js 16 (cacheComponents: true)
insights.content: Next.js 16 introduces Cache Components, making caching explicit and opt-in across routes, components, and functions.

blocks.text: Enable cacheComponents: true in next.config.ts to unlock the 'use cache' directive, cacheLife(), cacheTag(), and Partial Prerendering shells automatically.

insights.title: 76. The 'use cache' Directive (File, Component & Function Levels)
insights.content: Add 'use cache' at the top of a file, async component, or helper function to cache its rendered output or return value.

blocks.text: Next.js automatically builds cache keys from serialized arguments and closure values. Do not call request-time APIs like cookies() directly inside a 'use cache' scope—pass them as arguments instead.

insights.title: 77. Configuring Cache Lifetimes with cacheLife()
insights.content: Call cacheLife() inside a 'use cache' scope to control stale, revalidate, and expire durations.

blocks.text: Next.js 16 ships built-in profiles like 'seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', 'days', 'weeks', and 'max', or lets you pass an inline object { revalidate, stale, expire }.

insights.title: 78. Defining Custom cacheLife Profiles in next.config.ts
insights.content: Register reusable named cacheLife profiles under nextConfig.cacheLife for consistent caching across your app.

blocks.text: Named profiles like 'editorial' or 'catalog' standardize stale-while-revalidate policies across teams without repeating magic numbers in every component.

insights.title: 79. Tagging Cached Data with cacheTag()
insights.content: Attach semantic string tags to a 'use cache' function or component using cacheTag() for surgical on-demand invalidation.

blocks.text: Tag both collection queries ('projects') and individual records (`project-${id}`) so mutations only purge affected entries.

insights.title: 80. Instant Read-Your-Own-Writes with updateTag()
insights.content: Call updateTag() inside a Server Action to immediately expire cached entries so the user sees their own mutation right away.

blocks.text: Unlike revalidateTag (which serves stale data while revalidating in the background), updateTag() expires the tag synchronously inside Server Functions for instant read-your-own-writes consistency.

insights.title: 81. Stale-While-Revalidate Invalidation with revalidateTag()
insights.content: In Next.js 16, revalidateTag(tag, 'max') marks tagged cache entries as stale and refreshes them in the background.

blocks.text: Use revalidateTag inside webhook Route Handlers or background jobs when serving cached content for one more request while regenerating is ideal.

insights.title: 82. Path-Based Cache Invalidation with revalidatePath()
insights.content: Call revalidatePath('/projects') to purge cached route payloads for a specific URL path or layout.

blocks.text: Pass 'layout' as the second argument when invalidating a dynamic route pattern like revalidatePath('/blog/[slug]', 'page') or an entire layout subtree.

insights.title: 83. Partial Prerendering (PPR) with Cache Components
insights.content: PPR combines an instant static HTML shell with streamed dynamic Suspense holes inside a single HTTP response.

blocks.text: With cacheComponents: true in Next.js 16, static markup and 'use cache' components form the prerendered shell, while uncached dynamic components wrapped in <Suspense> stream in seamlessly.

insights.title: 84. Mixing Static, Cached, and Dynamic Content on One Route
insights.content: Combine a static shell, a 'use cache' catalog section, and a dynamic Suspense user banner on the same page.

blocks.text: Keep request-time cookies()/headers() inside dedicated Suspense-wrapped children so they never force the cached catalog to re-run per user.

insights.title: 85. Parallel Routes (@slot) for Multi-Pane Dashboards
insights.content: Folders prefixed with @ (like @analytics and @team) render multiple independent pages simultaneously inside a parent layout.

blocks.text: Slots do not add segments to the URL, and each slot can have its own independent loading.tsx and error.tsx boundaries.

insights.title: 86. Parallel Routes Fallback with default.tsx
insights.content: Add default.tsx inside every @slot folder so hard refreshes on nested child routes do not trigger a 404.

blocks.text: During soft navigation, Next.js keeps the previous slot state; on a full browser reload, Next.js needs default.tsx to know what to render when a slot lacks an exact subroute match.

insights.title: 87. Intercepting Routes ((.)photo) for Contextual Modals
insights.content: Intercepting routes let you load a target route inside a modal overlay on client navigation while rendering the full page on direct URL visit.

blocks.text: Use (.) for same-level segments, (..) for one level up, or (...) from the app root to intercept soft <Link> navigations cleanly.

insights.title: 88. Combining Parallel (@modal) and Intercepting Routes
insights.content: Pair a @modal parallel slot in your layout with an intercepting route inside @modal/(.)items/[id] so closing the modal with router.back() restores the list cleanly.

blocks.text: Include @modal/default.tsx returning null so the modal slot stays hidden on normal routes, and render {modal} alongside {children} in layout.tsx.

insights.title: 89. Dynamic OG Image Generation with next/og (ImageResponse)
insights.content: Create app/opengraph-image.tsx using ImageResponse from next/og to render dynamic social share cards from JSX and CSS.

blocks.text: Next.js renders Flexbox-based JSX into a PNG automatically and links the generated opengraph-image URL into your page's <meta property='og:image'> tag.

insights.title: 90. Dynamic and Sharded Sitemaps with generateSitemaps()
insights.content: Use app/sitemap.ts (and generateSitemaps for 50k+ URLs) to pull live routes from your database into /sitemap.xml.

blocks.text: Splitting large catalogs across multiple sitemap IDs keeps memory usage low and satisfies Google's 50,000-URL-per-sitemap limit.

insights.title: 91. Dynamic JSON-LD Structured Data for SEO
insights.content: Render schema.org JSON-LD inside a <script type='application/ld+json'> tag in Server Components for rich search snippets.

blocks.text: Sanitize '<' characters with .replace(/</g, '\\u003c') before serializing user or CMS data into JSON-LD to prevent XSS script-tag breakouts.

insights.title: 92. Webhook Verification with Raw Body in Route Handlers
insights.content: Read await request.text() instead of request.json() when verifying HMAC signatures from providers like Stripe or GitHub.

blocks.text: Cryptographic HMAC signatures depend on the exact raw byte payload; re-stringifying parsed JSON breaks whitespace and key ordering.

insights.title: 93. Node.js Runtime vs Edge Runtime Trade-offs
insights.content: Default to the Node.js runtime for full Node APIs, ORMs, and filesystem access; use Edge only for lightweight globally distributed endpoints.

blocks.text: In Next.js 16, proxy.ts runs on the Node.js runtime by default and Route Handlers support opting into 'edge' per route when zero-Node Web APIs suffice.

insights.title: 94. Server Observability with instrumentation.ts (register & onRequestError)
insights.content: Create instrumentation.ts at the root to initialize OpenTelemetry on server boot and capture server errors via onRequestError.

blocks.text: Next.js calls register() once when a server instance starts and invokes onRequestError(err, request, context) whenever a route, RSC render, or action throws.

insights.title: 95. Preloading Data Before Component Render (preload Pattern)
insights.content: Call a void-returning preload function before conditional checks or child renders to start fetching earlier.

blocks.text: Combining React's cache() with a preload(id) helper kicks off the database or fetch promise immediately so it is already in flight before the nested component awaits it.

insights.title: 96. Security Headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) in Next.js
insights.content: Configure baseline security headers in next.config.ts or dynamic nonce-based Content Security Policy (CSP) in proxy.ts.

blocks.text: Static headers like X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security harden every response at zero runtime cost.

insights.title: 97. Optimizing Bundle Size with next/dynamic
insights.content: Lazy-load heavy client-only widgets like rich editors, maps, or PDF viewers using next/dynamic.

blocks.text: Combine next/dynamic with a lightweight loading skeleton—and pass { ssr: false } inside Client Components when a browser-only library touches window at import time.

insights.title: 98. After-Response Background Work with after()
insights.content: Use after() from next/server to schedule analytics logging or cleanup after the HTTP response is sent to the user.

blocks.text: The user receives the rendered page or API response immediately while Next.js keeps the serverless/server lifecycle alive long enough to finish the after() callback.

insights.title: 99. Standalone Output (output: 'standalone') for Docker
insights.content: Set output: 'standalone' in next.config.ts to trace minimal production dependencies into .next/standalone for tiny Docker images.

blocks.text: Instead of copying the entire node_modules directory into your container, standalone mode bundles a self-contained server.js ready to run with Node or Bun.

insights.title: 100. Production Observability, Caching Audits, and CI Checks
insights.content: Run typecheck, production build, and bundle/cache audits in CI before shipping Next.js 16 applications.

blocks.text: Verify that 'use cache' boundaries do not leak user-specific cookies, all dynamic routes have Suspense/error boundaries, and next typegen + tsc --noEmit + next build pass cleanly.

interviewQuestions.title: How do App Router special file conventions (`page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`) nest at runtime?
interviewQuestions.content: Next.js wraps each route segment's `page.tsx` inside nested `layout.tsx`, `error.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, and `not-found.tsx` boundaries following a predictable React component hierarchy.

blocks.text:
• Component Hierarchy: For any segment, Next.js nests `Layout > Template > ErrorBoundary (error.tsx) > Suspense (loading.tsx) > ErrorBoundary (not-found.tsx) > Page`.
• Why Order Matters: Putting `error.tsx` *inside* `layout.tsx` keeps the layout navigation intact when a page throws, while `global-error.tsx` catches errors thrown in the root layout itself.
• Isolation: Only `page.tsx` or `route.ts` makes a folder publicly addressable as a URL.

interviewQuestions.title: When should you use Server Components vs. Client Components (`"use client"`) in Next.js App Router?
interviewQuestions.content: Default to Server Components for data fetching, secrets, and heavy dependencies; add `"use client"` only at interactive leaves needing state, effects, event listeners, or browser APIs.

blocks.text:
• Server Components (Default): Run exclusively on the server, query databases/APIs directly, keep secrets off the client, and ship zero component JS to the browser.
• Client Components (`"use client"`): Required for `useState`, `useEffect`, `onClick` handlers, browser APIs (`localStorage`, `window`), and third-party interactive hooks.
• Boundary Rule: `"use client"` marks the client boundary for that file *and* everything it imports—so keep client boundaries as small and leaf-level as possible.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the difference between `layout.tsx` and `template.tsx` in Next.js App Router?
interviewQuestions.content: A `layout.tsx` persists across child route navigations and preserves state, whereas `template.tsx` creates a fresh component instance (resetting state and re-running effects) on every navigation.

blocks.text:
• `layout.tsx`: Stays mounted while navigating between sibling/child pages, avoiding re-renders and preserving scroll, input state, or animations.
• `template.tsx`: Mounts a new instance on every route transition (useful for per-page enter animations, per-navigation `useEffect` analytics, or resetting feedback forms across steps).

interviewQuestions.title: How do Route Groups `(folder)` and Private Folders `_folder` organize an App Router codebase without changing URLs?
interviewQuestions.content: Parenthesized `(folder)` route groups organize routes or apply distinct layouts without appearing in the URL path, while `_folder` opts a directory and its subfolders completely out of routing.

blocks.text:
• Route Groups `(marketing)`, `(dashboard)`: Allow multiple root layouts or separate auth/marketing sections while keeping clean URLs like `/pricing` and `/settings`.
• Private Folders `_components`, `_lib`: Explicitly exclude colocated helpers/tests from Next.js routing—even if a `page.tsx` exists inside.
• Caveat: Navigating between two routes that belong to *different* root layouts triggers a full-page browser navigation rather than a soft SPA transition.

interviewQuestions.title: How do Parallel Routes (`@slot`) work, and why is `default.tsx` critical when using them?
interviewQuestions.content: Parallel Routes render multiple independent pages simultaneously inside the same layout via `@slot` props, and `default.tsx` prevents 404 errors on hard refreshes when a slot has no matching sub-route.

blocks.text:
• Named Slots: Folders like `@analytics` and `@team` become props (`analytics`, `team`) on the parent `layout.tsx`, each with its own `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx`.
• Soft vs. Hard Navigation: During soft navigation, Next.js preserves active slot states even if a slot doesn't define the new sub-segment. On a hard reload, Next.js cannot know the previous state—without `default.tsx`, it renders 404.

interviewQuestions.title: How do Intercepting Routes combine with Parallel Routes to build shareable, URL-driven modals?
interviewQuestions.content: Intercepting Routes (`(.)photo/[id]`) catch soft client navigations to render a modal inside a `@modal` slot, while a direct reload or shared link hits the real `/photo/[id]` full-page route.

blocks.text:
• Matcher Conventions: `(.)` matches same level, `(..)` one level up, `(..)(..)` two levels up, `(...)` from `app/` root (counting route segments, not `@slot` folders).
• Best-of-Both-Worlds UX: Clicking a photo card opens an overlay modal with a real URL (`/photos/42`), closing via `router.back()`; refreshing or pasting that URL renders the dedicated full page.
• Tip: Return `null` in `@modal/default.tsx` so the modal slot renders nothing when closed.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the difference between `[slug]`, `[...slug]`, and `[[...slug]]` dynamic route segments?
interviewQuestions.content: `[slug]` matches a single required segment, `[...slug]` matches one or more segments as an array, and `[[...slug]]` is an optional catch-all that also matches the base path with `undefined`.

blocks.text:
• `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`: Matches `/blog/a`, receives `{ slug: "a" }`.
• `app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx`: Matches `/docs/a` and `/docs/a/b`, receives `{ slug: ["a", "b"] }`, does NOT match `/docs`.
• `app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`: Matches `/docs` (`slug` is `undefined`) as well as `/docs/a/b`. Cannot coexist with a `page.tsx` at the same level.

interviewQuestions.title: Why did Next.js 15 make `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, and `draftMode()` asynchronous?
interviewQuestions.content: Making request-time APIs return Promises allows Next.js to prepare static/cached shells and defer dynamic work until a component actually `await`s request-specific data.

blocks.text:
• Breaking Shift in Next.js 15+: `params`, `searchParams`, `await cookies()`, `await headers()`, and `await draftMode()` must all be awaited in Server Components, Route Handlers, and `generateMetadata`.
• In Client Components: Page `params` or `searchParams` promises can be unwrapped with React 19's `use(params)` or via `useParams()` / `useSearchParams()`.
• Architectural Benefit: Next.js can detect exactly which subtree touches dynamic request data and stream/PPR around it.

interviewQuestions.title: How did default caching behavior for `fetch`, `GET` Route Handlers, and client navigations change in Next.js 15+?
interviewQuestions.content: Next.js 15 reversed aggressive implicit caching: `fetch()` requests default to `no-store`, `GET` Route Handlers are uncached by default, and client router page segments default to `staleTime: 0`.

blocks.text:
• Next.js 13/14 Pain Point: Implicit `force-cache` on `fetch` and `GET` handlers surprised developers with stale data.
• Next.js 15+ Defaults:
  1. `fetch()` defaults to uncached on every request unless `{ cache: "force-cache" }` or `next: { revalidate }` is passed (or wrapped in `"use cache"`).
  2. `GET` Route Handlers run dynamically unless `export const dynamic = "force-static"` is set.
  3. Client Router Cache no longer caches page segments indefinitely (though shared layouts and back/forward history still reuse cache).

interviewQuestions.title: How does Next.js 16's `cacheComponents` and `"use cache"` directive work compared to legacy route segment caching?
interviewQuestions.content: Enabling `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts` replaces heuristic route-level caching with explicit, compiler-driven `"use cache"` directives at the file, component, or function level.

blocks.text:
• Opt-In Explicit Caching: Place `"use cache"` at the top of a file, an async Server Component, or an async helper function—works for DB queries, ORM calls, and `fetch` alike.
• Automatic Cache Keys: Next.js hashes build ID, function location, and serializable arguments/props into the cache key.
• Strict Rule: Dynamic request APIs (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `searchParams`) cannot be read inside `"use cache"` directly; read them outside and pass needed values (like `tenantId`) as arguments.

interviewQuestions.title: How do `cacheLife()` and `cacheTag()` control freshness and invalidation inside `"use cache"` functions?
interviewQuestions.content: `cacheLife()` sets stale, revalidate, and expire durations via presets or custom objects, while `cacheTag()` attaches string labels for targeted on-demand invalidation.

blocks.text:
• `cacheLife(profile)`: Built-in profiles include `"seconds"`, `"minutes"`, `"hours"`, `"days"`, `"weeks"`, and `"max"`, or custom `{ stale, revalidate, expire }` timings (also definable in `next.config.ts` under `cacheLife`).
• `cacheTag(...tags)`: Tag entries dynamically based on arguments (e.g., `cacheTag("posts", `post-${slug}`)`) so updates invalidate only affected entries instead of flushing the whole site.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the difference between `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` and `updateTag(tag)` in Next.js 16?
interviewQuestions.content: `revalidateTag(tag, 'max')` triggers stale-while-revalidate background refreshing, whereas `updateTag(tag)` (Server Actions only) immediately expires the cache so the user sees their own write right away.

blocks.text:
• `revalidateTag(tag, profile)`: In Next.js 16, passing a second `cacheLife` profile argument (typically `"max"`) is required; single-arg `revalidateTag(tag)` is deprecated. It serves stale data to the next visitor while revalidating asynchronously—usable in Route Handlers and Server Actions.
• `updateTag(tag)`: Exclusive to Server Actions; it expires the cached entry synchronously so the immediate redirect or re-render fetches fresh data ("read-your-own-writes").

interviewQuestions.title: When should you use `revalidatePath()` versus tag-based invalidation (`revalidateTag` / `updateTag`)?
interviewQuestions.content: `revalidatePath()` purges all cached data associated with a specific URL path or layout group, while tag-based invalidation targets shared entities across any route that tagged them.

blocks.text:
• `revalidatePath("/blog/[slug]", "page" | "layout")`: Simple when a mutation clearly maps to one route, though `"layout"` invalidates an entire subtree broadly.
• Tag-Based Invalidation: Far better for normalized/shared data (e.g., an updated product price shown on `/`, `/cart`, and `/products/[id]`)—invalidating `"product-42"` updates every page displaying it without purging unrelated data.

interviewQuestions.title: How does Partial Prerendering (PPR) work with `cacheComponents` in Next.js 16?
interviewQuestions.content: PPR pre-renders a static HTML shell at build time (including cached components and Suspense fallbacks) and streams uncached dynamic `<Suspense>` holes concurrently on the same HTTP request.

blocks.text:
• Unified Route Model: You no longer have to choose between fully static SSG or fully dynamic SSR for an entire route.
• How It Executes: Build-time static/cached parts (`"use cache"` + layout + navigation) ship immediately from CDN/edge as the static shell; dynamic islands reading `cookies()` or uncached DB data sit inside `<Suspense>` and stream in parallel as they resolve.
• Next.js 16 Activation: Enabled via `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts`.

interviewQuestions.title: How does `loading.tsx` relate to React `<Suspense>`, and when should you place manual `<Suspense>` boundaries instead?
interviewQuestions.content: `loading.tsx` automatically wraps the entire `page.tsx` in a `<Suspense>` boundary, whereas manual `<Suspense>` lets fast sections appear immediately while slower widgets stream independently.

blocks.text:
• `loading.tsx`: Great for instant route-level feedback on navigation—keeps parent `layout.tsx` interactive immediately.
• Granular `<Suspense>`: If a page has fast product info (30ms) and slow reviews (900ms), fetching reviews inside their own async Server Component wrapped in `<Suspense>` prevents the 900ms query from blocking the whole page.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you prevent sequential data-fetching waterfalls in Next.js Server Components?
interviewQuestions.content: Avoid sequential `await` chains in one component; initiate independent promises in parallel with `Promise.all()`, push fetches into sibling Suspense components, or use preload helpers.

blocks.text:
• Parallel Fetching: Start promises before awaiting them (`const [user, posts] = await Promise.all([getUser(), getPosts()])`).
• Component-Level Parallelism: Two sibling async Server Components under separate `<Suspense>` boundaries start fetching concurrently during React's render pass.
• Preload Pattern: Call `void getItem(id)` early (backed by React `cache()`) so a deep child finds the promise already in flight.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the difference between React's `cache()` and Next.js's `"use cache"` (or `fetch` cache)?
interviewQuestions.content: React's `cache()` only deduplicates identical function calls within a single server request pass, whereas `"use cache"` persists results across multiple users and requests.

blocks.text:
• React `cache(fn)`: Request-scoped memoization. Useful when both `generateMetadata` and `Page` (or multiple nested components) call `getCurrentUser()`—the DB is queried once per HTTP request, never leaked across users.
• Next.js `"use cache"`: Cross-request persistent cache stored in the Next.js cache handler/CDN until its `cacheLife` expires or `revalidateTag`/`updateTag` invalidates it.

interviewQuestions.title: How do the `server-only` package and a Data Access Layer (DAL) prevent secret or PII leaks to Client Components?
interviewQuestions.content: Importing `server-only` fails the build if a server module is accidentally imported into a Client Component, while a DAL returns explicit DTOs instead of raw database rows.

blocks.text:
• Build-Time Guard: Putting `import "server-only";` at the top of DB/auth helpers prevents accidental bundling into `"use client"` graphs.
• DTO Projection (DAL): Never pass a full `user` Prisma/Drizzle row directly into a Client Component—every prop passed across the boundary is serialized into the HTML/RSC payload. Return only safe fields (`{ id, name, avatarUrl }`).

interviewQuestions.title: How do Server Actions (`"use server"`) work, and how do they integrate with forms and `useActionState`?
interviewQuestions.content: Server Actions are async functions marked with `"use server"` that Next.js exposes as POST endpoints, enabling form submissions and mutations with progressive enhancement and `useActionState`.

blocks.text:
• Defining Actions: Add `"use server"` at the top of an async function (inside a Server Component) or at the top of a dedicated actions file imported by Client Components.
• Form Integration: Pass directly to `<form action={myAction}>` or wrap with `useActionState(myAction, initialState)` for pending states and returned validation errors.
• Progressive Enhancement: Native `<form action={...}>` works even before JavaScript finishes hydrating.

interviewQuestions.title: What security checks are mandatory inside every Server Action?
interviewQuestions.content: Server Actions are public HTTP POST endpoints under the hood, so every action must independently verify authentication, authorization, and input schemas (e.g., via Zod).

blocks.text:
• Public Endpoint Reality: Any client can craft a POST request directly to a Server Action's action ID—never assume UI hiding or parent layout checks protect it.
• Required Checklist:
  1. Authenticate the session (`const session = await getSession()`).
  2. Authorize resource ownership (`post.authorId === session.userId`).
  3. Validate and type-parse every input with Zod (never trust `FormData` or client-passed IDs).
  4. Be aware Next.js validates `Origin` vs `Host` headers for CSRF protection; configure `serverActions.allowedOrigins` when behind reverse proxies.

interviewQuestions.title: Why does calling `redirect()` or `notFound()` inside a `try/catch` block in Next.js fail, and how do you fix it?
interviewQuestions.content: `redirect()` and `notFound()` work by throwing special internal control-flow errors; a broad `catch` block intercepts them unless you move `redirect()` outside `try` or call `unstable_rethrow(err)`.

blocks.text:
• Control-Flow Throw: Next.js interrupts server execution by throwing a framework error (`NEXT_REDIRECT` / `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK`).
• The Bug: Catching all errors in `try { ... redirect("/done"); } catch (e) { return { error: "Failed" }; }` swallows the redirect and shows a false failure!
• Solutions: Call `redirect()` *after* the `try/catch` block, or call `unstable_rethrow(err)` (from `next/navigation`) inside `catch`.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you combine Server Actions with React 19's `useOptimistic` for instant UI feedback?
interviewQuestions.content: Wrap the Server Action call inside a client form action that invokes `addOptimistic(payload)` immediately before `await serverAction(...)`, reverting automatically if the server throws or returns unchanged data.

blocks.text:
• Flow: User submits -> client action triggers `addOptimistic` (instant UI update) -> awaits Server Action -> Server Action calls `updateTag`/`revalidatePath` -> new server props replace the optimistic projection.
• Failure Handling: If the Server Action returns an error object instead of updating server data, `useOptimistic` discards the temporary item cleanly and you surface a toast/error message.

interviewQuestions.title: When should you use Route Handlers (`route.ts`) instead of Server Actions?
interviewQuestions.content: Use Route Handlers for external HTTP APIs, third-party webhooks, OAuth callbacks, custom streaming/binary downloads, and public REST endpoints; use Server Actions for UI-driven mutations.

blocks.text:
• Route Handlers (`app/api/.../route.ts`): Export HTTP verb handlers (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`), return `NextResponse` or Web `Response`, control status codes/headers/CORS, and handle non-form clients (mobile apps, Stripe webhooks).
• Conflict Rule: A `route.ts` and `page.tsx` cannot exist in the exact same route folder.

interviewQuestions.title: What is `proxy.ts` in Next.js 16 (formerly `middleware.ts`), and what belongs vs. does NOT belong in it?
interviewQuestions.content: Next.js 16 renamed `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts` (exporting `proxy()`) to clarify its role as an explicit network boundary for fast redirects, rewrites, and header/cookie checks—not heavy DB queries.

blocks.text:
• Evolution in Next.js 16: `middleware.ts` was renamed to `proxy.ts` (and `middleware` function to `proxy`), running at the request boundary before routing resolves.
• Good Uses: Locale detection/redirects, A/B rewrite routing, optimistic cookie/JWT presence checks, adding security headers.
• Anti-Pattern: Performing slow database queries or heavy authorization inside `proxy.ts` slows down *every* matched navigation; verify sessions securely in your DAL/Server Components too.

interviewQuestions.title: How do the Node.js Runtime and Edge Runtime compare in Next.js?
interviewQuestions.content: The Node.js Runtime supports full Node APIs and connection pooling for databases, while the Edge Runtime offers ultra-fast cold starts on V8 isolates with restricted Web-standard APIs.

blocks.text:
• Node.js Runtime (Default for Pages/Routes): Full access to `fs`, `crypto`, native drivers, ORMs (Prisma/Drizzle), and persistent TCP DB connections.
• Edge Runtime: Lightweight V8 isolate without Node built-ins (`fs`, `net`). Ideal for geographically distributed header checks or lightweight HTTP proxies, but prone to latency if your database lives in one region.

interviewQuestions.title: How do `error.tsx` and `global-error.tsx` work, and why must both be Client Components?
interviewQuestions.content: `error.tsx` wraps a route segment in a React Error Boundary and exposes a `reset()` function to retry rendering; `global-error.tsx` catches root layout failures and must render its own `<html>` and `<body>`.

blocks.text:
• Why `"use client"`? React Error Boundaries require client-side lifecycle hooks/state and interactive `reset()` buttons.
• Segment Scoping: `error.tsx` does *not* catch errors thrown inside the *same* folder's `layout.tsx`—those bubble to the parent's `error.tsx` or `global-error.tsx`.
• Recovery: Calling `reset()` inside `error.tsx` attempts to re-render the segment (pair with `router.refresh()` to re-fetch server components).

interviewQuestions.title: How do `notFound()`, `unauthorized()`, and `forbidden()` handle HTTP status codes and fallback UI in Next.js 15/16?
interviewQuestions.content: Next.js provides `notFound()` (404) alongside experimental/newer `unauthorized()` (401) and `forbidden()` (403) helpers that abort rendering and display matching `not-found.tsx`, `unauthorized.tsx`, and `forbidden.tsx` files.

blocks.text:
• `notFound()`: Triggers the nearest `not-found.tsx` boundary and returns a 404 HTTP status on SSR (or `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` when streamed).
• `unauthorized()` & `forbidden()`: Enabled via `experimental.authInterrupts: true`, returning clean 401/403 status codes and rendering `unauthorized.tsx` (e.g., login prompt) or `forbidden.tsx` (e.g., missing role UI).

interviewQuestions.title: How does `generateMetadata` create dynamic SEO tags without duplicating database queries?
interviewQuestions.content: `generateMetadata` runs on the server before streaming begins and shares deduplicated `fetch` or React `cache()` calls with the page component.

blocks.text:
• Async Params: Like pages in Next.js 15/16, `generateMetadata({ params })` receives `params` as a Promise and must `await` it.
• Deduplication: Wrapping `getPost(slug)` in React `cache()` (or using `fetch`) ensures calling it in both `generateMetadata` and `Page` executes only one query per request.
• Merging: Child metadata objects shallow-merge with parent layouts (e.g., `title.template` in root layout formats child titles automatically).

interviewQuestions.title: How do `opengraph-image.tsx` and `ImageResponse` generate dynamic social preview cards?
interviewQuestions.content: Exporting a Server route convention `opengraph-image.tsx` using `ImageResponse` (from `next/og`) renders JSX with Flexbox into a PNG/SVG social card and wires `<meta property="og:image">` automatically.

blocks.text:
• Zero Manual Meta Wiring: Placing `opengraph-image.tsx` inside `app/blog/[slug]/` automatically generates the image URL and injects `og:image` tags.
• Satori Constraints: `ImageResponse` converts JSX to SVG/PNG using Flexbox (no CSS Grid) and custom loaded fonts via `fetch` + `ArrayBuffer`.

interviewQuestions.title: How do `generateStaticParams` and `dynamicParams` control static build generation vs. on-demand rendering?
interviewQuestions.content: `generateStaticParams` pre-renders known dynamic route parameters at build time, while `dynamicParams` (`true` vs `false`) decides whether unknown slugs render on demand or return 404.

blocks.text:
• `generateStaticParams`: Returns an array of param objects (e.g., `[{ slug: "intro" }]`) to pre-render at `next build`. With `cacheComponents: true`, returning at least one sample param validates build-time caching.
• `dynamicParams = true` (default): Unlisted slugs render dynamically on first visit and get cached.
• `dynamicParams = false`: Unlisted slugs immediately return 404 without hitting your backend.

interviewQuestions.title: What are Route Segment Config options (`dynamic`, `revalidate`, `maxDuration`), and how do they interact with Next.js 16 `cacheComponents`?
interviewQuestions.content: Segment exports like `dynamic` and `revalidate` configure rendering and timeout behavior per route in traditional App Router, though `cacheComponents: true` replaces `dynamic`/`revalidate` with `"use cache"` and `cacheLife`.

blocks.text:
• Traditional Exports: `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic" | "force-static"`, `export const revalidate = 60`, and `export const maxDuration = 30` (serverless function timeout).
• Next.js 16 Migration Note: When `cacheComponents: true` is enabled, `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` segment configs are disallowed/replaced by explicit `"use cache"`, `cacheLife()`, and `<Suspense>` boundaries (while `maxDuration` remains valid).

interviewQuestions.title: How does the `after()` API from `next/server` run background work without slowing down responses?
interviewQuestions.content: `after(callback)` schedules non-critical tasks—such as analytics, audit logging, or webhook notifications—to run after the HTTP response finishes streaming to the user.

blocks.text:
• Why Not Fire-and-Forget Promises? On serverless platforms, an unawaited `fetch()` or log call gets frozen/killed as soon as the response ends. `after()` signals the runtime (`waitUntil`) to keep the invocation alive until the callback completes.
• Where It Works: Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, and `proxy.ts`/`middleware.ts`.
• Constraint: You cannot set cookies or headers inside `after()` because the response has already been sent.

interviewQuestions.title: What does `await connection()` from `next/server` do in Next.js 15/16?
interviewQuestions.content: `await connection()` explicitly signals Next.js to defer rendering until an incoming user request arrives, replacing the deprecated `unstable_noStore()` helper.

blocks.text:
• Why It Exists: If a Server Component reads `Math.random()`, `new Date()`, or an environment-driven value without calling `cookies()` or `headers()`, Next.js might pre-render it at build time.
• Dynamic Opt-In: Calling `await connection()` marks the boundary as request-time dynamic (wrapping it in `<Suspense>` keeps the outer shell static under PPR).

interviewQuestions.title: Why does `useSearchParams()` require a `<Suspense>` boundary during static builds, and what do `router.refresh()` vs. `Link` prefetch do?
interviewQuestions.content: Reading query parameters with `useSearchParams()` opts the Client Component tree into client-side rendering when statically pre-rendered, requiring a `<Suspense>` boundary to avoid de-opting the whole page.

blocks.text:
• `useSearchParams()` Build Error: During `next build` static generation, search params aren't known; wrapping the component calling `useSearchParams()` in `<Suspense>` lets Next.js pre-render the static shell.
• `router.refresh()`: Re-fetches Server Components for the current route and merges fresh props without losing client React state or scroll position.
• `<Link prefetch>`: Prefetches static shells and shared layouts in viewport automatically (pass `prefetch={false}` on huge lists to save bandwidth).

interviewQuestions.title: How does the Client-side Router Cache work in Next.js 15/16, and how do `staleTimes` or mutations affect it?
interviewQuestions.content: The Client Router Cache stores visited RSC payloads in browser memory for instant back/forward navigation; in Next.js 15+, dynamic page segments have a default `staleTime` of 0 while layouts and prefetched static routes remain cached.

blocks.text:
• What Gets Cached: Shared layouts, loading skeletons (prefetched), and back/forward history entries stay in browser memory across soft navigations.
• Customizing `staleTimes`: Configure `experimental: { staleTimes: { dynamic: 30, static: 180 } }` in `next.config.ts` if your app benefits from short-lived client navigation reuse.
• Invalidating: Server Actions calling `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag`/`updateTag` or client `router.refresh()` clear stale entries in the Client Router Cache.

interviewQuestions.title: How does `next/image` prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) and optimize LCP?
interviewQuestions.content: `next/image` enforces intrinsic aspect ratios to prevent CLS, serves modern AVIF/WebP formats via responsive `srcset`, and supports `preload`/`priority` on the above-the-fold hero image for LCP.

blocks.text:
• CLS Prevention: Always specify `width`/`height` or use `fill` inside a sized `relative` container.
• Responsive Delivery: Provide accurate `sizes` (e.g., `(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 50vw`) with `fill` so mobile users don't download desktop-sized images.
• Security: Remote URLs must be explicitly allowlisted under `images.remotePatterns` in `next.config.ts`.

interviewQuestions.title: How does `next/font` eliminate font-related layout shifts and external network requests?
interviewQuestions.content: `next/font` downloads Google or local fonts at build time, self-hosts them from your domain, and injects CSS `size-adjust` fallback metrics to prevent flash of unstyled text and CLS.

blocks.text:
• Privacy & Performance: Zero runtime requests to `fonts.googleapis.com`—fonts bundle as static assets on the same origin.
• Tailwind v4 Integration: Pass `variable: "--font-sans"` on `next/font/google` and map it in CSS `@theme` or `className`.

interviewQuestions.title: What are the loading strategies of `next/script` (`beforeInteractive`, `afterInteractive`, `lazyOnload`, `worker`)?
interviewQuestions.content: `next/script` schedules third-party scripts cleanly by priority—ranging from critical `beforeInteractive` in root layout to low-priority `lazyOnload` after browser idle.

blocks.text:
• `beforeInteractive`: Only in root `layout.tsx`; blocks/loads before hydration (cookie consent, critical polyfills).
• `afterInteractive` (default): Loads immediately after page becomes interactive (analytics, tag managers).
• `lazyOnload`: Defers until browser idle time (chat widgets, social embeds).

interviewQuestions.title: How do `NEXT_PUBLIC_` environment variables differ from server-only variables in Docker/CI deployments?
interviewQuestions.content: `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables are statically inlined into the client JS bundle at `next build` time, whereas server-only `process.env` variables are read dynamically at runtime.

blocks.text:
• Build-Time Inlining Trap: Changing `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` when starting a pre-built Docker container has no effect—the string was already baked into client chunks during `next build`.
• Runtime Config Pattern: Keep server secrets server-side, or fetch runtime client config via a Server Component passing props / Route Handler if one Docker image must target multiple environments.

interviewQuestions.title: How does `draftMode()` enable secure headless CMS previews on static or cached Next.js pages?
interviewQuestions.content: Calling `(await draftMode()).enable()` inside an authenticated Route Handler sets an HTTP-only bypass cookie that tells Next.js to skip cached/static output and fetch unpublished CMS drafts.

blocks.text:
• Preview Flow: CMS hits `/api/draft?secret=...&slug=/posts/hello` -> Route Handler verifies secret token -> calls `(await draftMode()).enable()` -> redirects to `/posts/hello`.
• Checking Draft State: Server Components check `const { isEnabled } = await draftMode()` to query draft content without caching.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you implement multi-language internationalization (i18n) routing in the Next.js App Router?
interviewQuestions.content: Use a dynamic `[locale]` root segment under `app/[locale]/`, negotiate `Accept-Language` or locale cookies in `proxy.ts`/`middleware.ts`, and load server-side translation dictionaries.

blocks.text:
• Segment Structure: `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` sets `<html lang={locale} dir={locale === "ar" ? "rtl" : "ltr"}>`, and `generateStaticParams` pre-builds supported locales.
• Proxy Redirection: `proxy.ts` inspects URLs missing a locale prefix, checks user cookie or `Accept-Language`, and redirects to `/en/...` or `/ar/...`.

interviewQuestions.title: What is Turbopack in Next.js 15/16, and how does it improve local development and production builds?
interviewQuestions.content: Turbopack is Next.js's Rust-based incremental bundler (default in Next.js 16) that caches computation graphs at function-level granularity for drastically faster HMR and builds.

blocks.text:
• Incremental Architecture: Unlike Webpack, Turbopack tracks fine-grained dependencies so editing one component only re-bundles affected modules regardless of app size.
• Next.js 16 Default: Turbopack became the default bundler for both `dev` and `build` with persistent filesystem caching and cleaner `next.config.ts` configuration.

interviewQuestions.title: How do `instrumentation.ts` (`register()` and `onRequestError()`) work for observability in Next.js?
interviewQuestions.content: `instrumentation.ts` exports `register()` to initialize OpenTelemetry or error SDKs once on server boot and `onRequestError()` to capture unhandled server errors with route context.

blocks.text:
• `register()`: Runs once per server instance startup; check `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === "nodejs"` before loading Node-only telemetry SDKs.
• `onRequestError(err, request, context)`: Captures Server Component, Route Handler, Action, and proxy errors along with `routePath`, `routeType`, and `routerKind`.

interviewQuestions.title: How do programmatic `sitemap.ts`, `robots.ts`, and `manifest.ts` metadata files work in App Router?
interviewQuestions.content: Exporting default functions from `app/sitemap.ts`, `app/robots.ts`, or `app/manifest.ts` dynamically generates standard SEO/PWA endpoints with full TypeScript types.

blocks.text:
• Dynamic Sitemaps: `sitemap.ts` can query your CMS/database and even split huge sites into multiple sitemaps using `generateSitemaps()`.
• Caching: Metadata routes are static by default unless they use dynamic request APIs or `connection()`.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you stream Server-Sent Events (SSE) or AI token chunks from an App Router Route Handler?
interviewQuestions.content: Return a standard Web `Response` backed by a `ReadableStream` with `text/event-stream` headers and `Cache-Control: no-cache`, encoding chunks with `TextEncoder`.

blocks.text:
• Web Streams API: Create `new ReadableStream({ async start(controller) { ... } })`, enqueue `TextEncoder().encode("data: ...\n\n")`, and close on completion or abort via `request.signal`.
• Proxy Buffering Gotcha: Include `"X-Accel-Buffering": "no"` and `"Cache-Control": "no-cache, no-transform"` so reverse proxies don't buffer chunks until stream end.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you wire global React Context providers (Redux, Theme, QueryClient) in App Router without making the entire app a Client Component?
interviewQuestions.content: Create a dedicated `"use client"` `Providers` wrapper component that accepts `{ children }`, and render it inside the Server Component `app/layout.tsx`.

blocks.text:
• Donut Composition: Because `children` is passed as a slot from the Server Component `RootLayout`, nested Server Component pages stay Server Components even though they render inside client Redux/Theme providers.
• SSR Safety for Stores: Create Redux/TanStack Query client instances per request/mount safely (using `useRef` or state initializer) rather than a module-level singleton on the server that could leak state across users.

interviewQuestions.title: When should you use `output: "standalone"` vs. `output: "export"` in `next.config.ts`?
interviewQuestions.content: `output: "standalone"` bundles a minimal Node server and traced `node_modules` for Docker containers, while `output: "export"` emits pure static HTML/CSS/JS files with no SSR server features.

blocks.text:
• `output: "standalone"`: Cuts Docker image sizes dramatically by copying only files traced by `@vercel/nft` into `.next/standalone` (requires manually copying `public/` and `.next/static/` in multi-stage Dockerfiles).
• `output: "export"`: Pure static hosting (S3, GitHub Pages), disabling Server Actions, dynamic Route Handlers, `cookies()`, and runtime SSR.

interviewQuestions.title: Why can you read `cookies()` in Server Components, but only write or delete cookies inside Server Actions, Route Handlers, or `proxy.ts`?
interviewQuestions.content: HTTP response headers are already streaming once a Server Component tree starts rendering, so mutating `Set-Cookie` headers is restricted to Server Actions, Route Handlers, and `proxy.ts`/`middleware.ts`.

blocks.text:
• Streaming Constraint: Server Components can render asynchronously while HTML chunks already flush to the client—too late to attach `Set-Cookie` headers.
• Mutation Places: Call `(await cookies()).set(...)` or `.delete(...)` only in Server Actions, Route Handlers, or `NextResponse.cookies` inside `proxy.ts`.

interviewQuestions.title: Why does calling `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` inside a `"use cache"` scope throw a Next.js error, and how do you structure personalized cached data safely?
interviewQuestions.content: Caching per-request headers/cookies inside a shared `"use cache"` entry would leak one user's private data to others; Next.js blocks it and requires passing non-sensitive cache keys (like `tenantId`) from outside.

blocks.text:
• Security By Design: `"use cache"` stores results globally across requests. Reading `cookies()` inside it would either fail or poison the cache with another user's session.
• Correct Pattern: Read `cookies()` or `auth()` in an uncached dynamic wrapper (inside `<Suspense>`), extract a scoped identifier (e.g., `orgId`), and pass `orgId` as an argument to the `"use cache"` function—or use `"use cache: private"` only when browser/runtime private caching is explicitly intended.

interviewQuestions.title: With `cacheComponents: true` in Next.js 16, why does accessing uncached async data outside `<Suspense>` fail the build?
interviewQuestions.content: With `cacheComponents: true`, Next.js enforces that any runtime/uncached async data either lives inside `"use cache"` or is wrapped in `<Suspense>`, guaranteeing a valid static shell can always be built.

blocks.text:
• Explicit Rendering Boundaries: Without `<Suspense>`, Next.js wouldn't know what fallback HTML to put in the pre-rendered shell while waiting for live DB/cookie work.
• Fix Options:
  1. Wrap the dynamic component in `<Suspense fallback={...}>` so it streams at request time.
  2. Add `"use cache"` + `cacheLife()` if the data is shared and cacheable.

roadmap.title: App Router, File Conventions & Layouts
roadmap.description: Master file-system routing, nested layouts, loading/error boundaries, route groups, and parallel or intercepting routes.

roadmap.title: Server vs. Client Component Architecture
roadmap.description: Design minimal client islands, keep data fetching and secrets on the server, and compose server children inside client wrappers.

versions.title: Turbopack Default, Cache Components & React Compiler

Introduced Cache Components and the use cache directive integrated with Partial Prerendering
Enabled stable React Compiler support for automatic component memoization
Added Turbopack filesystem caching (Beta), updateTag() API, and proxy.ts network boundary

versions.title: Turbopack Builds Alpha & Navigation Hooks

Added client-side instrumentation hook (instrumentation-client.ts) for early telemetry
Added onNavigate and useLinkStatus hooks for granular client routing feedback
Improved TypeScript checking performance and added experimental Rspack community support

versions.title: React 19 Support, Async APIs & Opt-in Caching

Made cookies(), headers(), params, and searchParams asynchronous request APIs
Switched fetch, GET Route Handlers, and client router cache defaults to uncached by default
Introduced the <Form> component with automatic prefetching and client-side navigation

versions.title: Turbopack RC & Build Memory Optimizations

Reduced production build memory usage and improved tree-shaking for large icon/UI libraries
Added experimental staleTimes configuration for client router cache invalidation
