interviewQuestions.content: Implement `LoggerService` (or use `nestjs-pino`) and pass it to `NestFactory.create(AppModule, { bufferLogs: true })` so even bootstrap logs emit structured JSON with request IDs.

blocks.text:
• `bufferLogs: true`: Buffers startup logs until `app.useLogger(app.get(Logger))` swaps in your DI-configured Pino/Winston logger.
• Why Pino: Asynchronous, ultra-low-overhead JSON logging that attaches `req.id`, latency, and user/tenant fields automatically for ELK/Datadog/Grafana Loki.

blocks.code:
const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule, { bufferLogs: true });
app.useLogger(app.get(PinoLoggerService));

interviewQuestions.title: How do Passport Strategies, JWT Guards, and `@Public()` Routes work together in NestJS?
interviewQuestions.content: `@nestjs/passport` wraps Passport strategies (`PassportStrategy(Strategy)`) inside an `AuthGuard('jwt')` that validates tokens, populates `request.user`, and skips routes marked `@Public()`.

blocks.text:
• Pattern: Register `JwtAuthGuard` globally via `APP_GUARD` (secure-by-default!), then opt specific routes (`/auth/login`, `/health`) out using a `@Public()` metadata decorator checked via `Reflector` inside `canActivate()`.
• Strategy `validate(payload)`: Returned object is assigned to `request.user`.

interviewQuestions.title: What are Durable Providers (`durable: true`) and `ContextIdFactory` for Multi-Tenancy?
interviewQuestions.content: Durable providers let you group request-scoped DI sub-trees by tenant ID via a custom `ContextIdFactory` strategy, caching one DI sub-tree per tenant instead of recreating it per request.

blocks.text:
• Problem: In multi-tenant apps, `Scope.REQUEST` recreates tenant DB connections/configs on EVERY HTTP request.
• Durable DI trees (`@Injectable({ scope: Scope.REQUEST, durable: true })`): A custom `ContextIdStrategy` returns `{ payload: { tenantId }, resolve: (info) => (info.isTreeDurable ? tenantSubTreeId : contextId) }`—reusing one cached DI sub-tree per tenant across thousands of requests!

frameworks.title: TanStack Query
frameworks.description: Powerful asynchronous state management for TypeScript and React (formerly React Query) handling caching, synchronization, and server state.
frameworks.aboutDescription: TanStack Query (formerly React Query) is the industry-standard asynchronous state management and server-state library for React and TypeScript applications. Instead of forcing remote API data into manual client-side stores or fragile useEffect hooks, it treats server state as an asynchronous, shared, potentially stale cache with declarative fetching, automatic background refetching, structural sharing, deduplication, mutations, optimistic updates, infinite pagination, Suspense integration, and SSR hydration.

versions.title: Type Inference Refinements & Adapter Sync
changes: Refined TypeScript generic inference across queryOptions, infiniteQueryOptions, and useQueries combine selectors
Improved edge-case cancellation and AbortSignal propagation during rapid query key transitions
Synchronized core observer optimizations across @tanstack/react-query and sibling framework adapters
Hardened hydration and streaming SSR boundary behavior with React 19 concurrent renders

versions.title: Simplified Single-Object API, Suspense & v5 Core
changes: Unified all hooks and QueryClient methods to a single object parameter signature and dropped legacy overloads
Renamed cacheTime to gcTime and standardized pending status naming (isPending / status: 'pending')
Promoted useSuspenseQuery, useSuspenseInfiniteQuery, and useSuspenseQueries to stable first-class hooks
Introduced queryOptions helper for end-to-end type safety across useQuery, prefetchQuery, and getQueryData
Added simplified optimistic updates via useMutation returned variables and maxPages option for infinite queries

versions.title: Rebrand to @tanstack/react-query & Offline Support
changes: Migrated package namespace from react-query to @tanstack/react-query atop a framework-agnostic core
Enforced array-only query keys and introduced networkMode ('online', 'always', 'offlineFirst') for offline workflows
Integrated React 18 useSyncExternalStore for tear-free concurrent rendering and enabled tracked properties by default
Stabilized persistQueryClient plugins and expanded useQueries with object-based query definitions

versions.title: Final v3 Feature Release & Pre-v4 Bridge

Improved React 18 compatibility warnings and StrictMode double-invocation resilience
Delivered bug fixes for infinite query refetchPage predicates and mutation retry edge cases

versions.title: QueryClient Architecture, Selectors & UseQueries
changes: Introduced QueryClient and QueryCache separation to decouple cache management from React components
Added useQueries for dynamic parallel fetching, data selectors (select), and bi-directional infinite queries
Replaced usePaginatedQuery with keepPreviousData and added offline mutation pause/resume persistence
Extracted framework-agnostic query core and shipped built-in React Query Devtools

interviewQuestions.title: What is the difference between Server State and Client State, and why does TanStack Query exist?
interviewQuestions.content: Client state is synchronous and owned by the browser, whereas server state is asynchronous, shared, remotely persisted, and potentially stale—requiring caching, deduplication, and background synchronization.

blocks.text:
• Client State: Synchronous, local to the session (theme, modal open/close, form draft). You own the single source of truth.
• Server State: Persisted remotely (database/API), fetched asynchronously, mutated by other users/processes, and becomes stale the moment it arrives.
• Why TanStack Query? Using Redux or useEffect for API data forces you to hand-write caching, request deduplication, race-condition guards, retries, and background revalidation. TanStack Query is an async state manager purpose-built for that lifecycle.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the role of QueryClient and QueryClientProvider, and why should QueryClient not be created inside a render body?
interviewQuestions.content: QueryClient holds the QueryCache, MutationCache, and default configuration; creating it inside a component render without memoization wipes the entire cache on re-renders.

blocks.text:
• QueryClient Role: It orchestrates QueryCache and MutationCache, manages active observers, deduplicates in-flight requests, and exposes imperative methods (invalidateQueries, prefetchQuery, setQueryData).
• QueryClientProvider: Distributes the QueryClient instance via React Context to all hooks.
• Render Pitfall: Instantiating `new QueryClient()` directly inside a component body recreates a brand-new empty cache on every render. Create it at module scope in SPAs, or inside `useState(() => new QueryClient())` / per-request factory in SSR.

interviewQuestions.title: Explain staleTime vs. gcTime (formerly cacheTime) in TanStack Query v5.
interviewQuestions.content: staleTime controls how long cached data is considered fresh before triggering background refetches; gcTime controls how long unused (inactive) cached data stays in memory before garbage collection.

blocks.text:
• staleTime (default: 0): While data is fresh, components mounting with the same queryKey read immediately from cache without network refetching. Once staleTime elapses, cached data is still shown immediately, but background refetches trigger on mount, window focus, or reconnect.
• gcTime (default: 5 minutes, renamed from cacheTime in v5): The countdown starts only when a query has zero active observers (all subscribed components unmount). When gcTime expires, the cache entry is garbage-collected.
• Rule of Thumb: Always keep `gcTime >= staleTime` so fresh data is not prematurely evicted.

interviewQuestions.title: How do queryKeys work internally, and how does object vs. array ordering affect cache hits?
interviewQuestions.content: queryKeys must be arrays and are serialized deterministically: array element order is significant, whereas plain object property order inside a key is normalized and identical.

blocks.text:
• Array-Only in v4/v5: Every queryKey is an array (`['users', id, filters]`) which enables hierarchical prefix matching during invalidation.
• Deterministic Hashing: TanStack Query serializes keys with `hashKey`, sorting object keys alphabetically. Thus `{ status: 'done', page: 1 }` and `{ page: 1, status: 'done' }` map to the exact same cache entry.
• Array Position Matters: `['todos', 1, 2]` and `['todos', 2, 1]` are distinct cache entries.
• Dependencies Rule: Include every variable used inside `queryFn` in `queryKey` so changing parameters automatically switches cache slots and refetches.

interviewQuestions.title: How do status and fetchStatus differ in TanStack Query v5, and what changed between isPending and isLoading?
interviewQuestions.content: status ('pending' | 'error' | 'success') tracks whether data exists in cache, while fetchStatus ('fetching' | 'paused' | 'idle') tracks whether queryFn is currently running. In v5, isLoading is an alias for isPending && isFetching.

blocks.text:
• Two Orthogonal Axes:
  - `status`: Describes the data (`pending` = no data yet, `error`, `success`).
  - `fetchStatus`: Describes the async `queryFn` (`fetching`, `paused` when offline, `idle`).
• Why Both? A disabled query (`enabled: false`) has `status: 'pending'` (no data) AND `fetchStatus: 'idle'` (not fetching). A background refresh has `status: 'success'` AND `fetchStatus: 'fetching'`.
• v5 Naming Change: `status: 'loading'` was renamed to `'pending'` (`isPending`), and `isLoading` now strictly means `isPending && isFetching` (replacing v4's `isInitialLoading`).

interviewQuestions.title: How does request deduplication work when multiple components mount with the same queryKey simultaneously?
interviewQuestions.content: TanStack Query attaches multiple QueryObservers to a single Query instance in QueryCache, sharing one in-flight Promise and firing only a single network request.

blocks.text:
• Single Query, Multiple Observers: Each `useQuery` call creates a `QueryObserver` subscribed to the `Query` entry identified by the hashed `queryKey`.
• In-Flight Sharing: If a fetch is already in progress (`fetchStatus === 'fetching'`), subsequent components mounting with the same key join the existing Promise instead of firing duplicate HTTP calls.
• Independent Options: Each observer can still specify its own `select` or `notifyOnChangeProps` while sharing the underlying cache entry.

interviewQuestions.title: What is Structural Sharing in TanStack Query, when does it help, and when should you disable it?
interviewQuestions.content: Structural sharing recursively diffs newly fetched JSON data against the previous cache entry and keeps identical object/array references intact to avoid unnecessary React re-renders.

blocks.text:
• How It Works: When a background refetch returns a fresh JSON payload where 9 of 10 items are unchanged, `replaceEqualDeep` reuses the exact old references for unchanged subtrees and only creates new references along modified paths.
• Benefits: Downstream `React.memo`, `useMemo`, and `useEffect` dependencies remain referentially stable.
• When to Disable (`structuralSharing: false`): Disable it for huge payloads (tens of thousands of rows) where deep diffing costs more CPU than rendering, or when `queryFn` returns non-JSON values (like `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, or class instances) unless you pass a custom comparator function.

interviewQuestions.title: How does the select option optimize performance, and why should the selector function be stabilized?
interviewQuestions.content: select transforms or slices cached data per observer and prevents re-renders if the derived result is unchanged, provided the selector reference is stable (module-level or useCallback).

blocks.text:
• Per-Observer Transformation: The raw API response remains intact in `QueryCache` for other components, while each observer transforms only what it needs.
• Render Bailout: TanStack Query compares the previous and next `select` outputs (using structural sharing); if the selected primitive or slice didn't change, the component does not re-render even when unrelated fields in the cache updated.
• Stability Rule: An inline arrow function creates a new function reference on every render, forcing `select` to re-run on every render. Define selectors outside the component or wrap them with `useCallback`.

interviewQuestions.title: What problem does queryOptions() solve in TanStack Query v5?
interviewQuestions.content: queryOptions() binds a queryKey and queryFn together with full TypeScript inference so hooks and imperative QueryClient methods share one type-safe source of truth.

blocks.text:
• Key/Fn Coupling: Defining `queryKey` and `queryFn` separately invites mismatches and forces manual generic annotations on `getQueryData<User>(['users', id])`.
• Tagged Query Keys (`DataTag`): `queryOptions()` attaches the inferred return type directly onto the `queryKey` tuple via a phantom symbol.
• End-to-End Reuse: Passing `userQueryOptions(id)` to `useQuery`, `useSuspenseQuery`, `prefetchQuery`, `ensureQueryData`, and `.queryKey` to `getQueryData` or `setQueryData` automatically infers the exact `TData` and `TError` types.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you implement dependent queries, and when should you prefer skipToken over enabled: false?
interviewQuestions.content: Dependent queries wait on prerequisite data using `enabled: Boolean(dep)` or v5's `skipToken`; `skipToken` eliminates non-null assertions by narrowing types inside `queryFn`.

blocks.text:
• Sequential Fetching: Pass `enabled: !!user?.id` so the second query stays `pending` & `idle` until `user.id` resolves.
• TypeScript Gap with `enabled`: TypeScript cannot narrow `userId` inside `queryFn` based on the sibling `enabled` boolean, often forcing `userId!`.
• `skipToken` Advantage: Assigning `queryFn: userId ? () => fetchProjects(userId) : skipToken` disables execution while letting TypeScript narrow `userId` to `string` cleanly.
• Caveat: Unlike `enabled: false`, queries using `skipToken` cannot be imperatively triggered with `refetch()`.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you execute dynamic parallel queries without violating React's Rules of Hooks, and what does combine do?
interviewQuestions.content: Use `useQueries` to run a variable-length array of queries in parallel, and use v5's `combine` option to aggregate results and limit re-renders.

blocks.text:
• Why Not `ids.map(() => useQuery(...))`? Calling hooks inside loops violates React's Rules of Hooks whenever `ids.length` changes.
• `useQueries`: Accepts a dynamic `queries` array and returns an array of query results executed concurrently.
• v5 `combine` Option: Reduces the array of observer results into a single derived object (e.g., merged data + combined loading flag). Combined with structural sharing, it prevents unnecessary re-renders when intermediate results match.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the key architectural difference between initialData and placeholderData?
interviewQuestions.content: initialData is persisted into the QueryCache (and respects staleTime), whereas placeholderData is observer-only temporary UI data that never writes to the cache.

blocks.text:
• `initialData`: Seeded directly into `QueryCache` as real data (`status: 'success'`). If `staleTime > 0`, it prevents an immediate background fetch. Ideal for SSR seeding or extracting an item from a cached list.
• `placeholderData`: Exists solely at the `QueryObserver` level (`isPlaceholderData: true`) while the real query remains `fetching`. It is never saved to cache and is ideal for `keepPreviousData` during pagination or showing skeleton partial previews.

interviewQuestions.title: Which automatic events trigger background refetches by default, and how does staleTime gate them?
interviewQuestions.content: By default, TanStack Query refetches on component mount, window focus, and network reconnection—but only when the cached data is stale (unless set to 'always').

blocks.text:
• Default Triggers:
  1. New observer mounts (`refetchOnMount`).
  2. Browser window/tab regains focus (`refetchOnWindowFocus`).
  3. Network reconnects (`refetchOnReconnect`).
  4. Periodic timer (`refetchInterval`, disabled by default).
• Role of `staleTime`: If data is still fresh, none of the first three triggers fire a request.
• Special Values: Setting `refetchOnMount: 'always'` forces a refetch regardless of `staleTime`, whereas `false` disables the trigger completely.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you configure conditional polling, and how does TanStack Query handle hidden browser tabs?
interviewQuestions.content: Pass a callback to `refetchInterval` returning milliseconds or `false` to stop polling dynamically; by default, polling pauses automatically when the tab is backgrounded.

blocks.text:
• Dynamic `refetchInterval`: In v5, the callback receives the `Query` object (`query.state.data`), allowing you to stop polling once a background job finishes (`return false`).
• Tab Visibility Optimization: `refetchIntervalInBackground` defaults to `false`, pausing timers when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` to save battery and server load.
• Error Backoff: Consider checking `query.state.error` inside the callback to pause or slow down polling on server failures.

interviewQuestions.title: How does automatic query cancellation work with AbortSignal, and when does TanStack Query trigger it?
interviewQuestions.content: TanStack Query passes an AbortSignal in QueryFunctionContext; forwarding it to fetch/axios aborts in-flight HTTP requests when all observers unmount or queryClient.cancelQueries() is called.

blocks.text:
• Context `signal`: Every `queryFn` receives `{ queryKey, signal, meta }`.
• When It Aborts:
  1. A component unmounts (or `queryKey` changes, e.g., fast search typing) before the promise resolves AND the `signal` was consumed by your code.
  2. You explicitly call `queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey })` (common inside `onMutate`).
• Important Note: Calling `fetch(url, { signal })` cancels the browser request cleanly and avoids wasted bandwidth and stale responses.

interviewQuestions.title: Why is checking response.ok critical when using native fetch() with TanStack Query?
interviewQuestions.content: Native fetch() only rejects on network failures and resolves on HTTP 404/500 responses; without throwing on `!res.ok`, TanStack Query treats error responses as successful data.

blocks.text:
• Fetch Behavior vs. Axios: Axios automatically rejects Promises on non-2xx statuses, whereas `fetch()` resolves normally on HTTP 400, 401, 404, or 500.
• Impact in TanStack Query: If `queryFn` does not throw, TanStack Query sets `status: 'success'`, caches the error JSON as valid `data`, and never triggers `retry` or `error` boundaries.
• Best Practice: Wrap `fetch` in a tiny helper that throws a typed `HttpError(res.status, body)` whenever `!res.ok`.

interviewQuestions.title: Compare mutate() vs. mutateAsync() in useMutation, including error handling and callback execution.
interviewQuestions.content: mutate() catches errors internally and routes them to mutation state and callbacks, while mutateAsync() returns a raw Promise that rejects on failure and requires try/catch.

blocks.text:
• `mutate`: Synchronous trigger that never throws an unhandled rejection. Handle outcomes via `useMutation` callbacks (`onSuccess`, `onError`, `onSettled`) or per-call options `mutate(vars, { onSuccess })`.
• `mutateAsync`: Returns a `Promise<TData>`, useful when chaining sequential awaits or integrating with form libraries expecting a Promise. Always wrap in `try/catch`.
• Callback Pitfall: Callbacks on `useMutation({ onSuccess })` run even if the component unmounts, whereas callbacks passed to `mutate(vars, { onSuccess })` only run if the component is still mounted.

interviewQuestions.title: Where should cache invalidation live vs. UI redirects in useMutation, and why return the invalidateQueries promise?
interviewQuestions.content: Put cache invalidation inside useMutation's callbacks (survives unmount) and UI side effects inside mutate()'s callbacks; returning the invalidateQueries promise keeps isPending true until data refreshes.

blocks.text:
• Lifecycle Separation:
  - `useMutation({ onSuccess })`: Runs regardless of whether the triggering component is still mounted—ideal for `invalidateQueries` or `setQueryData`.
  - `mutate(vars, { onSuccess })`: Skipped if the component unmounts mid-flight—ideal for `navigate()`, closing modals, or local toast messages.
• Awaiting Invalidation: Returning `queryClient.invalidateQueries(...)` from `useMutation`'s `onSuccess` makes the mutation stay `isPending` until the invalidated queries finish refetching.

interviewQuestions.title: Compare invalidateQueries, refetchQueries, resetQueries, and setQueryData.
interviewQuestions.content: invalidateQueries marks queries stale and refetches active ones; refetchQueries forces fetching; resetQueries restores initial/empty state; setQueryData writes synchronously to cache.

blocks.text:
• `invalidateQueries`: Marks matching queries stale (`isStale = true`) and refetches active ones in the background. Inactive queries will refetch next time they mount.
• `refetchQueries`: Immediately triggers fetching for matching queries (defaults to all, or filter with `type: 'active'`).
• `resetQueries`: Resets cached data back to `initialData` (or `undefined`) before refetching active observers—helpful on logout or full filter resets.
• `setQueryData`: Synchronously and immutably updates cached data with zero network calls; never mutate the `old` reference in place.

interviewQuestions.title: How does QueryFilters matching work in TanStack Query (prefix vs. exact vs. predicate)?
interviewQuestions.content: QueryClient methods match queryKeys by prefix by default; `exact: true` restricts to identical keys, and `predicate` runs custom filtering logic across Query instances.

blocks.text:
• Prefix Matching (Default): `{ queryKey: ['todos'] }` matches `['todos']`, `['todos', 'list']`, and `['todos', { done: true }]`.
• `exact: true`: Matches only `['todos']` with identical length and values.
• `predicate`: Receives the full `Query` instance (`queryKey`, `state`, `meta`), letting you invalidate e.g. all queries older than a timestamp or matching nested conditions.
• Additional Filters: `type: 'active' | 'inactive' | 'all'` and `stale: true | false` narrow which cached entries are targeted.

interviewQuestions.title: Compare the two optimistic update patterns in TanStack Query v5: UI-level variables vs. Cache-level onMutate rollback.
interviewQuestions.content: UI-level optimistic updates render `mutation.variables` directly while `isPending` (zero cache rollback code), while cache-level updates write to QueryCache in `onMutate` and restore snapshots in `onError`.

blocks.text:
• Pattern 1 — UI-Level (v5 simplified): Keep `useMutation` simple with `onSettled: () => invalidateQueries(...)`, then render `isPending ? [...todos, variables] : todos` in the single component displaying the mutation. No `onMutate` or manual rollback needed.
• Pattern 2 — Cache-Level (`onMutate`): Required when multiple components across the tree must reflect the optimistic change immediately.
  1. `await cancelQueries` to prevent stale in-flight refetches from overwriting the optimistic write.
  2. Snapshot `getQueryData` and return it as context.
  3. Roll back in `onError` using `context`, and always `invalidateQueries` in `onSettled`.

interviewQuestions.title: What happens if a user triggers two rapid optimistic mutations on the same list, and how do you prevent flickering?
interviewQuestions.content: If the first mutation's `onSettled` invalidates the list before the second mutation finishes on the server, the refetch can overwrite the second optimistic item; guard invalidation with `queryClient.isMutating()`.

blocks.text:
• The Concurrency Bug: User toggles Todo A then immediately toggles Todo B. Mutation A finishes first and calls `invalidateQueries(['todos'])`. Because Mutation B hasn't committed on the server yet, the refetch returns stale state for B, reverting B's optimistic toggle temporarily.
• Fix: Tag related mutations with `mutationKey: ['todos']` and inside `onSettled`, only invalidate when `queryClient.isMutating({ mutationKey: ['todos'] }) === 1` (or `<= 1` depending on phase), ensuring the final settled mutation triggers the authoritative refetch.

interviewQuestions.title: When should you use standard paginated useQuery vs. useInfiniteQuery, and what changed in v5 for useInfiniteQuery?
interviewQuestions.content: Use `useQuery` with `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` for numbered page navigation, and `useInfiniteQuery` for additive feeds ('Load More' / infinite scroll); v5 requires `initialPageParam`.

blocks.text:
• Standard Pagination (`useQuery`): Each page has its own `['items', page]` cache key. Keeping previous data avoids layout jumps between page clicks.
• Infinite Queries (`useInfiniteQuery`): Accumulates all fetched pages in `data.pages` and `data.pageParams` under one cache entry.
• v5 Changes:
  1. `initialPageParam` is now mandatory (removed implicit `undefined`).
  2. `maxPages` lets you cap memory by sliding a window of pages.
  3. `getPreviousPageParam` works seamlessly with `maxPages` for bi-directional scrolling.

interviewQuestions.title: How does refetching work for useInfiniteQuery, and how does maxPages control memory?
interviewQuestions.content: Invalidating an infinite query sequentially refetches every currently loaded page from page 1 using stored pageParams; `maxPages` bounds the stored page window and evicts distant pages.

blocks.text:
• Sequential Page Refetch: Unlike regular queries, refetching an infinite query with 10 loaded pages sequentially re-runs `queryFn` for all 10 stored `pageParams` (so mutations don't leave holes). Note: `refetchPage` was removed in v5 in favor of `maxPages`.
• `maxPages`: Caps the number of pages stored in `data.pages`. Fetching page 6 when `maxPages: 5` drops page 1; scrolling back up uses `getPreviousPageParam` and `fetchPreviousPage` to reload earlier pages on demand.

interviewQuestions.title: How does useSuspenseQuery differ from useQuery, and what waterfall pitfall should you avoid with Suspense?
interviewQuestions.content: useSuspenseQuery suspends rendering until resolved, throws errors to Error Boundaries, and guarantees non-undefined `data`; however, two consecutive useSuspenseQuery calls in one component create a request waterfall.

blocks.text:
• Key Differences from `useQuery`:
  1. `data` is never `undefined`—loading states move to `<Suspense>` and errors move to `<ErrorBoundary>`.
  2. `enabled` and `placeholderData` are disallowed (use conditional rendering or `useSuspenseQueries`).
• Waterfall Trap: Calling `useSuspenseQuery(A)` then `useSuspenseQuery(B)` in the same component suspends on A before B even starts!
• Solutions: Batch independent queries with `useSuspenseQueries`, or prefetch both queries ahead of render (e.g., in a route loader or parent component).

interviewQuestions.title: Why do you need QueryErrorResetBoundary when resetting an ErrorBoundary around failing queries?
interviewQuestions.content: Resetting a React ErrorBoundary alone only re-renders the failing child, which immediately reads the same cached error; QueryErrorResetBoundary clears query error states so they refetch on retry.

blocks.text:
• The Retry Loop Problem: When `throwOnError: true` or `useSuspenseQuery` throws, the error remains stored in `QueryCache`. Clicking 'Retry' inside `ErrorBoundary` re-renders the component, sees the same cached error, and throws again immediately.
• Solution: `QueryErrorResetBoundary` (or `useQueryErrorResetBoundary().reset`) marks queries inside that boundary to reset and refetch when `ErrorBoundary`'s `onReset` callback executes.

interviewQuestions.title: How do dehydrate() and HydrationBoundary work in SSR (e.g., Next.js App Router), and why create QueryClient per request on the server?
interviewQuestions.content: dehydrate() serializes QueryCache entries into JSON-safe dehydrated state for HydrationBoundary on the client; creating one QueryClient per server request prevents cross-user data leaks.

blocks.text:
• Request Isolation Security: A module-level singleton `QueryClient` on a Node.js server would share User A's private data with User B! Always instantiate a fresh `QueryClient` per SSR request.
• Client Singleton vs. State: On the client, keep one `QueryClient` across the browser session (via `useState` or a browser-only singleton gated by `isServer`).
• `dehydrate` + `HydrationBoundary`: `dehydrate(serverClient)` extracts successful (and optionally pending in v5.40+) queries into props; `HydrationBoundary` merges them into the browser `QueryClient` before client hooks read them.

interviewQuestions.title: How can TanStack Query v5 stream in-flight server queries to the client without awaiting prefetchQuery on the server?
interviewQuestions.content: By configuring `shouldDehydrateQuery` to include `status === 'pending'`, Next.js Server Components can fire `prefetchQuery` without `await` and stream the Promise resolution directly into HydrationBoundary.

blocks.text:
• Traditional Blocking SSR: `await queryClient.prefetchQuery(...)` delays the HTML shell until the slow API finishes.
• Streaming Pending Queries: In Next.js App Router, omit `await` on `queryClient.prefetchQuery(...)` and allow `status === 'pending'` inside `shouldDehydrateQuery`.
• Result: The server sends the shell immediately, keeps the promise alive, and streams the resolved query payload to the client `HydrationBoundary` seamlessly.

interviewQuestions.title: Compare prefetchQuery, fetchQuery, and ensureQueryData.
interviewQuestions.content: prefetchQuery never throws and returns void; fetchQuery returns data and throws on error when stale; ensureQueryData returns cached data immediately if present (even if stale unless revalidateIfStale is set) or fetches it.

blocks.text:
• `prefetchQuery`: Best for hover/intent prefetching. Resolves to `void` and catches errors internally so unhandled rejections don't crash UI.
• `fetchQuery`: Checks `staleTime`; if stale or missing, fetches and returns `TData` or throws on error.
• `ensureQueryData`: Ideal for route loaders and server utilities—returns existing cached `TData` synchronously if present (or fetches if missing), guaranteeing data availability.

interviewQuestions.title: Explain the three networkMode options ('online', 'always', 'offlineFirst') and how they interact with fetchStatus.
interviewQuestions.content: 'online' (default) pauses queries/mutations when offline; 'always' ignores network status (useful for AsyncStorage/IndexedDB); 'offlineFirst' runs the first request and pauses retries until reconnected.

blocks.text:
• `'online'` (Default): If the browser is offline, `fetchStatus` switches to `'paused'`, delaying execution and retries until the `online` event fires.
• `'always'`: Executes regardless of `navigator.onLine`—essential when `queryFn` reads IndexedDB, Electron IPC, or localhost services.
• `'offlineFirst'`: Fires once even if `navigator.onLine` is unreliable (allowing Service Worker cache hits), and only pauses subsequent retries when offline.

interviewQuestions.title: How does TanStack Query retry failed queries by default, and how should you customize retry for 4xx client errors?
interviewQuestions.content: Queries retry 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s capped at 30s), while mutations default to 0 retries; pass a function to `retry` to skip retrying 401/403/404 errors.

blocks.text:
• Default Behavior: `useQuery` retries 3 times on the client (0 on SSR to avoid slowing server responses), using `Math.min(1000 * 2 ** attemptIndex, 30000)`. `useMutation` does NOT retry by default (`retry: 0`).
• Skipping Deterministic Errors: Retrying a 404 Not Found or 401 Unauthorized wastes 7+ seconds before showing an error UI. Inspect `error.status` inside `retry(failureCount, error)` and return `false` immediately for client 4xx errors.

interviewQuestions.title: Why is QueryCache.onError preferred over component-level useEffect for global error toasts, and how does `meta` help?
interviewQuestions.content: QueryCache({ onError }) fires once per failed query fetch rather than once per subscribed component observer, and `query.meta` lets individual queries attach custom context.

blocks.text:
• The Multi-Observer Toast Bug: Putting `useEffect(() => { if (error) toast(...) }, [error])` inside a shared hook fires N duplicate toasts if N components mount that hook.
• Centralized `QueryCache` / `MutationCache`: Global `onError` callbacks fire exactly once per failed execution.
• Contextual `meta`: Pass `meta: { errorMessage: 'Failed to load billing' }` on specific queries so the global handler can customize alerts or skip silenced queries.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you globally customize the default `error` type across all hooks in TanStack Query v5?
interviewQuestions.content: Augment the `Register` interface inside `@tanstack/react-query` (`defaultError: ApiError`) via TypeScript declaration merging so every query and mutation infers your custom error class.

blocks.text:
• Default `Error` Type: In v5, `TError` defaults to `Error` (changed from `unknown` in v4).
• Module Augmentation: Declaring `interface Register { defaultError: ApiError }` in a `.d.ts` or shared TS file overrides the default globally.
• Benefit: `error.status` is immediately typed in every `useQuery`, `useMutation`, and `QueryCache` callback without repeating generics everywhere.

interviewQuestions.title: What are the essential best practices for unit/integration testing components that use TanStack Query?
interviewQuestions.content: Create a fresh isolated QueryClient per test, set `retry: false` so error tests fail fast without timeouts, and mock HTTP at the network boundary (e.g., MSW) rather than mocking `useQuery` itself.

blocks.text:
• Isolated `QueryClient` per Test: Prevents cache leakage between tests.
• `retry: false`: By default, a failing query retries 3 times (~7 seconds), causing test timeouts before error states appear.
• `gcTime: Infinity` in Jest/Vitest: Prevents 'Jest did not exit one second after test run' / open timer warnings.
• Mock Network, Not Hooks: Use MSW or mock fetchers so you test real caching, keys, and state transitions.

interviewQuestions.title: How do tracked properties and `notifyOnChangeProps` minimize re-renders in TanStack Query?
interviewQuestions.content: By default, TanStack Query tracks which result properties your component destructures (`data`, `isFetching`, `error`) via getters and only re-renders when those accessed properties change.

blocks.text:
• Tracked Queries (Default since v4): The object returned from `useQuery` defines property getters. If your component only reads `data`, background refetches that flip `isFetching` from `false` to `true` and back will NOT trigger re-renders unless `data` actually changed.
• Pitfall: Spreading the entire result (`const query = useQuery(...); console.log({ ...query })`) accesses every getter and opts out of tracking.
• `notifyOnChangeProps: 'all'` disables tracking if you intentionally need updates on every state transition.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you persist QueryCache across browser reloads, and what must `gcTime` be set to?
interviewQuestions.content: Use `PersistQueryClientProvider` with a storage persister (localStorage/IndexedDB), and ensure `gcTime` is at least equal to `maxAge` (e.g., 24 hours) so persisted entries aren't garbage-collected right after restoration.

blocks.text:
• Persistence Packages: `@tanstack/react-query-persist-client` plus `@tanstack/query-sync-storage-persister` (localStorage) or `@tanstack/query-async-storage-persister` (IndexedDB/AsyncStorage).
• Critical `gcTime` Gotcha: The default `gcTime` is 5 minutes. If a user returns 2 hours later, restored queries older than 5 minutes get garbage-collected immediately unless `gcTime >= maxAge`!
• Cache Busting: Pass `buster: APP_VERSION` to `persistOptions` to discard incompatible persisted schemas on new deployments.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the safest way to clear TanStack Query state on user logout or account switching?
interviewQuestions.content: Cancel in-flight queries and call `queryClient.clear()` (plus clear any storage persisters) on logout so private data from the previous user never leaks to the next session.

blocks.text:
• Why `invalidateQueries` Isn't Enough: `invalidateQueries()` keeps stale private data visible in memory while refetching (which may fail with 401 and leave stale data around) and retains inactive cache entries.
• Safe Sequence:
  1. `await queryClient.cancelQueries()` so in-flight responses for User A don't land in cache after logout.
  2. `queryClient.clear()` to purge `QueryCache` and `MutationCache` completely.
  3. If using persistence, also remove the persisted storage key.

interviewQuestions.title: How does v5's useMutationState() improve on useIsMutating() for cross-component mutation tracking?
interviewQuestions.content: useIsMutating() only returns a numeric count of active mutations, whereas useMutationState() subscribes to matching MutationCache entries and lets you select their variables, data, or errors anywhere in the tree.

blocks.text:
• `useIsMutating`: Great for a global spinner (`isMutating > 0`).
• `useMutationState` (New in v5): Subscribes to `MutationCache` using `filters` (`mutationKey`, `status`, `exact`) and `select`.
• Killer Use Case: A mutation triggered inside a modal or row item can be observed in a completely separate sibling list or status bar to render optimistic items or upload progress without lifting state or prop drilling.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you build a global background-fetching indicator while excluding noisy polling queries?
interviewQuestions.content: Use `useIsFetching(filters)` with a `queryKey` prefix or `predicate` function to exclude periodic background polls from triggering your global loading bar.

blocks.text:
• `useIsFetching()`: Without arguments, returns the total count of currently fetching queries across the whole `QueryClient`.
• Filtering Noise: Passing a `predicate` (or `queryKey`) lets you ignore silent polling queries like `['notifications']` or `['heartbeat']` so users aren't distracted by a flickering top progress bar every few seconds.

interviewQuestions.title: How do focusManager and onlineManager work, and how do you integrate them in non-browser environments like React Native?
interviewQuestions.content: focusManager and onlineManager abstract window focus and network connectivity events; in React Native, override their event listeners with AppState and NetInfo.

blocks.text:
• Browser Defaults: In web browsers, `focusManager` listens to `visibilitychange` and `onlineManager` listens to `online`/`offline` window events.
• Non-DOM Platforms: React Native lacks `window.visibilitychange`. Wiring `AppState` to `focusManager.setEventListener` and `@react-native-community/netinfo` to `onlineManager.setEventListener` restores automatic background refetches and offline mutation pausing.

interviewQuestions.title: Summarize the major breaking changes when migrating from TanStack Query v4 to v5.
interviewQuestions.content: v5 mandates a single-object API, removes `onSuccess`/`onError`/`onSettled` from `useQuery`, renames `cacheTime` to `gcTime`, replaces `loading` with `pending`, and replaces `keepPreviousData` with `placeholderData`.

blocks.text:
• Top v4 -> v5 Breaking Changes:
  1. Single object signature only (`useQuery({ queryKey, queryFn })`).
  2. Removed `onSuccess`/`onError`/`onSettled` on `useQuery` (caused duplicate calls per observer and stale closure bugs; move to `QueryCache` or `useMutation`).
  3. `cacheTime` -> `gcTime`, `status: 'loading'` -> `'pending'` (`isPending`), `isInitialLoading` -> `isLoading`.
  4. `useErrorBoundary` -> `throwOnError`.
  5. `keepPreviousData: true` -> `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`.
  6. `useInfiniteQuery` requires `initialPageParam`.

interviewQuestions.title: Why were onSuccess, onError, and onSettled callbacks removed from useQuery in v5?
interviewQuestions.content: They fired once per component observer rather than once per fetch, didn't fire when reading cached data, and encouraged anti-patterns like copying server state into `useState`.

blocks.text:
• Three Core Reasons:
  1. Multiple Observers = Multiple Executions: Two components using the same hook fired `onSuccess` twice for one HTTP call.
  2. Cache Hits Skipped It: If data was already cached and fresh, `onSuccess` wouldn't run, breaking imperative assumptions.
  3. State Duplication Anti-Pattern: Developers used `onSuccess: (d) => setLocalState(d)` which broke synchronization on background refetches.
• Replacements: Derive values during render, use `select`, pass `values` prop to form libraries (e.g., React Hook Form), or use `QueryCache` callbacks for global alerts.

interviewQuestions.title: How should you integrate WebSockets or Server-Sent Events (SSE) with TanStack Query?
interviewQuestions.content: Keep initial fetching in `useQuery` with a high `staleTime`, and inside a WebSocket listener either push full payloads via `setQueryData` or send lightweight invalidation signals via `invalidateQueries`.

blocks.text:
• Two Integration Strategies:
  1. Event-Driven Invalidation (Simplest & Most Resilient): Server pushes `{ type: 'invalidate', entity: 'orders' }`; client calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['orders'] })`.
  2. Direct Cache Patching: Server pushes the full updated object; client merges it with `queryClient.setQueryData` and sets `staleTime: Infinity` on the query so redundant HTTP polls don't fire.
• Reconnection Safety: On WebSocket reconnect after a drop, call `invalidateQueries` to catch up on missed events.

interviewQuestions.title: What is the idiomatic way to build a debounced search input with TanStack Query?
interviewQuestions.content: Debounce the input value before placing it into `queryKey`, pass `signal` for cancellation, gate short inputs with `enabled`, and optionally preserve prior results with `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`.

blocks.text:
• Debounce State, Not `queryFn`: Debouncing inside `queryFn` breaks TanStack Query's Promise tracking and key-based caching. Instead, store a debounced state (`debouncedQuery`) and put it in `queryKey`.
• Bonus Optimizations:
  - Cached results for previously typed terms appear instantaneously.
  - Passing `signal` aborts superseded requests if the user types again after 300ms.
  - `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` avoids flashing an empty list between keystrokes.

interviewQuestions.title: How do you seed a detail query from an existing list cache using `initialData` and `initialDataUpdatedAt`?
interviewQuestions.content: Pass a function to `initialData` that searches the list cache, and pair it with `initialDataUpdatedAt` from `getQueryState` so `staleTime` is evaluated against when the list was actually fetched.

blocks.text:
• Instant Detail Transitions: When clicking a row in a cached list, the detail page renders immediately without a spinner.
• Why `initialDataUpdatedAt` Matters: Without it, TanStack Query assumes `initialData` was created at `Date.now()`! If `staleTime` is 5 minutes, it would skip fetching full details even if the list cache is 4 minutes old.
• Passing `getQueryState(['posts'])?.dataUpdatedAt` accurately reflects the age of the seeded data.

interviewQuestions.title: Design a scalable Query Key Factory and explain why hierarchical keys make invalidation surgical.
interviewQuestions.content: A Query Key Factory centralizes `as const` key hierarchies from broad scopes (`all`, `lists`) to specific entries (`detail(id)`), preventing typos and enabling granular prefix invalidation.

blocks.text:
• Granular Invalidation Levels:
  - `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: orderKeys.all })`: Invalidates every order list AND detail.
  - `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: orderKeys.lists() })`: Invalidates all filtered lists while preserving cached individual details.
  - `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: orderKeys.detail('123') })`: Targets only one order.
• Tip: Combine with `queryOptions()` in v5 for full type-safe factories.

interviewQuestions.title: When should you use `staleTime: Infinity`, and how does it still allow manual refreshes?
interviewQuestions.content: `staleTime: Infinity` prevents automatic background refetches (mount, focus, reconnect) for static/rarely changing data, while `invalidateQueries()` or `refetch()` can still refresh it explicitly.

blocks.text:
• Ideal Use Cases: Country lists, static enums, feature-flag snapshots, or WebSocket-pushed caches where HTTP polling isn't desired.
• Does `Infinity` Freeze Forever? No! Calling `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['countries'] })` explicitly marks the entry stale and refetches it, and `refetch()` always bypasses `staleTime`.

interviewQuestions.title: Why does hydrated SSR data immediately refetch on client mount if `staleTime` stays at its default `0`?
interviewQuestions.content: With `staleTime: 0`, hydrated SSR data is immediately considered stale as soon as the client component mounts, triggering a redundant client-side HTTP request right after hydration.

blocks.text:
• The Double-Fetch Trap: The server renders HTML using prefetched data at T=0ms. At T=150ms, React hydrates on the client and mounts `useQuery`. Because `staleTime` defaults to `0`, TanStack Query sees `dataUpdatedAt < now` and fires a duplicate request!
• Fix: Set a positive default `staleTime` (e.g., `60 * 1000`) on your SSR `QueryClient` factory so the client trusts server-hydrated data for the first minute.

interviewQuestions.title: What can you inspect with ReactQueryDevtools, and is it automatically tree-shaken in production builds?
interviewQuestions.content: ReactQueryDevtools inspects live query statuses (fresh, fetching, stale, inactive), timelines, observer counts, and manual refetch/invalidate triggers; by default it is excluded from production bundles.

blocks.text:
• Inspection Capabilities: View exact serialized `queryKey`s, `dataUpdatedAt` timestamps, raw JSON cache payloads, active observer counts, and manually simulate Error, Loading, Invalidate, or Reset states.
• Bundle Size: `@tanstack/react-query-devtools` automatically compiles to `null` when `NODE_ENV === 'production'`. If you want it in production for staff debugging, use `@tanstack/react-query-devtools/production` with `React.lazy`.

interviewQuestions.title: How does TanStack Query compare to SWR and RTK Query when choosing a data-fetching layer?
interviewQuestions.content: TanStack Query offers richer cache primitives (mutations, optimistic rollbacks, infinite maxPages, Devtools, framework adapters) than SWR and avoids Redux coupling unlike RTK Query.

blocks.text:
• vs. SWR: SWR is minimal and lightweight for simple GET revalidation, whereas TanStack Query provides built-in `gcTime`, mutation tracking (`useMutationState`), `maxPages` bi-directional infinite queries, offline persistence, and `queryOptions`.
• vs. RTK Query: RTK Query excels if your app is already standardized on Redux Toolkit and OpenAPI codegen inside one Redux store. TanStack Query is transport-agnostic (REST, GraphQL, RPC, IndexedDB) and requires zero Redux boilerplate.

insights.title: 01. Bootstrapping QueryClient and QueryClientProvider
insights.content: Wrap your application root once with QueryClientProvider and a stable QueryClient instance.

blocks.text:
• `QueryClient` owns the in-memory `QueryCache` and `MutationCache`.
• Defining `queryClient` outside the component body ensures the cache persists across re-renders in a client SPA.

insights.title: 02. Enabling React Query Devtools in Development
insights.content: Mount ReactQueryDevtools inside QueryClientProvider to inspect live cache states without affecting production bundles.

blocks.text:
• Inspect active, fresh, stale, fetching, and inactive queries in real time.
• Trigger manual refetches, invalidations, or simulated errors directly from the panel.

insights.title: 03. Your First Declarative useQuery Hook
insights.content: useQuery requires a single options object with `queryKey` and `queryFn` in TanStack Query v5.

blocks.text:
• `queryKey` uniquely identifies the cache slot.
• `queryFn` returns a Promise resolving to the data (or throwing an Error).
• Check `isPending` and `isError` cleanly before rendering `data`.

insights.title: 04. Throwing Explicitly on Non-OK fetch() Responses
insights.content: Always check `res.ok` inside fetch wrappers because native `fetch` resolves normally on HTTP 4xx/5xx responses.

blocks.text:
• Unlike Axios, `fetch()` only rejects on network disconnection.
• Throwing on `!res.ok` ensures TanStack Query enters `status: 'error'` and applies retry rules.

insights.title: 05. Setting Global Default Options on QueryClient
insights.content: Configure application-wide caching and retry defaults once in `new QueryClient({ defaultOptions })`.

blocks.text:
• Individual `useQuery` hooks inherit these defaults and can override any field locally.
• Setting a global `staleTime` (e.g., 30s) immediately eliminates bursty duplicate refetches.

insights.title: 06. Deterministic Query Key Hashing Rules
insights.content: Plain object keys inside a `queryKey` are order-independent, whereas array element order is strictly significant.

blocks.text:
• TanStack Query sorts plain object keys during serialization so `{ a: 1, b: 2 }` equals `{ b: 2, a: 1 }`.
• Top-level array positions represent hierarchy and must stay consistent.

insights.title: 07. Building a Hierarchical Query Key Factory
insights.content: Centralize key arrays in a factory object with `as const` tuples to prevent key typos and simplify invalidation.

blocks.text:
• Broad invalidations target `productKeys.all` or `productKeys.lists()`.
• Surgical invalidations target `productKeys.detail(id)`.

insights.title: 08. Treating queryKey Like a Reactive Dependency Array
insights.content: Include every parameter used by `queryFn` inside `queryKey` so changing inputs automatically trigger a fresh fetch.

blocks.text:
• Whenever any value in `queryKey` changes, TanStack Query switches to that key's cache slot.
• Think of `queryKey` as the dependency array for your remote data.

insights.title: 09. Sharing Type-Safe Definitions with queryOptions()
insights.content: Use v5's `queryOptions()` helper to share identical query definitions with full type inference across hooks and QueryClient.

blocks.text:
• `queryOptions` is a runtime identity function with compile-time `DataTag` magic.
• `queryClient.getQueryData(taskOptions('t-1').queryKey)` automatically infers `Task | undefined`.

insights.title: 10. Distinguishing Initial Load (isPending) from Background Sync (isFetching)
insights.content: Show skeletons only on `isPending` (no cached data yet) and subtle indicators on `isFetching` during background refreshes.

blocks.text:
• `isPending` is true only when there is no cached data.
• `isFetching` is true whenever `queryFn` is executing, including background refreshes.

insights.title: 11. Detecting Offline Paused Queries via fetchStatus
insights.content: Check `fetchStatus === 'paused'` to display helpful offline notices instead of endless loading spinners.

blocks.text:
• When offline under default `networkMode: 'online'`, `status` stays `'pending'` while `fetchStatus` becomes `'paused'`.
• Once online again, the query resumes automatically.

insights.title: 12. Reading queryKey Directly from QueryFunctionContext
insights.content: Receive `{ queryKey, signal, meta }` inside `queryFn` instead of duplicating closures over parameters.

blocks.text:
• Extracting parameters from `queryKey` ensures `queryKey` and `queryFn` can never drift out of sync.
• Works seamlessly with reusable fetcher functions.

insights.title: 13. Wrapping Queries in Custom Domain Hooks
insights.content: Encapsulate each `useQuery` inside a domain hook like `useCurrentUser()` so multiple components share one key and contract.

blocks.text:
• Eliminates prop drilling or Redux boilerplate for shared server entities.
• Mounting `useCurrentUser()` in Navbar, Sidebar, and Profile triggers only one HTTP request.

insights.title: 14. Letting TypeScript Infer Query Types from queryFn
insights.content: Type your `queryFn` return Promise rather than passing explicit generics to `useQuery<...>`.

blocks.text:
• Passing explicit generics to `useQuery<Post[], Error>` overrides inference and breaks options like `select`.
• Strongly typing `queryFn` automatically propagates types to `data`, `select`, and `placeholderData`.

insights.title: 15. Registering a Custom Global Error Type in TypeScript
insights.content: Augment `@tanstack/react-query`'s `Register` interface to replace `Error` with your custom `HttpError` globally.

blocks.text:
• Every `error` property from `useQuery` and `useMutation` immediately exposes `error.status`.
• Removes repetitive `useQuery<Data, HttpError>` annotations.

insights.title: 16. Skipping Retries for Deterministic 4xx Client Errors
insights.content: Return `false` from `retry` on 400/401/403/404 responses so users see error feedback immediately.

blocks.text:
• Default retries (3 attempts with exponential backoff) only make sense for transient 5xx or network blips.
• Failing fast on 404/401 improves perceived responsiveness.

insights.title: 17. Customizing Exponential Backoff with retryDelay
insights.content: Control wait times between retry attempts using `retryDelay(attemptIndex, error)`.

blocks.text:
• Default backoff doubles from 1s to 2s to 4s, capped at 30s.
• You can even read a `Retry-After` header stored on a custom `HttpError`.

insights.title: 18. Forwarding Server Errors to Error Boundaries with throwOnError
insights.content: Pass a boolean or predicate to `throwOnError` in v5 to escalate unexpected 5xx failures to the nearest ErrorBoundary.

blocks.text:
• Renamed from `useErrorBoundary` in v5.
• Returning `error.status >= 500` handles 404 inline while letting 500s trigger a fallback boundary.

insights.title: 19. Centralizing Error Notifications with QueryCache and meta
insights.content: Attach `meta` metadata to queries and handle global side effects once in `QueryCache({ onError })`.

blocks.text:
• Fires once per failed query fetch regardless of how many components observe it.
• Adding `meta: { silent: true }` lets background polling opt out of user-facing toasts.

insights.title: 20. Gating Execution with the enabled Flag
insights.content: Set `enabled: false` (or a boolean expression) to pause automatic fetching until prerequisites are met.

blocks.text:
• While disabled, `isPending` is true (if no cache) and `isLoading` (`isPending && isFetching`) is false.
• Prefer `isLoading` over `isPending` when rendering spinners for conditionally enabled queries.

insights.title: 21. Type-Safe Conditional Queries Using skipToken
insights.content: Pass `skipToken` instead of `queryFn` when inputs may be undefined to eliminate non-null `!` assertions.

blocks.text:
• TypeScript narrows `employeeId` cleanly inside the ternary branch.
• Note: Queries disabled via `skipToken` cannot be triggered imperatively with `refetch()`.

insights.title: 22. Triggering On-Demand Queries Manually with refetch()
insights.content: Combine `enabled: false` with `refetch()` for user-initiated reads like report previews or validation checks.

blocks.text:
• `enabled: false` prevents fetching on mount, focus, or reconnect.
• Calling `refetch()` executes `queryFn` on click and stores the result in cache.

insights.title: 23. Displaying Freshness Timestamps with dataUpdatedAt
insights.content: Read `dataUpdatedAt` (epoch ms) from `useQuery` to show users when cached data was last synchronized.

blocks.text:
• Updated only when `queryFn` resolves successfully.
• Helpful in dashboards, financial tickers, and offline-capable apps.

insights.title: 24. Observing Cache Freshness with isStale
insights.content: `isStale` flips from `false` to `true` automatically once `staleTime` elapses or `invalidateQueries` is called.

blocks.text:
• Useful for debugging cache behavior or subtly indicating aged snapshots.
• `invalidateQueries` immediately sets `isStale: true` even before `staleTime` expires.

insights.title: 25. Accessing the Active QueryClient via useQueryClient()
insights.content: Call `useQueryClient()` inside components to access imperative cache methods without importing a global singleton.

blocks.text:
• Reads from `QueryClientProvider` context—essential for SSR and isolated tests.
• Grants access to `invalidateQueries`, `setQueryData`, `prefetchQuery`, and `getQueryData`.

insights.title: 26. Tuning staleTime vs. gcTime for Read-Heavy Catalogs
insights.content: Keep `gcTime` larger than `staleTime` so inactive queries survive tab switches and retain instant cache hits.

blocks.text:
• `staleTime` prevents redundant network requests while data is fresh.
• `gcTime` begins counting down only after the last component using that key unmounts.

insights.title: 27. Caching Immutable Reference Data with staleTime: Infinity
insights.content: Use `staleTime: Infinity` for countries, timezones, or static enums that never change during a session.

blocks.text:
• Fetches once per session unless manually invalidated.
• Eliminates wasted focus/mount refetches for static lookup tables.

insights.title: 28. Disabling refetchOnWindowFocus for Form & Editor Views
insights.content: Turn off `refetchOnWindowFocus` on interactive editors or wizards where sudden background updates are disruptive.

blocks.text:
• Leaving it `true` globally is great for dashboards, but forms should opt out locally.
• Users switching tabs to copy-paste text won't trigger distracting syncs.

insights.title: 29. Forcing Freshness on Visit Using refetchOnMount: 'always'
insights.content: Pass `'always'` to `refetchOnMount` when a screen must fetch fresh data on every mount regardless of `staleTime`.

blocks.text:
• Shows cached data immediately while guaranteeing a fresh server check on route entry.
• Stronger than `true` (which only refetches if stale).

insights.title: 30. Deriving View-Specific Projections with select
insights.content: Transform raw cached payloads per component via `select` without duplicating or mutating the shared cache entry.

blocks.text:
• The `['users']` cache entry stays intact as `User[]` for every other component.
• Defining `selectActiveEmails` at module scope keeps its function identity stable.

insights.title: 31. Stabilizing Parameterized Selectors with useCallback
insights.content: Wrap `select` functions that close over props like `userId` in `useCallback` so they only recompute when needed.

blocks.text:
• Inline closures create new function identities every render, bypassing memoization.
• Paired with structural sharing, this component only re-renders if this specific user's `role` changes.

insights.title: 32. Disabling structuralSharing for Non-JSON Class Instances
insights.content: Set `structuralSharing: false` when `queryFn` returns `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, or class instances instead of plain JSON.

blocks.text:
• Built-in `replaceEqualDeep` is designed for plain objects and arrays.
• Disabling it (or providing a custom comparator) avoids corrupting class prototypes or slow diffing on huge datasets.

insights.title: 33. Fine-Grained Re-Render Control with notifyOnChangeProps
insights.content: Restrict component updates to specific result fields via `notifyOnChangeProps` (or rely on automatic property tracking).

blocks.text:
• Automatic tracking already ignores properties you don't read.
• Explicit `['data', 'error']` guarantees a polling component never re-renders on `isFetching` transitions.

insights.title: 34. Chaining Dependent Sequential Queries with enabled
insights.content: Feed the resolved field of a parent query into a child query's `queryKey` and gate execution with `enabled`.

blocks.text:
• The second query stays dormant (`fetchStatus: 'idle'`) until `channelId` becomes truthy.
• Once `user` resolves, the child query fires automatically.

insights.title: 35. Fetching Variable-Length Parallel Arrays with useQueries
insights.content: Use `useQueries` whenever you need to run a dynamic number of queries concurrently without breaking hook rules.

blocks.text:
• Safe even when `ids` grows or shrinks between renders.
• Each entry maintains its own independent cache key and stale timer.

insights.title: 36. Merging Dynamic Parallel Results with useQueries combine (v5)
insights.content: Provide a `combine` function to `useQueries` in v5 to aggregate all query results into one clean object.

blocks.text:
• Reduces boilerplate mapping inside JSX.
• Structural sharing runs on the combined output to avoid unnecessary re-renders.

insights.title: 37. Fixed-Interval Background Polling with refetchInterval
insights.content: Set `refetchInterval` in milliseconds for live telemetry, queues, or health dashboards.

blocks.text:
• Automatically pauses when the browser tab is hidden unless `refetchIntervalInBackground: true`.
• Deduplicates timers across multiple observers of the same key.

insights.title: 38. Stopping Polling Conditionally via the refetchInterval Callback
insights.content: Return `false` from `refetchInterval(query)` once an async job reaches a terminal state.

blocks.text:
• In v5, the callback receives the `Query` instance (`query.state.data`, `query.state.error`).
• Eliminates manual `useEffect` + `setInterval` cleanup code.

insights.title: 39. Aborting Stale In-Flight Requests with AbortSignal
insights.content: Forward the `signal` from `QueryFunctionContext` into `fetch` or `axios` so obsolete requests cancel automatically.

blocks.text:
• When `queryKey` changes rapidly or the user navigates away, the browser aborts pending HTTP sockets.
• Saves server CPU and prevents stale network responses from consuming bandwidth.

insights.title: 40. Imperatively Cancelling Queries with queryClient.cancelQueries()
insights.content: Call `await queryClient.cancelQueries(...)` before optimistic cache writes to prevent race conditions.

blocks.text:
• Aborts matching in-flight fetches (if `signal` is wired) and prevents their resolutions from overwriting newer cache updates.
• Supports all `QueryFilters` (`queryKey`, `exact`, `predicate`).

insights.title: 41. Seeding Detail Queries from List Cache with initialDataUpdatedAt
insights.content: Pair lazy `initialData` functions with `initialDataUpdatedAt` so TanStack Query accurately tracks how old the seeded data is.

blocks.text:
• Renders detail views instantaneously from already-fetched lists.
• Prevents `staleTime` from misclassifying 10-minute-old list data as brand new.

insights.title: 42. Rendering Temporary Observer Stubs with placeholderData
insights.content: Supply `placeholderData` when you want immediate UI scaffolding without writing fake data into `QueryCache`.

blocks.text:
• Unlike `initialData`, `placeholderData` never touches the shared cache and sets `isPlaceholderData: true`.
• Ideal for smooth UI previews while the real fetch is in flight.

insights.title: 43. Running Local Storage Queries Offline with networkMode: 'always'
insights.content: Set `networkMode: 'always'` for queries backed by IndexedDB, localStorage, or Electron IPC that don't need internet access.

blocks.text:
• Default `networkMode: 'online'` pauses queries when `navigator.onLine` is false.
• `'always'` ensures local-first reads succeed immediately offline.

insights.title: 44. Configuring Key-Scoped Defaults with setQueryDefaults()
insights.content: Apply custom defaults to all queries matching a key prefix using `queryClient.setQueryDefaults`.

blocks.text:
• Every query whose `queryKey` starts with `['admin']` inherits these overrides automatically.
• Great for grouping strict security or high-frequency telemetry defaults in one place.

insights.title: 45. Inspecting Multiple Cache Entries with getQueriesData()
insights.content: Read all cached `[queryKey, data]` tuples matching a prefix using `queryClient.getQueriesData`.

blocks.text:
• Handy when updating or auditing multiple parameterized keys (e.g., paginated or filtered lists) together.
• Pair with `setQueriesData` for bulk cache updates.

insights.title: 46. Evicting Deleted Entities Immediately via removeQueries()
insights.content: Call `queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey })` after deleting a resource so stale detail views aren't kept in memory.
insights.code:
// Immediately evicts deleted project's cache without triggering a refetch
queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['project', deletedProjectId] });

blocks.text:
• Unlike `invalidateQueries`, `removeQueries` deletes the cache entry outright without triggering a 404 refetch on an already-deleted detail key.
• Navigate away before or right as you remove the active detail query.

blocks.code:
// Immediately evicts deleted project's cache without triggering a refetch
queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: ['project', deletedProjectId] });

insights.title: 47. Building a Noise-Free Global Fetching Bar with useIsFetching
insights.content: Filter `useIsFetching` with a `predicate` so background heartbeats or polling keys don't flash your global spinner.

blocks.text:
• `useIsFetching()` subscribes cleanly to the `QueryCache` count.
• Skipping noisy keys keeps the top loading indicator meaningful for user actions.

insights.title: 48. Controlling Focus Refetches Programmatically with focusManager
insights.content: Call `focusManager.setFocused(...)` to manually override or pause window-focus refetches during sensitive flows.

blocks.text:
• Passing `undefined` restores the default browser visibility listener.
• Useful for kiosks, live calls, or custom iframe/Electron window events.

insights.title: 49. Overriding Connectivity Detection with onlineManager
insights.content: Use `onlineManager.setOnline(boolean)` to drive pause/resume behavior from custom heartbeat checks or native bridges.

blocks.text:
• `navigator.onLine` can report `true` on captive portals; a real API ping feeding `onlineManager.setOnline` is far more accurate.
• Flipping back to `true` automatically resumes paused queries and mutations.

insights.title: 50. Smooth Debounced Typeahead Search with keepPreviousData
insights.content: Combine a debounced queryKey, `signal` cancellation, and `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` for flicker-free search UX.

blocks.text:
• Dimming results slightly when `isPlaceholderData` is true gives instant feedback while keeping layout stable.
• Previously searched terms load instantaneously from cache.

insights.title: 51. Performing Server Writes with useMutation
insights.content: Use `useMutation` for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE side effects and invalidate affected query keys on success.

blocks.text:
• Unlike `useQuery`, mutations never run automatically on mount—they execute when `mutate` or `mutateAsync` is called.
• In v5, `mutation.isPending` replaces `mutation.isLoading`.

insights.title: 52. Awaiting Mutations Sequentially with mutateAsync()
insights.content: Use `mutateAsync` inside `try/catch` when integrating with async form submit handlers or chaining dependent writes.

blocks.text:
• `mutateAsync` returns a standard Promise that rejects on failure.
• Always catch rejections explicitly to prevent unhandled Promise rejection warnings.

insights.title: 53. Separating Cache Callbacks from UI Callbacks in useMutation
insights.content: Keep cache updates in `useMutation` options (guaranteed to run) and navigation/toast calls in `mutate()` options.

blocks.text:
• `useMutation` callbacks survive component unmounts.
• Per-call `mutate(..., { onSuccess })` callbacks only run if the originating component stays mounted.

insights.title: 54. Returning invalidateQueries Promises from onSuccess
insights.content: Return `queryClient.invalidateQueries(...)` inside `onSuccess` so `mutation.isPending` stays true until fresh data arrives.

blocks.text:
• Prevents UI flicker where a 'Saving...' button re-enables before the updated row renders.
• Works cleanly with `onSettled` too.

insights.title: 55. Prefix Matching vs. Exact Matching in invalidateQueries
insights.content: By default `invalidateQueries` matches any key starting with your array; add `exact: true` for single-key precision.

blocks.text:
• Prefix matching automatically refreshes filtered lists like `['orders', { status: 'open' }]`.
• Use `exact: true` when a summary key shares a prefix with heavy sub-queries.

insights.title: 56. Targeting Complex Cache Slices with Invalidation Predicates
insights.content: Pass a `predicate(query)` callback when prefix matching isn't expressive enough for nested key criteria.

blocks.text:
• Inspects every `Query` in `QueryCache` (`queryKey`, `state.dataUpdatedAt`, `meta`).
• Great for invalidating all queries tagged with a tenant ID or stale threshold.

insights.title: 57. Updating Cache Directly from Mutation Responses with setQueryData
insights.content: When a PATCH/POST endpoint returns the updated entity, write it straight to `setQueryData` to save a round-trip GET.

blocks.text:
• Always return a brand-new immutable value inside the updater function—never mutate `old` in place.
• Instantly reflects changes across every mounted observer.

insights.title: 58. Patching Multiple Paginated/Filtered Lists with setQueriesData
insights.content: Use `setQueriesData` (plural) to update an item across every cached filter or page variant matching a prefix.

blocks.text:
• Iterates over all matching cache entries safely.
• Guard against `undefined` entries (`if (!old) return old`) because matching keys may have pending/empty data.

insights.title: 59. Clearing Stale Mutation Errors with mutation.reset()
insights.content: Call `mutation.reset()` when closing a modal or editing inputs to clear `error` and `data` back to `idle`.

blocks.text:
• `useMutation` retains its last `error` or `data` until another `mutate()` runs or `reset()` is called.
• Prevents old validation errors from lingering when reopening a dialog.

insights.title: 60. Zero-Boilerplate UI Optimistic Updates Using mutation.variables (v5)
insights.content: Render `mutation.variables` with dimmed styling while `mutation.isPending` is true when only one component displays the item.

blocks.text:
• Eliminates `cancelQueries`, cache snapshots, and `onError` rollbacks.
• Works seamlessly if you return the `invalidateQueries` promise or wait on `onSettled`.

insights.title: 61. Cache-Level Optimistic Updates with Rollback via onMutate
insights.content: Cancel in-flight queries, snapshot the previous cache, write optimistically, and roll back in `onError` when updates span multiple components.

blocks.text:
• Returning `{ prev }` from `onMutate` passes it as the third `context` argument to `onError` and `onSettled`.
• Always finish with `invalidateQueries` in `onSettled` so client and server converge.

insights.title: 62. Sharing Optimistic State Across Sibling Components via useMutationState
insights.content: Subscribe to another component's pending mutations anywhere in the tree using `useMutationState` and a shared `mutationKey`.

blocks.text:
• Lets a list component show pending items triggered from a completely separate modal or toolbar.
• Clean alternative to global context or complex cache snapshots.

insights.title: 63. Preventing Flicker During Rapid Concurrent Optimistic Mutations
insights.content: Check `queryClient.isMutating({ mutationKey }) === 1` in `onSettled` so only the last concurrent mutation triggers a refetch.

blocks.text:
• Avoids earlier settled mutations pulling stale server snapshots over newer pending optimistic edits.
• Essential for spreadsheets, kanban drag-and-drop, and multi-toggle checklists.

insights.title: 64. Resuming Offline Paused Mutations with resumePausedMutations()
insights.content: Persist mutation defaults with `setMutationDefaults` and call `resumePausedMutations()` on app boot to replay queued offline writes.

blocks.text:
• Mutations triggered offline enter `isPaused: true`.
• Note: You must register `mutationFn` via `queryClient.setMutationDefaults(key, { mutationFn })` since functions cannot be JSON-serialized across reloads.

insights.title: 65. Understanding Mutation Retry Defaults and Idempotency
insights.content: Unlike queries, `useMutation` defaults to `retry: 0` so non-idempotent POST operations aren't accidentally duplicated.

blocks.text:
• Only enable `retry` on mutations when your API supports idempotency keys or safe PUT/DELETE operations.
• Pair with `networkMode: 'online'` to pause safely offline.

insights.title: 66. Smooth Numbered Pagination Using placeholderData: keepPreviousData
insights.content: Use v5's `keepPreviousData` helper as `placeholderData` so page switches keep showing the prior page until the next arrives.

blocks.text:
• Prevents the table from collapsing to a loading spinner on every Next/Previous click.
• Disable the 'Next' button when `isPlaceholderData || !data?.hasMore`.

insights.title: 67. Making Page Transitions Instant by Prefetching Page N+1
insights.content: Prefetch the next page in the background as soon as the current page resolves so clicking Next renders instantaneously.

blocks.text:
• Paired with `staleTime`, clicking Next hits a warm fresh cache entry with zero spinner.
• Guard with `if (data?.hasMore)` to avoid unnecessary requests on the final page.

insights.title: 68. Cursor-Based Feeds with useInfiniteQuery and initialPageParam
insights.content: Implement 'Load More' or infinite scroll feeds with `useInfiniteQuery`, explicitly setting v5's required `initialPageParam`.

blocks.text:
• Returning `undefined` or `null` from `getNextPageParam` sets `hasNextPage` to `false`.
• Flatten `data.pages` cleanly via `.flatMap(...)`.

insights.title: 69. Triggering fetchNextPage Automatically with IntersectionObserver
insights.content: Observe a bottom sentinel element and guard `fetchNextPage()` with `hasNextPage && !isFetchingNextPage`.

blocks.text:
• Guards prevent firing duplicate page requests while a page is already loading.
• `fetchNextPage` is a stable function reference across renders.

insights.title: 70. Bi-Directional Infinite Lists for Chat Histories
insights.content: Combine `getPreviousPageParam` and `getNextPageParam` to load both older history upward and newer messages downward.

blocks.text:
• Calling `fetchPreviousPage()` prepends to `data.pages` and `data.pageParams`.
• Check `hasPreviousPage` and `isFetchingPreviousPage` for top scroll spinners.

insights.title: 71. Capping Infinite Query Memory Footprint with maxPages (v5)
insights.content: Set `maxPages` alongside `getPreviousPageParam` to keep only a sliding window of pages in RAM.

blocks.text:
• Prevents multi-thousand-item infinite feeds from consuming excessive memory or slowing down sequential refetches.
• Scrolling back smoothly reloads evicted pages via `fetchPreviousPage`.

insights.title: 72. Immutably Updating InfiniteData Cache Pages with setQueryData
insights.content: Preserve `{ pages, pageParams }` shape using `InfiniteData<TPage>` when inserting or deleting items inside an infinite cache.

blocks.text:
• Prepending new items to `pages[0]` gives instant feedback without refetching all loaded pages.
• Deleting an item maps over `pages` and filters `page.items` cleanly.

insights.title: 73. Flattening or Reversing Infinite Pages Inside select
insights.content: Use `select` on `useInfiniteQuery` to return a flattened array or reversed page order directly as `data`.

blocks.text:
• Keeps `QueryCache` stored as `{ pages, pageParams }` while components consume a flat list.
• Ideal for chat views needing reversed chronological order.

insights.title: 74. Serializing Conflicting Mutations with mutation scope (v5)
insights.content: Assign the same `scope: { id }` to mutations that must execute one-after-another instead of in parallel.

blocks.text:
• Mutations normally run concurrently; `scope` queues them in order so an earlier PATCH can't overwrite a newer one on the server.
• Useful for ordered document edits or sequential cart updates.

insights.title: 75. Configuring Mutation Garbage Collection with mutations.gcTime
insights.content: Tune `defaultOptions.mutations.gcTime` to retain or evict settled `MutationCache` entries used by `useMutationState`.

blocks.text:
• Settled mutations stay in `MutationCache` for 5 minutes by default.
• Lower `gcTime` if you trigger thousands of high-frequency mutations in long-lived sessions.

insights.title: 76. Hover & Focus Intent Prefetching with prefetchQuery()
insights.content: Warm the cache on `onMouseEnter` and `onFocus` with a reasonable `staleTime` so detail routes render instantly.

blocks.text:
• `prefetchQuery` resolves silently to `void` and ignores errors.
• Setting `staleTime` avoids re-fetching if the user hovers multiple times before clicking.

insights.title: 77. Route-Level Data Preloading with ensureQueryData()
insights.content: Use `ensureQueryData` inside router loaders (React Router / TanStack Router) to reuse warm cache or fetch before render.

blocks.text:
• Returns cached data immediately if available (or respects `revalidateIfStale`).
• Eliminates component mount waterfalls completely.

insights.title: 78. Prefetching Multiple Initial Pages via prefetchInfiniteQuery
insights.content: Pass `pages: N` to `prefetchInfiniteQuery` in v5 to warm multiple infinite pages ahead of navigation or SSR.

blocks.text:
• Requires `getNextPageParam` whenever `pages > 1`.
• Great for seeding above-the-fold feeds in SSR.

insights.title: 79. Guaranteed Defined Data with useSuspenseQuery (v5)
insights.content: Use `useSuspenseQuery` inside `<Suspense>` boundaries so `data` is strongly typed as `TData` (never `undefined`).

blocks.text:
• Removes `if (isPending)` branching inside leaf components.
• Loading states are declaratively coordinated by parent `<Suspense fallback={...}>`.

insights.title: 80. Avoiding Suspense Waterfalls with useSuspenseQueries
insights.content: Batch independent Suspense queries in a single `useSuspenseQueries` call so they execute in parallel rather than serially.

blocks.text:
• Two sequential `useSuspenseQuery` hooks suspend on the first before starting the second.
• `useSuspenseQueries` kicks off every request before suspending.

insights.title: 81. Infinite Pagination with Suspense via useSuspenseInfiniteQuery
insights.content: Combine React Suspense initial loading with `fetchNextPage` incremental loading using `useSuspenseInfiniteQuery`.

blocks.text:
• Initial page suspends at the `<Suspense>` boundary.
• Subsequent `fetchNextPage()` calls use `isFetchingNextPage` without re-suspending the list.

insights.title: 82. Recoverable Error Boundaries with QueryErrorResetBoundary
insights.content: Wire `QueryErrorResetBoundary`'s `reset` callback to `ErrorBoundary.onReset` so Retry actually clears failed query states.

blocks.text:
• Without resetting query error state, re-rendering re-throws the cached error immediately.
• Alternatively use the `useQueryErrorResetBoundary()` hook inside custom boundary components.

insights.title: 83. Pre-Warming Child Suspense Boundaries with usePrefetchQuery (v5)
insights.content: Call `usePrefetchQuery` in a parent component to kick off a child's Suspense fetch without subscribing the parent.

blocks.text:
• Parent doesn't re-render when the query resolves.
• Eliminates parent-child render waterfalls cleanly.

insights.title: 84. Safe SSR + Client QueryClient Singleton Pattern (Next.js)
