insights.content: Always return a fresh `QueryClient` when `isServer` is true, and reuse a single instance in the browser.

blocks.text:
• Prevents cross-request data leaks between users on Node/Edge servers.
• Setting `staleTime: 60 * 1000` avoids immediate redundant refetches upon client hydration.

insights.title: 85. Server-to-Client Cache Transfer with dehydrate & HydrationBoundary
insights.content: Prefetch inside a Server Component, serialize via `dehydrate(queryClient)`, and hydrate in `<HydrationBoundary>`.

blocks.text:
• Client hooks immediately read hydrated data on first render with zero loading flash.
• Works seamlessly alongside Next.js App Router layouts.

insights.title: 86. Streaming Pending Server Queries Without await (v5.40+)
insights.content: Include `query.state.status === 'pending'` in `shouldDehydrateQuery` so unawaited server prefetches stream to the browser.

blocks.text:
• Call `void queryClient.prefetchQuery(...)` in your Server Component without blocking TTFB.
• TanStack Query serializes the in-flight Promise across the RSC stream automatically.

insights.title: 87. Persisting Cache Across Page Reloads with Cache Busters
insights.content: Use `PersistQueryClientProvider` with `maxAge`, matching `gcTime`, and a `buster` version string for safe schema upgrades.

blocks.text:
• Always set `gcTime >= maxAge` so restored data isn't garbage-collected on startup.
• Incrementing `buster` discards incompatible old caches after breaking API changes.

insights.title: 88. Excluding Sensitive Queries from LocalStorage Persistence
insights.content: Filter `dehydrateOptions.shouldDehydrateQuery` so sensitive tokens or PII marked `meta: { noPersist: true }` never touch localStorage.
insights.code:
<PersistQueryClientProvider
  client={queryClient}
  persistOptions={{
    persister,
    dehydrateOptions: {
      shouldDehydrateQuery: (query) =>
        query.state.status === 'success' && !query.meta?.noPersist,
    },
  }}
/>

blocks.text:
• Only persist non-sensitive catalog or UI preference data.
• Protects user privacy on shared devices.

blocks.code:
<PersistQueryClientProvider
  client={queryClient}
  persistOptions={{
    persister,
    dehydrateOptions: {
      shouldDehydrateQuery: (query) =>
        query.state.status === 'success' && !query.meta?.noPersist,
    },
  }}
/>

insights.title: 89. Purging All Cached Data Safely on Sign-Out
insights.content: Cancel in-flight queries, invoke `queryClient.clear()`, and wipe persisted storage whenever a user logs out.

blocks.text:
• Prevents User A's cached private data from briefly appearing to User B.
• Cancelling first ensures late HTTP responses don't re-populate the cleared cache.

insights.title: 90. Combining WebSocket Push Events with TanStack Query Cache
insights.content: Patch individual entities directly via `setQueryData` and selectively invalidate affected lists when server events arrive.

blocks.text:
• Pair with `staleTime: Infinity` on WebSocket-backed queries to avoid redundant polling.
• Re-invalidate on socket reconnect to close any missed-event gaps.

insights.title: 91. Writing Fast, Isolated Unit Tests with a Fresh QueryClient
insights.content: Instantiate a per-test `QueryClient` with `retry: false` and `gcTime: Infinity` to avoid flaky shared state and test timeouts.

blocks.text:
• Disabling retries makes error-state tests resolve in milliseconds instead of ~7 seconds.
• `gcTime: Infinity` prevents lingering background GC timers after test teardown.

insights.title: 92. Testing Real Query Lifecycles Using MSW Instead of Mocking Hooks
insights.content: Mock HTTP endpoints with Mock Service Worker (MSW) rather than stubbing `useQuery` so keys, retries, and caching stay tested.

blocks.text:
• `screen.findBy*` naturally waits for `isPending` to transition to `success`.
• Verifies real serialization, `res.ok` checks, and `queryKey` wiring.

insights.title: 93. Syncing Server State into Forms Safely Without Copying to useState
insights.content: Pass `values: data` (or mount the form only once `data` is loaded) rather than copying query data into `useState` inside `useEffect`.

blocks.text:
• Avoids stale form defaults when `data` arrives asynchronously after mount.
• Consider setting `staleTime: Infinity` or `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` while editing.

insights.title: 94. React StrictMode Double-Invocation Resilience
insights.content: TanStack Query handles React StrictMode's dev mount-unmount-remount cycle seamlessly via observer attachment and cancellation.

blocks.text:
• Unlike raw `useEffect` fetches, cached results survive remounts immediately.
• Never fight StrictMode—ensure your `queryFn` is pure and supports `signal`.

insights.title: 95. Subscribing to QueryCache Events for Telemetry & Logging
insights.content: Listen to `queryClient.getQueryCache().subscribe` to emit structured observability metrics for query errors or timings.

blocks.text:
• Events include `'added'`, `'removed'`, `'updated'`, and `'observerAdded'`.
• Always clean up by calling `unsubscribe()` on teardown.

insights.title: 96. Observing Queries Outside React Components with QueryObserver
insights.content: Use `QueryObserver` directly in plain TypeScript modules, vanilla stores, or imperative services sharing the same `QueryClient`.

blocks.text:
• `useQuery` itself is just a thin React hook wrapper around `QueryObserver`.
• Keeps non-React singletons synchronized with your React UI cache.

insights.title: 97. Defining Reusable Infinite Factories with infiniteQueryOptions()
insights.content: Use `infiniteQueryOptions()` in v5 to get identical `InfiniteData` type inference across hooks and `prefetchInfiniteQuery`.

blocks.text:
• `getQueryData(logsInfiniteOptions('auth').queryKey)` automatically types the return as `InfiniteData<LogPage> | undefined`.
• Mirrors `queryOptions()` for paginated feeds.

insights.title: 98. Protecting Expensive Endpoints from Aggressive Background Refetches
insights.content: Combine long `staleTime` with disabled focus/reconnect triggers on heavy analytics or billing aggregation endpoints.

blocks.text:
• Prevents accidental server spikes when users alt-tab back into your app.
• Users can still trigger an explicit refresh via `refetch()`.

insights.title: 99. Using TanStack Query as a Transport-Agnostic Async Manager
insights.content: Pair TanStack Query seamlessly with REST, GraphQL, tRPC, gRPC-Web, or browser APIs since `queryFn` only requires a Promise.

blocks.text:
• Libraries like tRPC even wrap TanStack Query directly under the hood.
• You retain one unified Devtools and cache model across heterogeneous backends.

insights.title: 100. Production Feature Architecture: Colocating Query Factories & Mutations
insights.content: Organize each domain around colocated `queryOptions` factories, custom mutation hooks, and typed `AbortSignal` fetchers.

blocks.text:
• Components stay purely declarative without hardcoded URLs or raw `queryKey` strings.
• Switching between `useQuery`, `useSuspenseQuery`, `prefetchQuery`, and `HydrationBoundary` becomes effortless.
